Efficacy and safety of mitapivat in patients with sickle cell disease (RISE UP): a phase 3, double-blind, global, randomised, placebo-controlled trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Persistent haemolytic anaemia and recurrent vaso-occlusion drive complications and accelerate mortality in sickle cell disease. Mitapivat, an oral allosteric activator of pyruvate kinase, increases ATP and decreases 2,3-DPG with the potential to improve haemolytic anaemia and reduce sickling. We aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of mitapivat in patients with sickle cell disease. METHODS: We report results from RISE UP, a phase 3, double-blind, global, randomised, placebo-controlled trial from 69 sites across 15 countries. Patients older than 16 years with anaemia and recurrent sickle cell pain crises were randomly assigned (2:1) to either mitapivat 100 mg or placebo twice a day using permuted-block randomisation. Primary endpoints, assessed in all randomly assigned patients, were haemoglobin response (≥1·0 g/dL increase in average haemoglobin concentration from week 24 to week 52 compared with baseline) and annualised rate of sickle cell pain crises. This study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05031780, and the open-label extension is ongoing. FINDINGS: A total of 207 patients were randomly assigned to mitapivat (138 [67%]) or placebo (69 [33%]). 56 (41%) of 138 patients in the mitapivat group had a haemoglobin response, compared with two (3%) of 69 patients on placebo (adjusted difference 38%, 95% CI 29-47; two-sided p<0·0001). The annualised rate (95% CI) of sickle cell pain crises was 2·6 (2·3-3·0) for mitapivat and 3·1 (2·6-3·6) for placebo (two-sided p=0·1213). Serious adverse events were reported in 28 (20%) patients on mitapivat and 20 (29%) patients on placebo; one (1%) patient and 0 patients, respectively, were deemed treatment related. INTERPRETATION: Mitapivat, an oral pyruvate kinase activator, with a novel mechanism that ameliorates haemolytic anaemia, has the potential to be an effective and convenient disease-modifying treatment for people with sickle cell disease. FUNDING: Agios Pharmaceuticals.

recs.title: Implementation of a WatchPAT-Based Diagnostic Pathway for Obstructive Sleep Apnea in a Tertiary Hypertension Center: A Feasibility Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a prevalent yet underdiagnosed in hypertension, affecting 30% to 83% of patients. Limited polysomnography access delays diagnosis. We evaluated the feasibility, diagnostic yield, and downstream management decisions of an integrated diagnostic pathway using WatchPAT 300, a peripheral arterial tonometry-based home sleep apnea test, in a tertiary hypertension unit. METHODS: In this single-center, prospective, observational study, 200 patients underwent ambulatory OSA assessment from May 2023 through August 2025. We recorded clinical variables, peripheral arterial tonometry data, and management decisions. A subgroup underwent confirmatory in-laboratory polysomnography. Patients were classified as none-to-mild OSA (peripheral apneahypopnea index <15/h) and moderate-to-severe OSA (≥15/h). RESULTS: The pathway achieved 97.5% (95% CI, 94%-99%) technical success and reduced the mean time-to-diagnosis to 3.5±4.5 days, versus 154 days for in-laboratory polysomnography. Over half of the cohort was triaged: ∼30% met treatment criteria directly, and 22% were ruled out. Among patients completing confirmatory polysomnography, 83% (95% CI, 61%-94%) initially classified as none-to-mild were reclassified as moderate-to-severe OSA, and 77% required treatment. Furthermore, symptoms were dissociated from severity, and Snoring-Tired-Observed-Pressure-BMI-Age-Gender (STOP-Bag) association with severity did not remain significant after multiplicity correction. CONCLUSIONS: A peripheral arterial tonometry-based home sleep apnea test-first model is feasible and efficient, eliminating diagnostic delays. Although effective for triaging clear-cut cases, the high reclassification rate underscores the almost mandatory role of confirmatory polysomnography for milder or equivocal results, suspected comorbid sleep disorders, or high STOP-Bag score. These data argue against symptoms-based screening alone to screen populations with hypertension.

recs.title: Arrhythmias detected by implanted cardiac rhythm recorders in transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis.
recs.abstract: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Arrhythmias are a common complication of transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CM). We sought to characterize the prevalence, risk factors, and prognosis of arrhythmias in ATTR-CM using implantable loop recorders (ILRs). METHODS: ILRs were implanted in 49 patients with ATTR-CM (84% male; median age, 73.2 [66.2-78.8] years; 71% wild-type, 51% with known atrial fibrillation [AF]). Factors associated with the development of AF or pacemaker implantation were analyzed, and clinical outcomes were compared with those of a contemporary cohort of patients with 125 ATTR-CM without an ILR. RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 37.2 [26.6-41.1] months, an advanced conduction disorder (ACD) prompting pacemaker implantation was detected in 16 individuals (33%) and new-onset AF was detected in 17 patients (71% of those without previous AF). Patients with new-onset AF more frequently had wild-type ATTR-CM. Those who needed pacemaker implantation were older and had a higher prevalence of hypertension and right bundle branch block, and a longer PR interval. Compared with patients without an ILR, early detection of arrhythmias by ILR was not associated with a prognostic benefit in terms of survival (P = .57), reduction of syncope (P = 1), heart failure admissions (P = .34), or embolic events (P = .999). CONCLUSIONS: Although a higher incidence of arrhythmias was identified through ILR monitoring in patients with ATTR-CM, no significant benefits were observed in terms of survival or other hard clinical endpoints. Significant differences were identified in patients who developed new-onset AF and ACD. These differences should be considered during the clinical follow-up of this population.

recs.title: Machine Learning Integration of Ablation Quality Metrics for Predicting Atrial Fibrillation Recurrence: A Multicenter Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Current prediction models for atrial fibrillation (AF) recurrence after ablation rely predominantly on nonmodifiable clinical characteristics, demonstrating limited predictive accuracy and offering little guidance for intraprocedural decision-making and outcome optimization. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to develop and externally validate a machine learning model that integrated clinical characteristics with ablation quality metrics to individually predict AF recurrence. METHODS: We conducted a multicenter, retrospective cohort study of patients undergoing their first AF ablation in 14 hospitals from mainland China. Patients aged 18 to 80 years were enrolled, and data on clinical characteristics and quality metrics were collected. An XGBoost model was developed using 7 selected features to predict 1-year AF recurrence. The model was developed using 5-fold cross-validation for internal validation and was further externally validated on data from 2 independent hospitals. RESULTS: Among 1,782 patients enrolled between December 2021 and December 2023, 294 (16.5%) experienced AF recurrence within 1 year. The final XGBoost model achieved strong discrimination in internal validation (area under the curve [AUC]: 0.918, 95% CI: 0.874-0.962). In feature-combination analyses, model performance improved from an AUC of 0.588 using clinical features alone to 0.918 after incorporating ablation quality metrics. In 2 independent external validation centers (n = 239), the model showed good discrimination, with AUCs of 0.992 and 0.951 and precision-recall AUCs of 0.960 and 0.815, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Integrating ablation quality metrics yielded an validated model that showed strong discrimination for 1-year AF recurrence, outperforming clinical features alone. This approach highlights the prognostic value of intraprocedural quality assessment and may support personalized patient management.

recs.title: Beyond clinical phenotypes: endotype-specific environmental cardiovascular susceptibility.
Intracoronary imaging to assess atherosclerosis and to guide percutaneous coronary intervention.
recs.abstract: Intracoronary imaging has become an important tool for the in vivo assessment of coronary atherosclerosis and for guiding percutaneous coronary intervention. By enabling high-resolution visualization of coronary anatomy, these modalities allow for more accurate lesion characterization, precise stent sizing, and optimized procedural strategies. In recent years, multiple randomized controlled trials have demonstrated that imaging-guided percutaneous coronary intervention reduces major adverse cardiac events (including cardiac death, myocardial infarction, and repeat revascularization), particularly in complex clinical and anatomical settings. This state-of-the-art review synthesizes contemporary evidence supporting the use of intravascular ultrasound and optical coherence tomography to guide percutaneous coronary intervention and improve clinical outcomes, drawing from recent trial data and current guideline recommendations. Special emphasis is placed on complex lesion subsets, such as left main coronary artery disease and other complex bifurcation lesions, calcified lesions, long lesions, and scenarios involving patients at heightened risk, such as those with acute coronary syndrome. Finally, this review considers the strengths and limitations of intracoronary imaging, as well as unresolved questions and priority areas for future research aimed at further improving patient outcomes.

recs.title: Testosterone, Testosterone Replacement Therapy, and Cardiovascular Disease: A Contemporary Review.
recs.abstract: Whether low endogenous testosterone is causal for cardiovascular disease, and how the cardiovascular risk of testosterone replacement therapy should now be classified, remain contested, while US labeling has moved in 2 opposing directions within 16 months. We conducted a targeted narrative review reported in accordance with the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles, searching MEDLINE and primary regulatory documents from January 2000 through July 2026. Evidence was graded with a prespecified 3-tier structured author-consensus rating separating established randomized findings, unresolved secondary signals, and evidentiary absence. Low endogenous testosterone is consistently associated with higher all-cause and cardiovascular mortality but most plausibly marks multimorbidity rather than causation. TRAVERSE established that physiologic transdermal testosterone replacement therapy was noninferior to placebo for 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events over ∼3 years, within a permissive margin and against a 61% discontinuation rate. Observational analyses linking normalization to lower mortality were not reproduced under randomization. Atrial fibrillation, pulmonary embolism, acute kidney injury, fracture, and noncalcified plaque progression remain unresolved. Blood pressure rises across the class; on ambulatory monitoring the magnitude differs by individual product rather than by route. Long-term exposure and nontransdermal formulations remain untested, and the age-related-hypogonadism limitation of use is now proposed for removal. Noninferiority over 3 years should not be read as long-term clinical equivalence. Safe use of testosterone replacement therapy requires appropriate patient selection, distinction between pathologic hypogonadism and functional or age-associated low testosterone, mapping of each recommendation to its evidentiary tier, and close multidisciplinary collaboration.

recs.title: Safety and Outcomes of Transvenous Lead Extraction of Advisory ePTFE-Coated Implantable Cardioverter-Defibrillator Leads: A Multicenter Experience With RELIANCE G.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (ePTFE)-coated implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) leads are associated with progressive coil calcification and rising shock impedance, prompting a recent safety advisory. However, data regarding the safety and efficacy of transvenous lead extraction (TLE) for these chronic leads remain limited. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the safety, efficacy, and procedural outcomes of TLE in patients with advisory ePTFE-coated ICD leads. METHODS: We performed a retrospective multicenter study at 13 centers of patients undergoing TLE of ePTFE-coated ICD leads. Primary endpoints included procedural success, complications, and short-term mortality. Multivariable analyses identified predictors of outcomes. RESULTS: Among 423 patients undergoing extraction of advisory RELIANCE ICD leads (Boston Scientific), mean lead dwell time was 7.5 ± 5.3 years, and impedance-defined coil calcification was present in 15.1%. Laser sheaths were used in 63.8% of procedures and multiple extraction tools in 21.7%. Complete lead removal was achieved in 95.5%, clinical success in 98.8%, and extraction failed occurred in 1.2%. Major complications occurred in 0.9% of patients, with no procedural deaths. Calcified leads were associated with longer dwell times but not higher rates of major complications. Thirty-day mortality was 2.8%, primarily among patients undergoing extraction for infection. CONCLUSIONS: In this large multicenter cohort, TLE of advisory ePTFE-coated ICD leads was associated with high procedural success and low major complication rates despite long lead dwell times. Outcomes were consistent with contemporary TLE experience and do not suggest increased procedural risk attributable to this lead model. The presence of impedance-defined coil calcification did not adversely affect procedural outcomes, supporting TLE at experienced centers when clinically indicated.

recs.title: Making every vial count: fractional dosing of yellow fever vaccine.
Atacicept in IgA Nephropathy - Phase 3 Trial Final Efficacy Analysis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Atacicept resulted in a significantly greater reduction in the urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio than placebo in a previously published analysis of this trial, ORIGIN 3. Final prespecified efficacy results are reported here. METHODS: We randomly assigned adults with biopsy-confirmed IgA nephropathy to receive weekly subcutaneous atacicept at a dose of 150 mg or placebo. We carried out final analyses of two secondary end points: the change in the estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) at week 52 and the annualized eGFR slope through week 104; additional hierarchically tested end points and safety were assessed. RESULTS: Of 431 patients who underwent randomization, 428 received atacicept or placebo (214 per group). At week 52, the mean change in the eGFR was -0.11 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area (95% confidence interval [CI], -1.44 to 1.22) with atacicept and -5.69 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 (95% CI, -7.04 to -4.35) with placebo (mean difference, 5.58 ml per minute per 1.73 m2; 95% CI, 3.68 to 7.48; P<0.001). Through week 104, the mean annualized eGFR slope was -0.60 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 (95% CI, -1.62 to 0.41) with atacicept and -5.60 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 (95% CI, -6.64 to -4.57) with placebo (difference, 5.00 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 per year; 95% CI, 3.55 to 6.45; P<0.001). Composite kidney-disease progression occurred in 11 patients (5.1%) in the atacicept group and in 38 patients (17.8%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.24; 95% CI, 0.12 to 0.48; P<0.001); no patients in the atacicept group had progression to dialysis, transplantation, or death, as compared with 7 patients in the placebo group. Adverse events occurred in 160 of 214 patients (74.8%) in the atacicept group and in 167 of 214 patients (78.0%) in the placebo group; serious adverse events occurred in 7.0% and 15.4%, respectively. One patient (in the placebo group) died. CONCLUSIONS: Atacicept slowed and stabilized the decline in the eGFR as compared with placebo. (Funded by Vera Therapeutics; ORIGIN 3 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04716231.).

Dose-Response Associations of Exercise Modalities With Cardiorespiratory Fitness in Heart Failure: A Systematic Review and Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis.
recs.abstract: AIMS: Exercise training improves cardiorespiratory fitness in patients with heart failure, yet the dose-response relationship across different exercise modalities remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of different exercise modalities and their standardized doses on peak oxygen uptake (VO2peak) in patients with heart failure. METHODS: We systematically searched multiple databases from inception through March 2026 for randomized controlled trials comparing exercise interventions with controls. Exercise modalities were categorized as interval aerobic training (IAT), continuous aerobic training (CAT), resistance training (RT), mind-body training (MBT), and their combinations. Exercise dose was uniformly quantified as weekly metabolic equivalents (MET-min/week). A Bayesian model-based network dose-response meta-analysis was performed. RESULTS: A total of 100 trials involving 5,353 patients were included. The dose-response relationship followed an Emax curve, with ED50 values clustering around 80-90 MET-min/week. A weekly dose of 500 MET-min yielded considerable benefit, and 750-1000 MET-min approached maximal benefit for nearly all modalities. The top three ranked interventions were IAT (Emax = 3.50, 95% CrI: 2.49-4.60), RT (Emax = 3.66, 95% CrI: 1.96-5.85), and IAT+RT (Emax = 3.49, 95% CrI: 1.26-5.79). CONCLUSIONS: The exercise dose-response relationship in heart failure follows an Emax curve, with distinct dose-benefit profiles across different exercise modalities. Based on the current evidence, the following preliminary considerations may be offered: for patients with limited exercise tolerance, MBT may be considered as one of the preferred options; for those with moderate exercise tolerance, IAT+RT or CAT+RT may be suitable choices; for patients with good exercise tolerance, IAT or RT may be considered; and for patients with comorbid obesity, CAT may be incorporated into a comprehensive management program.

recs.title: Latent class analysis-derived patterns of comorbidities in patients with atrial fibrillation, adherence to integrated care and impact on long-term outcomes: an analysis from a prospective cohort.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) commonly coexists with multiple cardiovascular (CV) and non-CV comorbidities, which may cluster in distinct clinical phenotypes with different outcome implications. OBJECTIVE: We aim to identify comorbidity-based phenotypes in AF using latent class analysis (LCA), characterize their clinical course and assess the association of integrated care adherence with outcomes across phenotypes. METHODS: A LCA based on 11 conditions (CV and non-CV) was performed. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death, thromboembolic (TE) events, and acute coronary syndrome (ACS). Secondary outcomes were all-cause death and ACS/TE events. RESULTS: We included 1233 AF patients (median age 75 [66-82] years, females 37.5%). Four clinical LCA-derived phenotypes were identified: "Low comorbidity" (31.5%); "Cardio-metabolic" (33.9%); "Elderly comorbid" (22.9%); and "Atherosclerotic-HF" (11.8%). During a median follow-up of 542 days, 234 patients (22.7%) experienced the primary outcome. Compared to "Low comorbidity", "Cardio-metabolic" (aHR 1.64, 95% CI 1.13-2.39), "Elderly comorbid" (aHR 1.62, 95% CI 1.09-2.42) and "Atherosclerotic-HF" (aHR 2.81, 95%CI 1.83-4.34) phenotypes were independently associated with a higher risk of the primary outcome. Adherence to integrated care varied across phenotypes and was associated with a lower risk of adverse events, with no evidence of significant heterogeneity across phenotypes (p int=0.157). CONCLUSIONS: Latent class analysis identified distinct AF clinical phenotypes characterized by specific patterns of comorbidities and associated with different risk of adverse outcomes. The absence of significant heterogeneity in the association between integrated care and outcomes across phenotypes supports its potential value across different levels of clinical complexity in AF patients.

Day-Night Patterns of Wearable-Derived Electrocardiographic Age and Left Atrial Remodeling in Atrial Fibrillation-Naïve Individuals.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence-derived electrocardiographic (AI-ECG) age is conventionally treated as a static marker. Its diurnal dynamics and structural correlates in individuals without atrial fibrillation (AF) remain unknown. OBJECTIVE: To characterize diurnal AI-ECG age patterns, their reproducibility, and associations with left atrial (LA) remodeling. METHODS: We analyzed continuous wearable ECGs from two prospective registries (NCT05119725, NCT05355948). In 499 AF-naïve participants with ≥48-hour recordings, AI-ECG age was estimated every 10 minutes. Unsupervised clustering identified day-night trajectories, summarized by day-night difference (ΔAge) into Restorative (>0.6 years) or Disrupted (≤0.6 years) phenotypes. Reproducibility was evaluated across sequential periods. Age- and sex-adjusted associations of binary and continuous ΔAge with LA volume index (LAVI) were pooled in a cross-sectional echocardiographic substudy (n=122). RESULTS: Three trajectories emerged in both registries. Restorative prevalence was 47.6%-50.2%. Agreement between two consecutive 48-hour periods was 75.8% (κ = 0.516; 95% CI, 0.395-0.631); 6- to 8-day intraclass correlation coefficients were 0.51-0.54. The Disrupted phenotype was associated with higher LAVI (pooled mean difference, 5.54 mL/m2; 95% CI, 1.11-9.98; P = .014) and greater odds of LA enlargement (LAVI ≥40 mL/m2; pooled odds ratio, 3.68; 95% CI, 1.45-9.29; P = .006). Per 1-SD higher ΔAge, LAVI was lower (β, -2.89 mL/m2; P = .007) and LA enlargement less likely (odds ratio, 0.53; P = .004). CONCLUSION: Wearable-derived AI-ECG age exhibits a reproducible day-night pattern. A Disrupted phenotype is associated with adverse LA remodeling. Because reproducibility remains insufficient for individual-level classification, prospective outcome-based validation is warranted.

recs.title: Real-world, digital-first delivery of GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy in women.
recs.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have demonstrated substantial weight reduction and cardiometabolic benefit in randomized trials; however, prospective implementation evidence from digital care models and female sex community populations remains limited. Here we report outcomes from an observational study of 8,127 women initiating GLP-1RA therapy (99.8% tirzepatide) through a structured digital program incorporating mandatory biochemical monitoring, weekly video-supported follow-up and clinician-guided dose titration in the UK. Mean weight reduction was 16.1 kg (95% confidence interval 15.9 to 16.2; P < 0.001), representing 15.5% of baseline weight; 83.1% achieved ≥10% and 22.4% achieved ≥20% weight loss, with consistent responses across age, baseline weight and socioeconomic strata. Among participants with paired biomarker data, mean glycated hemoglobin decreased by 3.3 mmol mol-1 (95% confidence interval 3.1 to 3.4; P < 0.001), normalizing in 84.5% of those with baseline diabetes-range values and 96.3% with prediabetes, and lipid parameters improved significantly (reductions in total cholesterol of 0.77 mmol l-1, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol of 0.61 mmol l-1 and triglycerides of 0.47 mmol l-1). Retention was 91.4% at 6 months, with no serious treatment-related adverse events. These findings support the feasibility of delivering structured, digitally enabled obesity pharmacotherapy at scale and provide prospective real-world implementation evidence for this care model. Interpretation is limited by the observational design, absence of a comparator group, self-pay population and 6-month follow-up.

recs.title: Life-Course Blood Pressure Trajectories and Focal Myocardial Fibrosis in Older Age in MyoFit46.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The impact of life-course blood pressure (BP) trajectories on later-life focal left ventricular (LV) fibrosis by late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) remains elusive. METHODS: MyoFit46 prospectively recruited ≈500 participants from a 1946 birth cohort for a cardiovascular magnetic resonance scan at 77 years, assessing LV LGE calculated using the 3-SD method or 5-SD method. Systolic BP (SBP) and diastolic BP were recorded at 36, 43, 53, 63, 69, and 77 years. For each participant, annual rates of BP change (steepness) and area under the BP trajectory (cumulative burden) for each age interval were calculated using mixed-effects models. Associations between life-course BPs and LGE were tested using generalized linear models, adjusted for antihypertensives, demographics, lifestyle, and comorbidities. Time-to-event associations between LGE and incident major adverse cardiovascular event (hospitalizations for coronary artery disease, stroke, heart failure, and atrial/ventricular arrhythmias; n=29) were also evaluated. RESULTS: Among 472 participants (54% male), each 10 mm Hg greater individual SBPs at 36 to 69 years were associated with 6% to 11% greater LV LGE calculated using the 3-SD method (all P≤0.033), whereas each 10 mm Hg sustained greater SBPs on any age interval from 36 to 69 associated with 16% to 24% greater LGE calculated using the 3-SD method at 77(all P≤0.005), independent of SBP at 77 years. Each 1 mm Hg/y steeper SBP rise during age intervals 36 to 43, 43 to 53, and 53 to 63 was associated with 6% to 12% greater LGE calculated using the 3-SD method at 77 years. LGE presence was associated with greater major adverse cardiovascular event rates (hazard ratio, 2.5 [95% CI, 1.2-5.2]). CONCLUSIONS: Higher life-course BPs, cumulative burden, and steeper increases were associated with greater older-age LV LGE, which was linked to incident major adverse cardiovascular events. BP trajectories, beyond single-point BP measurements, warrant further investigation as tools to guide BP management strategies.

recs.title: Temporal Changes in LGE-CMR Enhancement After Monopolar Biphasic Focal Pulsed Field Ablation for Pulmonary Vein Isolation.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) has emerged as a novel non-thermal ablation modality for pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) in atrial fibrillation (AF). While chronic lesion formation after PFA has been described, data regarding acute lesion characteristics and lesion maturation remain limited. OBJECTIVE: To characterize acute and chronic lesion formation following focal point-by-point PFA for PVI using serial late-gadolinium-enhancement cardiovascular-magnetic-resonance-imaging (LGE-CMR). METHODS: Six consecutive patients with symptomatic paroxysmal or persistent AF underwent index PFA-guided PVI using the CENTAURI system and a focal point-by-point lesion delivery strategy. LGE-CMR was performed 1 day and 90±10 days after ablation. Quantitative assessment of regional and global left atrial (LA) enhancement was performed using a standardized segmentation protocol. Changes in enhancement burden and LA dimensions were analyzed between imaging timepoints. RESULTS: Among six patients at mean age 65±7 years, five patients (83%) had paroxysmal AF. Acute PVI was achieved in all patients without procedural complications. Serial LGE-CMR demonstrated substantial temporal changes between acute and chronic imaging. Enhancement within the right pulmonary vein (PV) region decreased from 3.3±2.2% to 0.8±0.8%(p=0.030), while the proportion of enhanced tissue decreased from 24.1±13.5% to 5.7±5.8%(p=0.017). Similar reductions were observed around the left PVs (4.4±3.1%vs.1.4±1.2%, p=0.064). Posterior wall enhancement decreased from 2.4±1.1% to 0.3±0.3%(p=0.007) and global LA enhancement from 12.8±6.2% to 3.3±1.6%(p=0.013), while LA volume remained unchanged. CONCLUSION: Serial LGE-CMR demonstrated substantial enhancement reduction of acute lesions following focal point-by-point PFA for PVI, which remained largely confined to the PV antra and adjacent posterior wall, providing novel in-human insights into lesion maturation following focal PFA delivery.

recs.title: Global Heart Failure Burden Increased Between 1990 and 2023.
Incidence, Modifiable Risk Factors, and Management of Cardiomyopathy After Ventricular Leadless Pacemaker Implantation.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Leadless ventricular pacemakers (LPM) provide only RV pacing, which may lead to pacing-induced cardiomyopathy (PICM). It is unclear whether LPM implant site or atrioventricular synchronous pacing using the Micra AV device influence PICM occurrence. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the incidence of cardiomyopathy after LPM implantation and explore the association of implant site and AV-synchronous pacing with cardiomyopathy risk and LVEF evolution. METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 401 patients implanted with an LPM (Micra AV n=145) between July 2015 and March 2025. PICM was defined as cardiomyopathy (≥10% LVEF decline to <50%) in the presence of >20% ventricular pacing, where pacing was considered the primary cause. Risk factors for cardiomyopathy and LVEF evolution were assessed using Cox regression and mixed-effects modelling. RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 33.0 months, all-cause cardiomyopathy occurred in 13.6% (4.8%/year), while PICM was identified in 5.5% (1.9%/year). RVOT implantation was independently associated with a lower incidence of all-cause cardiomyopathy (HR 0.48, P=0.019), and a slower LVEF decline (-0.56%/year vs -1.43%/year, P=0.013) compared with mid-septal implantation. Device type (Micra AV vs VR) was not associated with clinical outcomes or LVEF evolution. Among patients developing cardiomyopathy, 92.7% were medically treated, with 57.9% achieving ≥10% LVEF improvement, and 36.8% complete recovery. CRT upgrade was uncommon (7.3%). CONCLUSION: Cardiomyopathy occurred in a substantial proportion of LPM recipients. RVOT implantation was associated with lower cardiomyopathy incidence and slower LVEF decline, whereas Micra AV implantation did not improve clinical outcomes. However, higher AV synchrony was linked to slower LVEF deterioration.

Sex Differences in the Associations of Age-Related Genetic Predisposition With Incident Atrial Fibrillation: A Prospective Cohort Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Polygenic risks for diseases are age-dependent. However, sex differences in the age-related association between polygenic risk score and incident atrial fibrillation (AF) remain unclear. METHODS: A prospective cohort study was conducted using UK Biobank data, including 386 154 participants aged 40 to 69 years, with a median follow-up of 15.6 years. High AF polygenic risk score was defined as ≥0.858 (top quintile). Cox regression, 10-fold cross-validated C-statistic, Royston's R2, and population-attributable risk percentages were used to evaluate sex- and age-specific genetic effects on incident AF. RESULTS: High polygenic risk score was significantly associated with incident AF, and continuous-age analyses showed that the age-related trajectories differed across sexes (P for difference in age-related trajectories=0.005). In age-stratified analyses, the association was numerically higher in men aged 40 to 49 years (hazard ratio [HR], 2.76 versus 2.07 in women; Bonferroni-adjusted P for interaction=0.077), whereas it was higher in women aged 60 to 69 years (HR, 2.22 versus 1.95 in men; Bonferroni-adjusted P for interaction <0.001). Cross-validated prediction analyses showed broadly similar age- and sex-specific patterns. Population-attributable risk of high polygenic risk score gradually declined across age strata in men, whereas it first increased and then decreased in women. CONCLUSIONS: Age-related genetic predisposition to AF exhibits distinct sex-specific patterns, offering a foundation for personalized risk stratification and prevention strategies tailored to age and sex.

recs.title: Correction: Hypertension.
Multidisciplinary Collaboration in the Performance of Aortic Surgery: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
recs.abstract: Intraoperative management of a patient undergoing cardiac surgery requires continuous and independent interventions by multiple healthcare professionals, including surgeons, anesthesiologists, and perfusionists, among others. Although each clinician performs tasks based on their training and accepted techniques, guidelines, and protocols, an action by one member of the team can have immediate consequences for other team members. Aortic surgery adds a level of complexity, with the need for interventions such as single-lung ventilation, systemic cooling (and subsequent rewarming), and myocardial, cerebral, and visceral protection. Much has been made of the utility of the multidisciplinary team. This scientific statement is intended to approach the patient undergoing aortic surgery from 3 different viewpoints: that of the surgeon, the anesthesiologist, and the perfusionist. This scientific statement is not intended to provide an exhaustive summary of approaches to aortic surgery but rather to illustrate the specific concerns that each member of the team may have.

recs.title: Assessment of Severity of Chronic Aortic Regurgitation: Importance of a Hierarchical Approach to Echocardiogram Doppler Parameters.
Real-Life Psychological Experiences and Cardiac Autonomic Physiology Among Survivors of a Myocardial Infarction in Midlife.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Young and middle-aged women with ischemic heart disease have a higher burden of psychosocial factors compared with male counterparts. They also have worse morbidity and mortality, despite less atherosclerotic burden. Data on daily life stress and autonomic physiology could help guide targeted interventions. METHODS: We studied 302 individuals ≤61 years of age recently hospitalized for a myocardial infarction. All underwent a 7-day home monitoring of mood and stress using ecological momentary assessments, with concomitant Holter monitoring for autonomic physiology. Deceleration capacity, a prognostic marker of parasympathetic activity, was the primary autonomic outcome; heart rate variability was also examined. RESULTS: The sample was 43% women with mean age of 51 years (SD, 7 years). Across the week of monitoring, women reported higher levels of negative mood and stress than men. Women also exhibited significantly lower parasympathetic activity (daily average of deceleration capacity) than men; heart rate variability was also lower. Among women, daily negative mood was inversely associated with lower deceleration capacity: for each 1-log unit higher daily negative mood score, deceleration capacity declined 4.5% in women, but among men, the difference was close to zero: 0.5% (P=0.02 for interaction). Adjustment for other risk factors did not materially affect the associations. A similar pattern of results was observed for heart rate variability metrics. CONCLUSIONS: Young and middle-aged women who recently survived a myocardial infarction have more parasympathetic withdrawal than men in daily life, especially during moments of negative mood. These results underscore the need for greater attention to psychosocial management in women after myocardial infarction.

recs.title: Pregnancy Outcomes After Living Kidney Donation.
recs.abstract: IMPORTANCE: People who become pregnant after living kidney donation may be at increased risk of pregnancy-related adverse outcomes, although the evidence is unclear. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether pregnancies after living kidney donation are associated with a higher risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes than matched pregnancies among nondonors. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This matched cohort study used provincial administrative health care databases from Ontario, British Columbia, and Alberta, Canada, and included living female kidney donors aged 18 to 42 years who donated a kidney between July 1992 and August 2021 and subsequently had singleton pregnancies of at least 20 weeks' gestation. These pregnancies were matched 1:4 with singleton pregnancies of at least 20 weeks' gestation among female nondonors. Pregnancies in donors and nondonors were matched on delivery date, age at delivery, years between cohort entry and delivery, number of prior pregnancies, and income. Final follow-up occurred until March 2023. Outcome analysis occurred from August 2024 to September 2026. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was a composite of hospitalization with a diagnosis of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or eclampsia. Secondary outcomes included 12 maternal, fetal and neonatal adverse outcomes, including the individual components of the primary outcome, the composite of low birth weight or preterm birth, and small for gestational age at birth. RESULTS: The sample included 385 pregnancies in 252 living kidney donors (mean [SD] age, 27.8 [5.0] years) matched to 1540 pregnancies in 1535 nondonors (mean [SD] age, 27.0 [4.8] years). The primary composite outcome of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or eclampsia occurred in 46 donor pregnancies (11.9%) and 128 nondonor pregnancies (8.3%; risk ratio, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.10-2.08). Among the 12 secondary outcomes, the 95% CI for the risk ratio excluded 1.00 for the outcome of small for gestational age, which occurred in 53 donor pregnancies (13.8%) and 121 nondonor pregnancies (7.9%) (risk ratio, 1.86; 95% CI, 1.37-2.52). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, pregnancy after living kidney donation was associated with a higher risk of the composite outcome of hospitalization with a diagnosis of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or eclampsia, when compared with matched pregnancies in nondonors. Most postdonation pregnancies were uncomplicated. These findings support counseling donor candidates who may become pregnant about this risk and informing the prenatal care of donors who become pregnant.

recs.title: Optimizing Echocardiographic Evaluation of Chronic Mitral Regurgitation: Comparison With Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging and Implications for Guideline Recommendations.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The ASE (American Society of Echocardiography) guidelines recommend the presence of at least 4 specific criteria to confirm a diagnosis of definite severe mitral regurgitation (MR). However, the performance of these criteria, particularly when <4 are present, remains unclear. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate and optimize the ASE native MR guidelines by comparing them with quantitative cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), considered the reference standard for MR assessment. METHODS: In this prospective study, 177 patients underwent near-simultaneous CMR and transthoracic echocardiography for the assessment of MR. MR severity was classified using a 4-grade scale based on CMR-derived regurgitant volume, which was calculated as the difference between total left ventricular (LV) stroke volume and aortic forward flow. MR severity was similarly graded using the ASE algorithm, with quantification performed when necessary, by averaging the regurgitant volume from 3 methods: 1) the proximal isovelocity surface area method; 2) the biplane LV volumetric method; and 3) the mitral valve volumetric method. RESULTS: The study cohort had a median age of 61.7 years, with 55% being men. Primary MR was the predominant pathology (73% of patients), with 42% having mitral valve prolapse and 25% presenting with flail leaflets. There was exact agreement between transthoracic echocardiography and CMR MR grading in 51% of cases, whereas agreement within 1 grade was observed in 89%. Patients who met any of the ASE severe MR criteria were predominantly classified as having grades 3 to 4 MR by CMR. The following ASE parameters demonstrated high specificity for identifying grade 4 MR by CMR: pulmonary vein systolic flow reversal (specificity 88%), enlarged LV with normal systolic function (specificity 85%), proximal isovelocity surface area radius ≥1.0 cm (specificity 83%), and vena contracta width ≥0.7 cm (specificity 80%). Combining color Doppler with either pulmonary vein systolic reversal or enlarged LV with normal function resulted in 91%-95% specificity for severe MR. Importantly, reliance on fewer ASE criteria reduced the need for quantification from 86% (4 criteria) to 73% (3 criteria) and 59% (2 criteria), thereby enhancing diagnostic efficiency. CONCLUSIONS: Certain ASE criteria, especially when used in combination, are highly specific for diagnosing severe MR, even when <4 criteria are present. This study suggests that in many cases, the reliance on extensive quantification may be reduced, streamlining the diagnostic process and improving clinical workflow.

recs.title: Silencing the Storm Lazarus, Come Forth! We Found the Purkinje Potentials.
A Common CD36 Variant and the Genetic Landscape of Dilated Cardiomyopathy in Individuals of African Ancestry.
recs.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is a major cause of heart failure that disproportionately affects individuals of predominantly African ancestry, among whom familial clustering of disease is more pronounced relative to those of predominantly European ancestry. Truncating variants in TTN, which encodes the sarcomeric protein titin, are the most common established monogenic cause of DCM. A common CD36 nonsense variant enriched among individuals of African ancestry has also been shown to account for a substantial burden of DCM. OBJECTIVE: To compare the contribution of a CD36 nonsense variant to DCM risk with that of truncating variants in TTN and pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in other established genes for DCM. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Multicohort genetic association study including participants of African and European ancestry with exome or genome sequence data and DCM case status from the following 4 US datasets: All of Us Research Program (recruitment: 2017-present; last follow-up: August 27, 2024), Million Veteran Program (recruitment: 2011-present; last follow-up: September 30, 2024), Penn Medicine Biobank (recruitment: 2013-present; last follow-up: November 14, 2022), and the DCM Precision Medicine Study (recruitment: 2016-2020; last follow-up: March 15, 2020). EXPOSURE: Carrier status for TTN truncating variants, pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in 11 high-confidence genes for DCM, and the nonsense variant CD36 Y325* (0, 1, or 2 copies). MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Risk of DCM, prevalence of variant carriers among DCM cases, and population attributable fraction of DCM. RESULTS: Among 82 623 individuals of predominantly African ancestry across 4 cohorts, the mean age was 53.4 years (SD, 13.9 years), 47 124 were male, and 1316 had DCM. Individuals who were homozygous for the CD36 Y325* risk allele had a higher risk of DCM (odds ratio [OR], 4.8; 95% CI, 3.1-7.3) as did those who were heterozygous (OR, 1.4; 95% CI, 1.2-1.7). TTN truncating variants also conferred an elevated risk of DCM in participants of African ancestry (OR, 8.5; 95% CI, 5.5-13.0). Among 1316 individuals of African ancestry classified as DCM cases, 33 (2.5%) were homozygous for CD36, 56 (4.3%) had TTN truncating variants, and 16 (1.2%) had pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in other high-confidence genes for DCM. In population-level analyses incorporating both heterozygous and homozygous CD36 Y325* carriers, the population attributable fraction for CD36 (9.0% [6.2% for heterozygous carriers and 2.8% for homozygous carriers]) surpassed the population attributable fraction for TTN truncating variants (3.7%). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In 4 US cohorts, an ancestry-specific CD36 variant contributed more to DCM burden among individuals of African ancestry than established genes for DCM, including TTN truncating variants that are typically considered the most common genetic cause. These findings reshape the known genetic architecture of DCM in individuals of African ancestry and highlight the importance of representation in genomic research.

Early Introduction and Prolonged Full-Dose Anakinra Reduce Recurrence Risk After Discontinuation in Recurrent Pericarditis: An International Multicenter Cohort.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Anakinra is effective in recurrent pericarditis, yet optimal treatment duration and strategies for safe drug discontinuation remain uncertain. Identifying predictors of sustained remission after discontinuation is important for clinical management. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 185 consecutive adult patients with corticosteroid-dependent and colchicine-resistant refractory recurrent pericarditis across 16 international referral centers, who permanently discontinued therapy after clinical remission. The primary end point was pericarditis recurrence after drug discontinuation. Univariate and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression and Kaplan-Meier analyses were performed to identify demographic, clinical, and therapeutic predictors of postdiscontinuation relapse. RESULTS: Among 185 patients who discontinued anakinra (58.4% women, mean age 50.4±17.8 years, 77% idiopathic cause), treatment was initiated a median of 10 months (interquartile range [IQR], 4.0-19.5) after the first episode and continued at 100 mg/d for a median of 6 months (IQR, 4-12). Over a median follow-up of 7.2 months (IQR, 1.5-23.3) after discontinuation, 68 patients (36.8%) experienced recurrence, with a median time to recurrence of 2.1 months (IQR, 0.7-8.5). Initiation within 12 months from the first pericarditis episode and maintenance of full-dose therapy (100 mg/d) for ≥6 months were independently associated with lower recurrence risk (hazard ratio [HR], 0.33 [95% CI, 0.18-0.66]; P=0.001 and HR, 0.48 [95% CI, 0.23-0.86]; P=0.017; respectively). CONCLUSIONS: Early initiation of anakinra and maintenance of full-dose therapy for at least 6 months are associated with a significantly lower risk of relapse after discontinuation and may inform treatment duration and discontinuation strategies in recurrent pericarditis.

recs.title: Plasminogen Activator Inhibitor-1 Deficiency Exacerbates Pressure Overload-Induced Cardiac Hypertrophy in Mice.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pathological cardiac hypertrophy is a key precursor to heart failure. PAI-1 (plasminogen activator inhibitor-1) is a recognized profibrotic mediator, yet its role in the heart remains paradoxical and incompletely understood. METHODS: Six-week-old male wild-type (PAI-1+/+) and PAI-1 knockout (PAI-1-/-) mice underwent sham or transverse aortic constriction surgery, followed by assessment of cardiac morphology, molecular markers, and function. In H9C2 cardiomyocytes, PAI-1 was silenced or overexpressed before angiotensin II stimulation, with or without targeted signaling inhibitors, followed by coimmunoprecipitation, Western blotting, and immunofluorescence. RESULTS: Pressure overload increased plasma and myocardial PAI-1 levels. PAI-1 deficiency exacerbated transverse aortic constriction-induced cardiac dysfunction, hypertrophy, and fibrosis, accompanied by JAK2/STAT3 (Janus kinase 2/signal transducer and activator of transcription 3) activation and collagen overexpression, whereas cardiac-specific overexpression attenuated these maladaptive changes. Moreover, STAT3 inhibition reversed the adverse cardiac remodeling associated with PAI-1 deletion. In vitro, PAI-1 knockdown potentiated angiotensin II-induced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, an effect that was rescued by PAI-1 overexpression. Mechanistically, PAI-1 associated with JAK2 and STAT3, with reduced phosphorylation of both proteins and impaired STAT3 nuclear translocation. Critically, pharmacological inhibition of STAT3 abolished the harmful effects of PAI-1 silencing. CONCLUSIONS: PAI-1 acts as an endogenous cardioprotective checkpoint by negatively regulating JAK2/STAT3 signaling. These findings suggest a noncanonical cardiomyocyte-associated function of PAI-1 beyond its classical fibrinolytic role and identify the PAI-1-JAK2/STAT3 axis as a potential therapeutic target for heart failure with hypertrophy.

recs.title: Radiation Vasculopathy of the Coronary Arteries: State-of-the Art Review.
recs.abstract: Radiation-associated coronary artery disease (RACAD) is a distinct form of coronary artery disease with several specific biological and clinical aspects as well as key knowledge gaps. RACAD is prevalent in patients with cardiac exposure to radiotherapy. As radiotherapy is integral to the effective treatment of many thoracic malignancies, improved long-term survivorship is coupled with increased risk for RACAD. Ionizing radiation induces free radical generation and activation of proinflammatory cascades, leading to endothelial dysfunction and accelerated atherosclerosis. Risks for RACAD are determined both by radiotherapy, including the radiation dose and the proximity of coronary arteries to the radiotherapy field, and by patient-specific factors, such as younger age, higher baseline cardiovascular risk, and concurrent cardiotoxic systemic therapies. Importantly, radiotherapy delivery is highly individualized on the basis of tumor location and treatment strategy, resulting in heterogeneous coronary exposure to radiation and patient-to-patient variability. Clinical presentation may occur early, within 1 to 2 years, especially in patients with higher cardiac radiation doses (eg, lung or esophageal cancer), or after a latency period of 5 to 20 years with lower cardiac dose radiation exposure (eg, left-sided breast cancer). Patients generally present with symptoms similar to conventional coronary artery disease. However, RACAD symptoms may be underrecognized in cancer survivors due to overlapping treatment-related fatigue, pulmonary disease, or competing oncologic symptoms. Diagnosis and management generally follow standard coronary artery disease guidelines while incorporating cancer-specific considerations, such as planned oncologic surgeries, bleeding risk, postradiotherapy complications such as atretic internal mammary arteries, and cardiotoxic effects of systemic cancer therapies. Primary prevention of RACAD is critical, emphasizing advances in precision radiotherapy, including delivery techniques with improved coronary dosimetry, and cardiac shielding. Key knowledge gaps include understanding long-term outcomes with contemporary 3-dimensional conformal radiotherapy techniques, validated cancer-specific risk prediction models on the basis of coronary dosimetry, optimal surveillance protocols, targeted molecular pharmacotherapies, and risk analysis of percutaneous versus surgical management of RACAD. Prospective studies are needed to develop cancer- and dosimetry-specific risk calculators, validating cardioprotective interventions, and improving multidisciplinary cardio-oncology collaboration to optimize early detection of RACAD and timely intervention in the growing population of cancer survivors.

recs.title: Combined Prognostic Value of Cardiac Magnetic Resonance-Derived Myocardial Extracellular Volume and the Fibrosis-4 Index in Patients With Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction is increasingly recognized as a multisystem metabolic-inflammatory syndrome. We investigated the comparative and complementary prognostic value of cardiac magnetic resonance-derived extracellular volume fraction (ECV) and the Fibrosis-4 index for predicting adverse cardiovascular outcomes in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. METHODS: Between 2017 and 2019, 250 patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction underwent assessment of myocardial ECV by cardiac magnetic resonance and hepatic fibrosis using the Fibrosis-4 index. The primary outcome was a composite of cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization. Multivariable Cox regression and discrimination analyses were performed to evaluate prognostic performance. RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 1190 days, 75 patients (30.0%) experienced the primary outcome. Both ECV (hazard ratio [HR], 1.13 [95% CI, 1.08-1.17]; P<0.001) and the Fibrosis-4 index (HR, 1.12 [95% CI, 1.02-1.22]; P=0.015) independently predicted the primary outcome. Patients with concomitantly elevated ECV and Fibrosis-4 index had a markedly increased risk of adverse events compared with those with low values of both markers. ECV-based models demonstrated superior discrimination compared with Fibrosis-4-based models (concordance index, 0.732 versus 0.663; P=0.011). Addition of ECV to the Fibrosis-4 model significantly improved discrimination, whereas addition of the Fibrosis-4 index to the ECV model improved reclassification (continuous net reclassification improvement and integrated discrimination improvement) but not discrimination. CONCLUSIONS: Both myocardial ECV and the Fibrosis-4 index independently predict adverse cardiovascular outcomes in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. Although ECV provides greater prognostic discrimination, combined assessment of ECV and the Fibrosis-4 index identifies a subgroup at particularly high risk and may provide complementary information for risk stratification.

recs.title: Pulsed Field Ablation for Persistent Atrial Fibrillation.
Obesity in Children Aged 2 to 12 Years: A Review.
recs.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Obesity affects 15% of children aged 2 to 5 years and 22% of children aged 6 to 11 years in the US. Obesity in children is associated with dyslipidemia, hypertension, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, and obstructive sleep apnea. Compared with normal-weight peers, children with obesity have lower quality of life and are 5 times more likely to have obesity in adulthood. OBSERVATIONS: Body mass index (BMI; calculated as weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared) is used to identify children at risk for excess adiposity, and guidelines recommend that clinicians screen for obesity using BMI starting at age 2 years. Among children, obesity is defined using standardized age- and sex-specific growth charts, with obesity defined as BMI in the 95th or higher percentile and severe obesity as BMI of 120% or greater of the 95th percentile. Obesity treatment in children includes intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment, consisting of at least 26 contact hours of face-to-face group or family-based activities that incorporate nutrition, physical activity, and behavior change education delivered to the child and caregivers over a 3- to 12-month period. Intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment reduces BMI by 0.7 compared with children who do not participate in intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment. The only obesity pharmacotherapy currently approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for children younger than 12 years is setmelanotide, a melanocortin-4 receptor agonist, which is indicated for 3 forms of rare monogenic obesity (LEPR, POMC, and PCSK1 genetic variants), Bardet-Biedl syndrome, and acquired hypothalamic obesity. Liraglutide is currently only FDA approved for youth aged 12 years or older; however, a randomized clinical trial among children aged 6 to younger than 12 years demonstrated that, compared with placebo, liraglutide reduced BMI by 7.4%. Metabolic and bariatric surgery is rarely used in children younger than age 12 years and evidence supporting its use in children is limited. Early identification and treatment of obesity during childhood may reduce risk of type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, hypertension, and mortality in adulthood. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Obesity in children is associated with chronic disease, such as hypertension, and with poor quality of life. Evidence-based treatment for obesity in children includes intensive health behavior and lifestyle treatment, and pharmacotherapy may provide additional benefit, although short- and long-term safety and efficacy data are limited. Early identification and treatment of obesity during childhood may reduce risk of type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, hypertension, and mortality in adulthood.

recs.title: Feasibility and Restenosis Predictors of Optical Frequency Domain Imaging-Guided Drug-Coated Balloon Treatment for Femoropopliteal Lesions.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The clinical utility of optical frequency domain imaging (OFDI) for guiding endovascular therapy in femoropopliteal lesions has not been established. Additionally, the prognostic value of OFDI findings during drug-coated balloon (DCB) treatment for femoropopliteal lesions has never been evaluated. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to clarify the feasibility of OFDI-guided DCB treatment and investigate the OFDI findings associated with restenosis after DCB treatment in femoropopliteal lesions. METHODS: This multicenter, prospective, observational study included patients with symptomatic, nonseverely calcified femoropopliteal lesions who underwent DCB treatment under OFDI guidance. Procedural success was defined as residual stenosis of less than 30% without flow compromise and without any procedural complications. The primary outcome was restenosis of the target lesion, defined as a peak systolic velocity ratio of ≥2.5, as measured by duplex ultrasound at rest or target lesion revascularization. RESULTS: A total of 202 lesions were initially enrolled, of which 35 (17.3%) were excluded primarily because of severe calcification or inadequate OFDI data. Among the 167 analyzable lesions included in the present analysis, the procedural success rate and 1-year freedom from restenosis were 91.6% and 85.5%, respectively. In the procedural OFDI findings, a calcified nodule in the target lesion (subdistribution hazard ratio: 3.25; 95% CI: 1.01-10.42; P = 0.048) was associated with restenosis. CONCLUSIONS: OFDI-guided DCB treatment is feasible in selected femoropopliteal lesions. An OFDI-detected calcified nodule is associated with an increased risk of restenosis after DCB treatment for femoropopliteal lesions.
