PASCAL Precision System Outcomes by Implant Location and Lesion Location in Degenerative Mitral Regurgitation Patients From the STS/ACC TVT Registry.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair can be more challenging in noncentral regions of the valve and in anterior or bileaflet lesions. We assess effect of implant location and leaflet lesion location on safety and effectiveness of PASCAL Precision system in degenerative mitral regurgitation (MR). METHODS: Mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair outcomes in patients with degenerative MR treated with PASCAL Precision system (September 2022-October 2024), from the US STS/ACC TVT (Society of Thoracic Surgeons/American College of Cardiology Transcatheter Valve Therapy) Registry, were analyzed by implant location (A2P2/non-A2P2) and leaflet lesion location (anterior/posterior/bileaflet). Procedural, clinical, and echocardiographic outcomes to 30 days were assessed. RESULTS: At 30 days, both A2P2 (n=1526) and non-A2P2 (n=299) groups had low event rates (cardiovascular mortality: 1.1% versus 1.0%, mitral valve reintervention: 0.4% versus 0.0% and single leaflet device attachment: 0.5% versus 0.3%; all P>0.05) and demonstrated significant MR reduction (P<0.001 versus baseline) with no significant difference between groups (P=0.750) (MR ≤2+: 93.4% versus 95.4%; MR ≤1+: 72.0% versus 73.3%). Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary scores improved significantly in both groups (∆19.3, ∆17.7 points; P=0.741). The anterior (n=250), posterior (n=902), and bileaflet (n=192) disease groups also had low event rates (cardiovascular mortality: 0.4%, 1.1%, 0.0%; mitral valve reintervention: 0.8%, 0.1%, 0.5%; and single leaflet device attachment: 0.8%, 0.2%, 0.5%; all P>0.05), and demonstrated significant MR reduction (P<0.001 versus baseline) with no significant difference across groups (P=0.459) (MR ≤2+: 94.1%, 93.1%, and 94.5%; MR ≤1+: 79.0%, 69.2%, and 72.4%). All groups experienced significant improvement in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary scores (∆21.4, ∆18.8, ∆12.0 points; P=0.087). CONCLUSION: In real-world patients with degenerative mitral regurgitation, treatment with the PASCAL Precision system was associated with favorable safety and effectiveness at 30 days, regardless of implant location or leaflet lesion location.

recs.title: Macrophage-derived TNF-α promotes vascular inflammation and cell crosstalk in human atherosclerotic plaques via TNFRSF1A.
recs.abstract: AIMS: Atherosclerosis (AS) is a chronic inflammatory disease driven by complex cellular crosstalk within plaques. How a key inflammatory pathway orchestrates multicellular vascular injury and whether this is conserved across vascular beds remains incompletely understood. METHODS: Carotid and coronary plaques were profiled by single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics. Immunofluorescence validated cell localization and TNF-TNFRSF1A signaling, and CellChat analyzed intercellular communication. THP-1 macrophages were subjected to hypoxia/nutrient deprivation or ox-LDL, and conditioned media were applied to endothelial and smooth muscle cells to assess TNFRSF1A-dependent cytotoxicity, NF-κB/MAPK activation, lipid accumulation, and cytokine release. RESULTS: Single-cell and spatial analyses revealed a conserved plaque architecture: myeloid cells enriched in the lipid core, mural and endothelial cells at the periphery. Five endothelial, eight mural, and six macrophage subtypes showed distinct spatial and functional features. Central to these interactions, TNF-TNFRSF1A emerged as a central signaling axis linking macrophages, endothelial cells, and smooth muscle cells. Microenvironmental stress amplified macrophage TNF-α secretion, leading to promoting TNFRSF1A-dependent vascular cell death, NF-κB/MAPK activation, and foam cell formation. Mechanistically, ox-LDL upregulated increased macrophage CD36 and TREM2, while TNFRSF1A knockdown mitigated lipid accumulation, cytokine release, and downstream signaling. CONCLUSIONS: These findings delineate the spatial and functional landscape of AS plaques and reveal a conserved, spatially constrained mechanism: macrophage-derived TNF-α drives TNFRSF1A-dependent vascular injury, inflammatory amplification, and foam cell formation, highlighting this axis as a promising therapeutic target for atherosclerotic diseases.

recs.title: Individualized Cardiac Index-Guided Hemodynamic Therapy in High-Risk Patients Undergoing Elective Major Abdominal Surgery: The PELICAN Randomized Clinical Trial.
recs.abstract: IMPORTANCE: It remains unclear if intraoperative hemodynamic therapy should be guided by cardiac index. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether individualized cardiac index-guided hemodynamic therapy vs routine hemodynamic therapy improves outcomes in high-risk patients undergoing elective major abdominal surgery. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This multicenter, single-blind, superiority randomized clinical trial enrolled high-risk patients undergoing elective major abdominal surgery between October 8, 2023, and October 25, 2025, at 12 university medical centers in Austria, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Germany, and Spain. The date of last follow-up was January 15, 2026. INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomized to individualized cardiac index-guided hemodynamic therapy targeting the patient's preoperative resting cardiac index vs routine hemodynamic therapy (with blinded cardiac index monitoring). MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was a composite of acute kidney injury, acute myocardial injury, severe infectious complications, nonfatal cardiac arrest, or death within the first 7 postoperative days. Secondary outcomes included the individual components of the primary outcome within the first 7 postoperative days. RESULTS: Of the 1128 patients enrolled, 1111 were randomized and 1095 were included in the primary analysis (median age, 67 years [IQR, 59-74 years]; 49.4% were female). The primary outcome occurred in 243 of 549 patients (44.3%) in the individualized cardiac index-guided hemodynamic therapy group vs 256 of 546 patients (46.9%) in the routine hemodynamic therapy group (relative risk, 0.94 [95.1% CI, 0.83-1.08]; P = .38). There were no between-group differences for the incidence of the individual components of the primary outcome within the first 7 postoperative days. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Among high-risk patients undergoing elective major abdominal surgery, individualized cardiac index-guided hemodynamic therapy targeting the patient's preoperative resting cardiac index did not reduce the incidence of a composite outcome of acute kidney injury, acute myocardial injury, severe infectious complications, nonfatal cardiac arrest, or death within the first 7 postoperative days compared with routine hemodynamic therapy. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05648279.

recs.title: Computational Modeling Reduces Leaflet Modification Rates in Valve-In-Valve and Redo Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Coronary obstruction (CO) complicates valve-in-valve (ViV) and redo transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) at higher rates than native TAVR. Leaflet modification mitigates this risk but increases procedural burden. Traditional computed tomography angiography (CTA)-based risk stratification relies on static parameters that may overestimate risk; computational predictive modeling (CPM) uses patient-specific data to refine risk assessment. OBJECTIVES: The study aims to characterize leaflet modification rates in conventional ViV TAVR and redo-TAVR and evaluate the impact of CPM preprocedural planning augmentation on leaflet modification rates. METHODS: A total of 157 consecutive ViV TAVR or redo-TAVR patients treated from 2022 to 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. CO risk status was derived from traditional CTA parameters. Leaflet modification rates among CTA high-risk subgroups (non-CPM, n = 62; and CPM, n = 29) were compared using Boschloo's one-sided exact test. CPM risk-reclassification patterns were studied using counterfactual binomial analysis. RESULTS: Leaflet modification occurred in 26.3% of ViV TAVR and 24.1% of redo-TAVR procedures that used only conventional CTA-based planning methods. Among patients deemed high risk for CO by conventional methods, leaflet modification was significantly lower in the CPM-augmented subgroup vs that in the non-CPM subgroup (24.1% vs 46.8%; OR: 2.76; 95% CI: 1.03-7.40; P = 0.021). CPM-augmented planning reclassified 82.8% of patients to low-risk status, and 79.2% of reclassified patients were managed without leaflet modification. No COs occurred during the study period. CONCLUSIONS: Among ViV TAVR and redo-TAVR patients at high risk of CO based on conventional CTA-based planning, the use of CPM to augment standard risk assessment was associated with a significant reduction in leaflet modification procedures.

recs.title: Beyond the lifestyle paradigm: environmental triggers and susceptible cardiovascular phenotypes.
Contemporary Management and Rechallenge Practices for 5-Fluorouracil-Associated Cardiotoxicity: Insights From an International Cardio-Oncology Society Survey.
Prolonged inflation instead of a double tap: pursuing the optimal deployment strategy for the SAPIEN 3 Ultra RESILIA.
Exercise Prescriptions for Cardiovascular Health in Adults: 2026 ACC Scientific Statement: A Report of the American College of Cardiology.
recs.abstract: Regular physical activity and structured exercise are foundational for cardiovascular prevention and treatment, yet exercise prescription remains inconsistently integrated into routine cardiovascular care. This American College of Cardiology scientific statement provides contemporary, practical guidance for clinicians on prescribing exercise across the spectrum of cardiovascular health and disease. The statement reviews evidence supporting physical activity, exercise training, and cardiorespiratory fitness as powerful determinants of cardiovascular outcomes, emphasizing that the greatest absolute benefits occur when inactive individuals begin moving and that additional benefits accrue with higher volumes and intensity, within appropriate clinical limits. It summarizes approaches to aerobic, resistance, balance, and flexibility training; highlights the role of cardiac rehabilitation and supervised, home-based, hybrid, and virtual models; and addresses individualized exercise prescription for patients with coronary artery disease, peripheral artery disease, heart failure, cardiomyopathies, hypertension, overweight and obesity, adult congenital heart disease, and older age. The statement also discusses when exercise testing is useful to assess safety, guide intensity, establish baseline fitness, and monitor responses, while recognizing that routine preparticipation testing is not required for most asymptomatic individuals. Wearable devices and digital tools are reviewed as adjuncts to self-monitoring, goal setting, and cardiac rehabilitation extension, with attention to equity, access, and digital literacy. Key implementation priorities include improving clinician training, embedding physical activity counseling into cardiovascular care, tailoring prescriptions to patient goals and functional capacity, and expanding research on long-term adherence, clinical outcomes, diverse populations, and scalable delivery models. Exercise should be prescribed as a core component of cardiovascular prevention and disease management.

recs.title: Trends in Use of Coronary Angiography, Percutaneous Coronary Intervention, and Coronary Artery Bypass Graft Over a Decade in France: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Coronary angiography, percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), and coronary artery bypass graft are among the most commonly performed procedures globally. The influence of recent scientific evidence on national-level temporal trends remains poorly explored. METHODS: The frequency, characteristics, and outcomes of elective and nonelective coronary angiography, PCI, and coronary artery bypass graft were described using the French National Hospitalization Database from 2014 to 2023 (covering a population of 67.0 million inhabitants), totaling 6 290 951 coronary interventions among 2 985 822 patients (mean age, 67.8±12.2 years; 69.9% men). RESULTS: Over 10 years, the annual number of coronary interventions increased by 33%, driven by a rise in coronary angiography (+32%) and PCI (+40%), while coronary artery bypass graft decreased (-8%). The growth in PCI was predominantly related to an increase in elective procedures (from 53.5% to 56.9%, P<0.001), particularly among older patients (+73%), and in multivessel disease (from 16.7% in 2014-2015 to 19.0% in 2022-2023, P<0.001). Attempts to recanalize chronic total coronary occlusion doubled (from 1.9% to 3.3%, P<0.001). In-hospital death after PCI decreased (from 2.05% in 2014 to 1.58% in 2023, P for trend<0.001), with the most notable improvements observed in nonelective PCI. Similarly, in-hospital death after coronary artery bypass graft declined (from 3.5% to 2.9%, P<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: These findings underscore a significant increase in both coronary angiography and PCI over the past decade in France, particularly in procedures classified as elective among older patients. This trend raises questions about the influence of recent scientific evidence and guidelines on clinical practice in this country.

recs.title: Clinical Impact of Physiology-Guided PCI: 1-year Results of the Post-Revascularization Optimization and Physiological Evaluation of Intermediate Lesions using Fractional Flow Reserve (PROPHET-FFR) Study.
recs.abstract: Background: The clinical value of physiological assessment after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains uncertain. We evaluated clinical outcomes associated with post-PCI physiology and temporal trends in its adoption. Methods: PROPHET-FFR (NCT05056662) is an ambispective observational study of patients undergoing invasive physiological assessment of intermediate coronary stenoses. Patients were categorized into three strategies: deferred revascularization based on non-ischemic physiology (deferred PCI), PCI for ischemic lesions without post-PCI physiological assessment (conventional PCI), and physiology-guided PCI with post-PCI assessment and optimization when indicated (post-PCI physiology). Temporal trends in the use of post-PCI physiology and physiology-guided optimization were evaluated, together with the incidence of 12-month major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), comprising cardiovascular death, spontaneous myocardial infarction, and target-vessel revascularization (TVR). Propensity score matching between conventional PCI and post-PCI physiology was performed to confirm the primary findings. Results: Among 1,986 patients, 1,307 underwent deferred PCI, 331 conventional PCI, and 348 post-PCI physiology. At 12 months, MACE occurred in 4.1%, 7.6%, and 3.4%, respectively (p=0.011). Compared with conventional-PCI, post-PCI physiology had lower MACE (3.4% vs 7.6%; p=0.019), primarily driven by reduced TVR (2.6% vs 5.4%; p=0.057), with consistent findings after propensity score matching (226 patients/group; 2.7% vs 8.0%; p=0.0114). Post-PCI physiology increased from 11.8% to 22.8% across registry phases (p<0.001), with a numerical increase in physiology-guided optimization (11.6% vs 18.1%; p=0.08). Conclusions: In this observational study, post-PCI physiology appears to be associated with lower 12-month MACE compared with conventional PCI, with consistent findings after propensity score matching.

recs.title: Multivariate Genomic Analysis Reveals Shared Genetic Architecture and Potential Therapeutic Targets for Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) is a leading cause of mortality worldwide and comprises multiple clinical phenotypes, but their shared genetic architecture remains incompletely defined. METHODS: We integrated genome-wide association study summary statistics for coronary artery disease, peripheral artery disease, large-artery atherosclerotic stroke, and carotid plaque using genomic structural equation modeling to derive a multivariable ASCVD common factor. We applied fine-mapping, multi-marker analysis of genomic annotation, transcriptome-wide association studies, Mendelian randomization, colocalization, mediation analysis, and virtual screening. RESULTS: We identified 289 linkage disequilibrium-independent lead single-nucleotide polymorphisms mapping to 177 genomic risk loci; 13 lacked corresponding genome-wide significant signals in the input genome-wide association studies. Eleven had prior genome-wide association study catalog association records, whereas no relevant records were identified for the loci represented by rs2294777 near SASH1 and rs4843053 near AKAP13. Fine-mapping prioritized 26 putative causal variants. Integrated functional summary-based imputation, multi-tissue transcriptome-wide association study, and multi-marker analysis of genomic annotation analyses implicated 123 genes. Enrichment analyses highlighted endothelial cells and H3K27ac-marked regulatory regions. Lipidomic analyses linked higher triacylglycerols and sterol esters to increased multivariable ASCVD common factor risk. Protein Mendelian randomization analyses in deCODE and Fenland prioritized aldehyde dehydrogenase 2 (ALDH2), phosphodiesterase 5A (PDE5A), HtrAserinepeptidase 1 (HTRA1), and transcription elongation factor A2 (TCEA2) as candidate targets. Colocalization supported a shared causal variant between TCEA2 and multivariable ASCVD common factor. Mediation analyses suggested partial mediation by diastolic blood pressure for ALDH2, PDE5A, and TCEA2 and by triglycerides for TCEA2. Virtual screening identified candidate compounds with favorable predicted binding to PDE5A and ALDH2. CONCLUSIONS: Integrating multivariate genome-wide association study with multi-omics and causal inference analyses identified shared genetic signals associated with ASCVD susceptibility and prioritized candidate protein targets, informing future functional studies and target validation.

recs.title: The Duke Clinically Linked Electrocardiogram and Arrhythmia Repository.
recs.abstract: Artificial intelligence-electrocardiogram (ECG) algorithms are becoming increasingly powerful tools in the clinical world, allowing for earlier and subclinical detection of ubiquitous and harmful pathologies. However, the strength of these algorithms is directly informed by the strength of the data sets on which they are trained, and there is a growing need for large-scale, diverse, publicly available ECG repositories. The Duke Clinically Linked ECG and Arrhythmia Repository is a large-scale ECG database containing over 5 million clinically acquired ECGs linked to longitudinal clinical data. Its strengths-including demographic diversity, large sample size, linked clinical databases, breadth of represented conditions, access to linked procedure codes, various options for data export, and ease in creating targeted subcohorts-position it as a significant tool in the artificial intelligence-ECG research landscape. This Methods paper outlines the demographics and structure of this database and explores promising research applications of this resource.

recs.title: Bromocriptine for Myocardial Recovery in Peripartum Cardiomyopathy: Design and Rationale of the REBIRTH Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: There is evidence suggesting that bromocriptine potentially improves outcomes among women with peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM); however, there is currently no randomized controlled trial comparing bromocriptine vs placebo on top of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) in a diverse, multiethnic cohort in North America. OBJECTIVES: The REBIRTH trial will enroll 200 women with PPCM to evaluate whether the addition of oral bromocriptine to GDMT is superior to placebo for improving myocardial function and event-free survival. In addition to the randomized trial, REBIRTH will enroll 50 women with PPCM excluded from randomization because of breastfeeding into an observational cohort. METHODS: The principal inclusion criteria are ≥18 years of age, within 5-months postpartum, and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) ≤40%. The primary endpoint is LVEF at 6 months postrandomization. Secondary endpoints include LVEF at 12 months, survival free from major events (ie, death, heart transplantation, or implantation of a durable left ventricular assist device), and survival free from heart failure hospitalization for up to 3 years. RESULTS: The study is currently enrolling women in both the randomized trial and observational breastfeeding cohort. Primary results are expected to be reported in 2027. CONCLUSIONS: REBIRTH will determine whether the addition of bromocriptine to GDMT for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction improves postpartum myocardial recovery and clinical outcomes in a diverse cohort of women with PPCM. (Randomized Evaluation of Bromocriptine in Myocardial Recovery Therapy for PPCM [REBIRTH]; NCT05180773).

recs.title: Selective Imaging-Informed Prevention of Coronary Atherosclerosis.

Correction to: 2026 ESC Guidelines on cardiac rehabilitation: Developed by the task force on cardiac rehabilitation of the European Society of Cardiology (ESC)Endorsed by the European Society of Physical and Rehabilitation Medicine (ESPRM) and World Organization of Family Doctors (WONCA).
Immediate Complete Revascularization During Index Admission in Older Patients With ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Whether age affects the comparative treatment effect of immediate complete revascularization (CR) vs staged CR during the index admission in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and multivessel disease remains unknown. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to assess how age influences clinical outcomes in patients with with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and multivessel disease randomized to immediate or in-hospital staged CR. METHODS: This is a secondary analysis of the OPTION-STEMI (Optimal Timing of Fractional Flow Reserve-Guided Complete Revascularization for Non-Infarct-Related Artery in ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction with Multivessel Disease) trial, which included 994 patients randomized to immediate or in-hospital staged CR. The primary endpoint at 1 year, defined as a composite of all-cause death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or any unplanned revascularization, was analyzed according to age and CR strategy. RESULTS: A significant interaction was found between age, as a continuous variable, and CR strategy for the primary endpoint (interaction P = 0.015). The HR for the primary endpoint was initially higher in the staged CR arm until approximately 67 years, after which it increased steadily in the immediate CR arm. In the binary analysis, a significantly higher incidence of the primary endpoint was observed in the immediate CR arm compared with the staged CR arm in patients ≥70 years (45 of 202 [22.3%] vs 29 of 210 [13.8%]; HR: 1.68; 95% CI: 1.06-2.69; log-rank P = 0.029), but not in patients <70 years (20 of 296 [6.8%] vs 24 of 286 [8.4%]; HR: 0.80; 95% CI: 0.45-1.45; log-rank P = 0.470) (multiplicative interaction P = 0.054; relative excess risk due to interaction P = 0.016). CONCLUSIONS: This post hoc analysis of the OPTION-STEMI trial demonstrates that older patients experience significantly worse clinical outcomes with immediate CR than with in-hospital staged CR. These findings suggest that age modifies the treatment effect of the CR strategy and warrant confirmation in adequately powered trials (Timing of FFR-guided PCI for Non-IRA in STEMI and MVD [OPTION-STEMI]; NCT04626882).

recs.title: Interatrial Shunts for Heart Failure: Safe, But for Who?
Evaluating Patients for Renal Denervation: A Pragmatic Approach.
Contemporary Analysis of the Volume-Outcome Relationship for Patients With Nontraumatic Subarachnoid Hemorrhage.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Nontraumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) carries a substantial mortality burden and risk of long-term morbidity. Although prior investigations have demonstrated an inverse association between SAH admission volume and in-hospital mortality, reported thresholds remain broad. Importantly, the relative importance of both admission and procedural volume has yet to be evaluated on a national scale. We examined the association of volume metrics with outcomes in an SAH cohort. METHODS: All adult (≥18 years) hospitalizations with a primary diagnosis of nontraumatic SAH were identified from the 2016 to 2022 Nationwide Readmissions Database. Multivariable regression models were developed to evaluate the independent and joint associations of SAH admission and clipping and coiling procedural volume with in-hospital outcomes. RESULTS: Of an estimated 142 271 hospitalizations, index mortality was 20.2%. Following risk adjustment, both increasing SAH admission volume and clipping and coiling procedural volume were independently associated with reduced mortality. When modeled jointly, however, clipping and coiling procedural volume remained an independent predictor of mortality (adjusted odds ratio, 0.981 per 10 procedures, P<0.001) whereas SAH admission volume was no longer significant (P=0.40). CONCLUSIONS: Joint examination of SAH and clipping and coiling procedural volume revealed procedural caseload to be the dominant predictor of in-hospital mortality, suggesting that survival benefits historically attributed to admission volume may be more precisely explained by procedural expertise. These findings support reexamination of volume-based benchmarks in contemporary cerebrovascular care frameworks.

recs.title: Psychological Stress and the Diurnal Patterns of Sodium Excretion and Blood Pressure: Results From the SABRE Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Psychological stress is associated with reduced blood pressure (BP) dipping, but the underlying mechanisms are unclear. This study examined the associations among stress-induced sodium excretion, diurnal sodium excretion, and BP dipping. METHODS: Apparently healthy adult participants underwent a laboratory session during which urinary sodium excretion was measured before and after mental stress tasks. Participants then completed 24-hour ambulatory BP monitoring and separate awake and asleep urine collections. The change in urinary sodium excretion rate with stress was defined as the difference in urinary sodium excretion rate before and after stress. The awake-to-asleep ratio of the urinary sodium excretion rate and systolic BP dipping were calculated from the 24-hour urine and BP measurements. RESULTS: In an adjusted model including age, sex, race, ethnicity, body mass index, mean systolic BP, mean diastolic BP, parental history of hypertension, fasting glucose, and 24-hour creatinine clearance, a smaller stress-induced urinary sodium excretion rate was associated with a lower awake-to-asleep ratio of urinary sodium excretion rate (n=180, B=0.2253 [95% CI, 0.0490-0.4016]). In an adjusted model including age, sex, race, ethnicity, body mass index, current smoking, alcohol use, fasting glucose, 24-hour sodium excretion, 24-hour potassium excretion, 24-hour creatinine clearance, and fractional excretion of sodium, a lower awake-to-asleep ratio of the urinary sodium excretion rate was associated with lower systolic BP dipping (n=175, B=1.0127 [95% CI, 0.0599-1.9656]). CONCLUSIONS: A lower stress-induced urinary sodium excretion rate was associated with a worse diurnal pattern of urinary sodium excretion, which was associated with lower systolic BP dipping. REGISTRATION INFORMATION: clinicaltrials.gov. Identifier: NCT03636490.

recs.title: Sudden Cardiac Arrest in Athletes With Cardiomyopathies: Focusing on the Fundamentals.
Long-Term Outcome Following Idiopathic Ventricular Fibrillation and Potential Emerging Etiologies.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Unexplained cardiac death and cardiac arrest associated with idiopathic ventricular fibrillation (IVF) are heterogeneous pathologies responsible for significant mortality in young people. OBJECTIVES: This retrospective multicenter cohort study evaluated the natural history of a large cohort of IVF survivors including recurrence burden, emerging etiologies, and long-term management. METHODS: This study included IVF patients from 46 tertiary centers and followed for at least 5 years. Patients over the age of 15 years who had documented ventricular fibrillation and extensive negative investigations supporting the diagnosis of IVF were included. Patients were followed in each center with their outcome being established on data collection from subsequent clinical records, new investigations, genetic results, and implanted defibrillator recordings. Recurrent arrhythmias and mortality were assessed. Diagnoses were graded as definite (direct evidence) or probable (indirect criteria). RESULTS: A total of 825 patients (37% women; age 35.7 ± 12 years) were followed for a median duration of 120 months (Q1-Q3: 78-180 months). Death occurred in 27 patients (3.3%) from cardiac (n = 10; 1.2%), noncardiac (n = 9; 1.1%), and unknown (n = 8; 1%) causes, and few patients (4.5%) developed overt cardiomyopathy. Overall arrhythmia recurrence increased steadily over 2 decades, reaching 52.7% of patients, with a median time to first recurrence of 20 months (Q1-Q3: 5-48 months) and a similar incidence in men and women. Emergent etiologies occurred in 68.8% of the total population, and were associated with new information during recurrences, structural changes, genetic results, and mapping procedures. They included reclassified inherited arrhythmia conditions in 73 (8.8%), focal sources in 272 (33.0%), and definite or probable microstructural myocardial alterations (MiCMs) with normal imaging in 223 (27.0%), while no diagnosis was identified in 257 (31.2%). Compared with MiCM, focal IVF included more women, occurred more frequently at rest/sleep, and was associated with narrow QRS complexes (90.1 ± 12 milliseconds vs 104.8 ± 16 milliseconds; P < 0.001). Quinidine appeared effective in preventing focal IVF (68.3%) whereas beta-blockers appeared effective (49.3%) in MiCM-IVF. Catheter ablation was performed in 181 patients with no recurrence observed in 75.7%. CONCLUSIONS: This multicenter long-term cohort study of IVF survivors shows low cardiac mortality, a persistent risk of arrhythmia recurrences over time, and identifies potential emerging etiologies.

recs.title: Systemic Inflammation and Adverse Heart Failure Outcomes: Insights From the Veterans Affairs Health Care System.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The association between systemic inflammation (SI) and outcomes among patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) or mildly reduced ejection fraction (HFmrEF) is uncertain. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the association between SI and clinical and economic outcomes among individuals with HFpEF/HFmrEF. METHODS: We identified Veterans with HFpEF/HFmrEF with outpatient high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) testing from 2008 to 2022. We classified Veterans as with SI (hsCRP 2-10 mg/L) and without SI (hsCRP <2 mg/L). The primary outcome was the 3-component major adverse cardiovascular event (MACE) outcome of death, HF hospitalization, and HF-related emergency department encounters. Additional outcomes included acute care utilization and costs. We evaluated the adjusted associations between SI and clinical outcomes, acute care utilization, and costs via Cox regression, negative binomial regression, and gamma regression, respectively. RESULTS: We identified 49,986 Veterans with HFpEF/HFmrEF with outpatient hsCRP levels. We compared 8,696 (17.4%) Veterans without SI (hsCRP <2 mg/L) and 25,352 (50.7%) Veterans with SI (hsCRP ≥2 mg/L and ≤10 mg/L Over a median follow-up of 3.4 years (IQR: 1.8-5.8), MACE incidence was 15.1/100 patient-years (95% CI: 14.9-15.4) among those with SI vs 11.8/100 patient-years (95% CI: 11.4-12.1) among those without SI (P < 0.001). After adjustment, SI was associated with increased MACE (HR: 1.28; 95% CI: 1.24-1.33). SI was also associated with increased all-cause hospitalizations (incidence rate ratio: 1.19; 95% CI: 1.137-1.246) and $9,112 (95% CI: $6,135-$12,089) in additional per-patient costs over 1 year. CONCLUSIONS: Among Veterans with HFmrEF/HFpEF, SI is associated with increased adverse clinical outcomes and higher costs.

recs.title: GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment and cardiovascular outcomes following aortic valve replacement: a nationwide observational study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: GLP-1 receptor agonists reduce major adverse cardiovascular events among patients with diabetes, overweight, and obesity. Whether these benefits extend to patients undergoing aortic valve replacement (AVR) for severe aortic stenosis (AS) remains unknown. Thus, we investigated the association between GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment and cardiovascular outcomes after AVR. METHODS: Nationwide population-based cohort study including consecutive patients with severe AS undergoing TAVI or SAVR in Western Denmark between January, 2016 and April, 2022. Patients were followed until death, emigration, crossover, or end of follow up on May 12, 2026. Propensity score-matching was performed to balance confounding. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, or aortic valve reoperation. Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, aortic valve reoperation, with analyses accounting for the competing risk of death. RESULTS: Among 5259 eligible patients undergoing AVR, 292 propensity score-matched patients were included in the final analyses. During a mean follow up of 4.8±2.4 years, GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment was associated with a lower risk of the primary composite outcome compared with controls (HR 0.69, 95%CI 0.50-0.96, p=0.029). GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment was also associated with lower risk of all-cause mortality (HR 0.66, 95%CI 0.46-0.95, p=0.025). In competing risk analyses accounting for death, lower risks were observed for heart failure hospitalization (HR 0.67, 95%CI 0.48-0.93, p=0.018), and aortic valve reoperation (HR 0.69, 95%CI 0.49-0.98, p=0.037). CONCLUSION: Treatment with GLP-1 receptor agonists was associated with lower risk of cardiovascular outcomes including mortality following AVR among patients with severe AS.

recs.title: Effect of Colchicine on Arterial Stiffness in Patients With Hypertension: The COlchicine HypERtENsion Trial (COHERENT).
recs.abstract: AIM: This trial investigated whether colchicine, an anti-inflammatory treatment, affects cardiovascular structure and function, assessed by arterial stiffness, blood pressure and biochemistry, compared with placebo. METHODS: COHERENT was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of the effects of colchicine on arterial stiffness in adults with pharmacologically treated hypertension without cardiovascular disease. Eligible patients were randomized 1:1 to colchicine 0.5mg daily or placebo for six months. Assessment of arterial stiffness, echocardiography, and biomarker measurement were performed at baseline and six months. The primary endpoint was change in carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity (cfPWV). Secondary endpoints included change in blood pressure (BP), left ventricular mass index, as well as change in cardiac and inflammatory biomarkers. RESULTS: Of 183 screened, 150 were randomized (75 per group). Mean age was 64.5 (±8.0) years, 53 (35.3%) were female, and mean systolic blood pressure was 137.6 (±15.6) mmHg. At six months, cfPWV did not differ between groups (between-group difference in ΔcfPWV -0.1m/s, 95% CI: -0.5 to 0.3m/s, p=0.53). Office systolic BP decreased significantly more in the placebo group than in the colchicine group (between-group difference in Δoffice systolic BP 5.7 mmHg, 95% CI: 1.0 to 10.5 mmHg, p=0.018. hsCRP decreased significantly in the colchicine group compared with the placebo group (between-group difference in % change in hsCRP -39.8%, 95% CI: -59.1 to -11.4%, p=0.010). Left ventricular mass index or cardiac biomarkers did not differ between groups. CONCLUSIONS: Six months of colchicine did not affect arterial stiffness in pharmacologically treated hypertension without cardiovascular disease. Colchicine significantly decreased hsCRP.

recs.title: Role for Factor XIa Inhibitors after an Acute Coronary Syndrome Event.
Sex differences in cardiovascular disease burden, risk factors, and disease spectrum in Europe: a global burden of disease 2023 analysis within the ESC Atlas framework.
recs.abstract: Despite growing recognition of sex disparities in cardiovascular disease (CVD), contemporary, harmonized analyses of sex-specific burden in the European region that could inform targeted prevention strategies, remain limited. Sex-specific patterns in CVD burden and risk factor exposure across 55 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) member countries were examined using data from the 2023 Global Burden of Disease study. Risk factor exposure was quantified using age-sex-standardized summary exposure values for 10 established cardiovascular risk factors. Disease incidence and mortality for major CVD categories, including maternal hypertensive disorders, were estimated by calculating age-sex-standardized rates per 100 000 person-years using the 2013 European Standard Population. Analyses were performed by sex at country, regional, and ESC-wide levels and over time (1990-2023). In 2023, in the ESC region, the overall CVD burden was broadly similar in men and women, with women accounting for 55% (6.0 million) of cases and 50% of deaths (1.5 million). This apparent parity, however, concealed marked sex differences in disease composition, risk exposure, and geographic disparities. Compared with men, women had a lower proportion of CVD due to ischaemic heart disease (21% vs 38%) and a higher contribution from peripheral arterial disease (23% vs 19%). Major differences were also apparent in risk profiles, particularly for behavioural risk factors-with summary exposure values of tobacco and alcohol being 10%-20% points higher in men than women; contrasting with cardiometabolic factors, such as high body mass index and low physical activity, that were often 5%-15% points higher in women than men, and more modest differences in environmental and biological risks, including air pollution, fasting glucose, or cholesterol. Cardiovascular disease burden further varied widely across countries and disparities affected women more strongly than men, with an approximately three-fold difference between the lowest- and highest-incidence countries in women, compared with a two-fold difference in men, and even larger disparities in mortality and premature mortality (up to 25-fold in women). Maternal hypertensive disorders substantially shaped both the scale and composition of CVD burden in women, accounting for 25% of incident CVD in women and exhibiting substantial geographic variation, with up to 18-fold differences in incidence across countries. These findings challenge conventional approaches that treat CVD as a homogeneous condition. In particular, the substantial contribution of non-ischaemic conditions and maternal hypertensive disorders to the burden in women, alongside distinct patterns of risk exposure and wider geographic disparities, underscore the importance of adopting a life-course and sex- and gender-informed approach to cardiovascular prevention and policy.

recs.title: Beyond tetramer stability: wild-type ATTR-CM as a disease of the ageing myocardium.
Risk-weighted apoB and lipoprotein-associated coronary risk across ethnic groups.
recs.abstract: AIMS: Apolipoprotein B (apoB) reflects the number of circulating atherogenic lipoproteins but does not account for differences in particle atherogenicity. Risk-weighted apoB (RW-apoB), which incorporates triglyceride-rich lipoproteins and lipoprotein(a) (Lp(a)), may better capture lipoprotein-driven coronary risk, but its performance across diverse populations remains uncertain. We assessed whether the prespecified triglyceride - and Lp(a)-weighted information captured by RW-apoB was associated with coronary events beyond apoB and compared the discrimination of RW-apoB and measured apoB across ethnicities. METHODS: We analyzed 40,132 participants with 4,509 coronary events from ARIC, CARDIA, MESA, the Framingham Offspring Study, and China Kadoorie Biobank. RW-apoB was calculated using a prespecified equation. Mutually adjusted Cox estimates were pooled within ethnic groups using random-effects meta-analysis. Separate single-marker models compared discrimination. Sensitivity analyses included age and sex adjustment, standardized exposures, hard-events, truncated follow-up, and CKB-specific logistic regression. RESULTS: Mean RW-apoB exceeded apoB by approximately 8 mg/dL in African American and Chinese participants, reflecting higher lipoprotein(a) and triglycerides, respectively. RW-apoB was associated with coronary events conditional on apoB in White, African American, Chinese, and Hispanic participants: hazard ratios per 10 mg/dL were 1.11 (95% CI 1.05-1.18), 1.11 (1.08-1.15), 1.08 (1.05-1.11), and 1.10 (1.01-1.21), respectively. C-indices for RW-apoB versus apoB were 0.630 versus 0.617 in White (P<0.001), 0.606 versus 0.595 in African American (P=0.085), 0.567 versus 0.554 in Chinese (P=0.014), and 0.540 versus 0.535 in Hispanic participants (P=0.756). CONCLUSION: RW-apoB captured lipoprotein-associated risk beyond measured apoB, with discrimination gains statistically demonstrable in the larger White and Chinese groups.

recs.title: Acute Myocardial Infarction in Cancer Patients Treated With Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
Follistatin-Mediated Browning of Adipose Tissue Improves Cardiometabolic Health.
BAFF Bridge Linking Lupus Autoimmunity to Pulmonary Vascular Damage.
Biophysical principles of pulsed field ablation.
recs.abstract: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) is emerging as a major advance in cardiac ablation because it induces irreversible electroporation rather than relying primarily on thermal injury. This article provides an overview of the core biophysical principles underlying PFA, focusing on concepts broadly relevant across systems and clinical applications. Externally applied pulsed electric fields interact with biological tissues and affect their transmembrane potential. When a critical threshold is exceeded, nanoscale aqueous pores form in the lipid bilayer, initiating electroporation. Depending on pulse amplitude, duration, number, repetition frequency, waveform, and tissue characteristics, membrane permeabilization may remain reversible or progress to irreversible injury and cell death. This article focuses on the fundamental biophysical principles of electroporation that underpin PFA. The article outlines how membrane charging, cell geometry, and tissue heterogeneity influence electric field distribution and biological response and explains why lesion formation depends on both field intensity and exposure conditions. It also summarizes the molecular basis of pore formation, the potential contribution of lipid peroxidation and membrane proteins, and the downstream processes linking sustained permeability to loss of homeostasis and delayed cell death. Finally, it places cardiac PFA in the broader context of electroporation-based therapies developed in oncology, drug delivery, and gene transfer, while highlighting the remaining need for cardiomyocyte-specific mechanistic evidence to further optimize safety, precision, and durability.

recs.title: Coexistance of Carotid Sinus Hypersensitivity and Orthostatic Hypotension in Patients with Unexplained Syncope.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Carotid sinus hypersensitivity (CSH) and orthostatic hypotension (OH) are established causes of syncope but are often considered separate entities. However, evidence suggests that CSH and OH may coexist and jointly contribute to syncope. This study investigates the relationship between CSH and OH in patients with unexplained syncope. METHODS: A total of 1,908 patients aged ≥40 years (age, 63.7 ± 13.0 years; men, 45.3%) with unexplained syncope underwent carotid sinus massage (CSM) and head-up tilt testing (HUT). Occurrence of CSH in classical and delayed OH, including asystolic CSM responses was analysed. RESULTS: Six-hundred-and-eighteen patients (32.4%, 68.9 ± 11.3 years) had OH, while CSH was present in 320 patients (16.8%, 72.2 ± 9.9 years), and was more common in patients with OH than without OH (24.1% vs. 13.3%, p < 0.001). Among patients with CSH, 46.6% also had OH. CSH occurred equally in both classical OH (62/275, 22.5%) and delayed OH (87/345, 25.2%). Among OH patients, CSH was associated with older age, male sex, lower supine diastolic blood pressure, hypertension, and syncope-related hospital admission. An asystolic CSM response was observed more often in OH patients (n = 42; 6.8%) compared with non-OH patients (n = 44, 3.4%, p < 0.001) and was associated with older age and lower resting heart rate. CONCLUSIONS: CSH and OH frequently coexist in adults over 40 years evaluated for syncope. CSM may reveal a clinically relevant cardioinhibitory reflex in a subgroup of OH patients, supporting comprehensive cardiovascular autonomic testing in unexplained syncope.

recs.title: Temporal Alignment of Remodeling Trajectories in Mild HCM.
ANOCA Patients With Prior Obstructive Coronary Artery Disease and PCI Have Higher Odds of Epicardial Spasm.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Up to 50% of patients undergoing coronary angiography have angina with no obstructive coronary arteries (ANOCA). Among ANOCA patients, 2 distinct groups exist: patients with and without a history of prior obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD) treated with percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). OBJECTIVES: This study aims to evaluate associations between history of prior obstructive CAD treated with PCI and coronary microvascular and vasomotor dysfunction endotypes in ANOCA patients. METHODS: A prospective Coronary Microvascular and Vasomotor Dysfunction Registry of consecutive ANOCA patients undergoing invasive coronary functional testing (ICFT). RESULTS: Among 624 ANOCA patients undergoing ICFT, 11% had prior obstructive CAD treated with PCI. ANOCA patients with prior obstructive CAD had a higher prevalence of males, were older, and had higher rates of cardiovascular risk factors. Prior obstructive CAD treated with PCI was associated with an 11-point lower Seattle Angina Questionnaire 7 summary score in unadjusted (β -11.0; 95% CI: -17.0 to -4.4; P = 0.001) and adjusted models. Patients with prior obstructive CAD treated with PCI had a higher prevalence of epicardial spasm by angiographic criteria (70% vs 34%; P < 0.001) and 4.55-fold higher odds of epicardial spasm in unadjusted (OR: 4.55; 95% CI: 2.65-8.07; P < 0.001) and adjusted models, with similar odds of coronary microvascular dysfunction. CONCLUSIONS: Among ANOCA patients, those with prior obstructive CAD treated with PCI had over a 4-fold higher odds of epicardial spasm. These findings underscore the need for comprehensive ICFT in ANOCA patients with prior PCI.

recs.title: Joint Impacts of Ambient Air Pollution and Temperature on Cardiovascular Disease in West Florida.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Ambient temperature and fine particulate matter with an aerodynamic diameter ≤2.5 μm (PM2.5) are well-established contributors of acute cardiovascular events, but their joint short-term effects in subtropical coastal regions have not been well characterized. We evaluated their joint associations with major cardiovascular outcomes in West Florida. METHODS: We analyzed daily hospital admissions for myocardial infarction, heart failure, and stroke within the BayCare Health System from 2017 to 2024. Daily mean temperature and PM2.5 were obtained from national monitoring networks. Joint exposure-response relationships were estimated using distributed-lag generalized additive models with tensor-product interactions across lags 0 to 7 days, adjusting for temporal trends, day of week, and copollutants. Effect modification by age, sex, and race was examined. RESULTS: Temperature showed stronger short-term associations with cardiovascular risk than local PM2.5. Among adults aged ≥65 years, myocardial infarction risk was higher at lower temperatures, compared with higher temperatures (relative risk comparing the 75th versus the 25th percentile of the exposure distribution [RR75/25], 0.92 [95% CI, 0.89-0.95]). Heart failure exhibited a U-shaped temperature-risk relationship, with greater heat-related risk observed among younger adults (RR75/25, 1.05 [95% CI, 1.02-1.09]) and Black patients (RR75/25, 1.05 [95% CI, 1.02-1.09]). In contrast, PM2.5 showed weaker overall associations, with only a modest elevation in stroke risk among Black patients (RR75/25, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.96-1.08]). Joint exposure surfaces revealed outcome-specific nonlinear patterns, particularly for heart failure at higher temperature and PM2.5. CONCLUSIONS: Temperature and PM2.5 jointly influence short-term cardiovascular risk through nonlinear and subgroup-specific pathways, highlighting the need for integrated climate and air-quality strategies to reduce cardiovascular disparities.

recs.title: Time-Varying Spatial Ventricular Gradient Orientation Is Associated With Anthracycline Heart Failure.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Anthracycline use is limited by cardiotoxicity resulting in heart failure (HF). The spatial ventricular gradient (SVG) is a vectorcardiographic measurement of myocardial electrical heterogeneity associated with sudden death and incident HF. It is unclear if serial measurement of SVG after anthracycline initiation can help predict subsequent HF. OBJECTIVES: The objective of the study was to determine if time-varying SVG measurements are associated with anthracycline HF. METHODS: Retrospective, single-center study of adult patients with cancer treated with anthracyclines between 1992 to 2019. Standard 12-lead electrocardiograms obtained within 6 months before and up to 5 years after anthracycline initiation were analyzed. Patients with prior HF or ≤1 electrocardiogram within 5 years were excluded. Median vectorcardiograms were constructed, and the SVG vector was obtained by integrating under the X, Y, and Z QRST complexes. Multivariable competing-risks regression was performed with SVG parameters included as time-varying covariates, incident HF as the main outcome, and death as a competing outcome. RESULTS: Among 594 patients (median age 61 years, 48% male), 83 (14%) developed HF within 5 years. In multivariable competing-risks regression, time-varying SVG azimuth (circular angle in the transverse plane) was independently associated with HF (P = 0.0024), demonstrating a 9.4-fold gradient in risk across values. Leftward/anterior azimuth values were the lowest risk areas, whereas posterior/rightward orientations were the highest risk. CONCLUSIONS: Time-varying SVG azimuth was independently associated with HF risk in patients treated with anthracyclines. Assessing dynamic changes in SVG azimuth during anthracycline treatment may enhance early identification of patients at risk for HF and inform the use of cardioprotective strategies during cancer therapy.

recs.title: Reproducible haemodynamics, unresolved indication: where does thrombectomy for acute pulmonary embolism stand?
Ten-year Performance of the Multi-Layer Insulated Defibrillation Lead in the Medicare Population.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Long-term surveillance of implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) leads is essential because clinically important mechanical failures may emerge years after implantation. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate 10-year mechanical complication-free survival of the Optisure ICD lead (Abbott, Sylmar, CA) in a large real-world Medicare population. METHODS: Manufacturer device-tracking records were linked to Medicare Fee-for-Service claims and device complaint data using the EP PASSION framework. Patients receiving an Optisure lead from February 2014 through December 2024 were included. Mechanical lead-related complications were defined by claims containing both a diagnosis of mechanical lead malfunction and a lead-related surgical intervention more than 30 days after implantation. Kaplan-Meier survival was estimated under a best-case scenario including confirmed Optisure-related events and a worst-case scenario also including potentially related events. RESULTS: The cohort included 26,830 patients with 27,033 Optisure leads. Mean age was 73.8 ± 8.6 years, 28.4% were women, and 49.8% had cardiac resynchronization therapy ICDs. Overall, 379 complications were classified as confirmed lead-related and 606 as confirmed or potentially lead-related. At 10 years, complication-free lead survival was 97.2% (95% confidence interval [CI], 96.7%-97.7%) in the best-case scenario and 95.6% (95% CI, 94.9%-96.2%) in the worst-case scenario. Survival did not differ significantly by age, lead length, coil configuration, or device type. CONCLUSION: The Optisure ICD lead demonstrated favorable mechanical performance through 10 years in routine clinical practice. These findings support both the long-term durability of Optisure and the use of integrated real-world data for post-market device surveillance.

recs.title: Outcomes of Intra-Arterial Urokinase After Endovascular Reperfusion for Acute Ischemic Stroke Due to Cardioembolism: A Secondary Analysis of the POST-UK Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Whether adjunctive intra-arterial thrombolysis improves outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke due to cardioembolism remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the efficacy and safety of adjunctive intra-arterial urokinase in patients with acute ischemic stroke due to cardioembolism who achieved near-complete to complete reperfusion. METHODS: This study was a secondary analysis of the POST-UK (Adjunctive Intra-Arterial Urokinase After Near-Complete to Complete Reperfusion for Acute Ischemic Stroke) trial, which was conducted from November 15, 2022, to March 29, 2024. Patients were randomly assigned to the intra-arterial urokinase group or the control group. The primary outcome was disability-free survival at 90 days, defined as a modified Rankin Scale score of 0 to 1. Safety outcomes included 90-day all-cause death, symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage and any intracranial hemorrhage within 48 hours. RESULTS: Among 209 patients with cardioembolism (median age 73 [interquartile range, 63-81] years; 45.9% men), 106 were assigned to the control group and 103 to the intra-arterial urokinase group. Compared with the control group, adjunctive intra-arterial urokinase significantly increased the odds of disability-free survival at 90 days (adjusted risk ratio, 1.49 [95% CI, 1.08-2.06]; P=0.01; inverse probability of treatment weighting adjusted risk ratio, 1.47 [95% CI, 1.04-2.09]; P=0.03). No significant differences were found between groups in 90-day mortality rate, symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage, or any intracranial hemorrhage within 48 hours. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with acute ischemic stroke due to cardioembolism who achieved near-complete to complete reperfusion, adjunctive intra-arterial urokinase significantly improved disability-free survival at 90 days without increasing the risk of death or intracranial hemorrhage. REGISTRATION: URL: ChiCTR.org.cn; Unique identifier: ChiCTR2200065617.

Steatotic liver disease phenotypes and stroke risk in patients with atrial fibrillation: A nationwide population-based cohort study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The updated nomenclature of steatotic liver disease (SLD) recognizes distinct phenotypes, including Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), MASLD with increased alcohol intake (MetALD), and alcohol-related liver disease (ALD). Although cardiovascular risk may differ across SLD phenotypes, their association with stroke risk in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) remains unclear. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the association between SLD phenotypes and ischemic stroke risk in AF patients. METHODS: AF patients diagnosed between 2010 and 2018 were identified from the Korean health insurance database. According to SLD phenotype, patients were categorized into No-SLD, MASLD, MetALD, and ALD. The primary outcome was ischemic stroke. Subgroup analyses were conducted by CHA2DS2-VA score. RESULTS: Among 196,242 patients (No-SLD: 101,308; MASLD: 77,715; MetALD: 8,678; ALD: 8,541), median follow-up was 5.9 years. Compared with No-SLD, MASLD was not associated with stroke risk (adjusted hazard ratio and 95% confidence interval; 1.00, 0.97-1.04), whereas MetALD and ALD were associated with higher risk (1.09, 1.00-1.18 and 1.16, 1.08-1.26, respectively). In exploratory subgroup analyses, the higher risk associated with alcohol-related phenotypes appeared more apparent at lower CHA2DS2-VA scores; however, the 6-year absolute risk differences were approximately 1% or less, and these findings are regarded as hypothesis-generating. CONCLUSION: In patients with AF, stroke risk was significantly higher in the alcohol-related SLD phenotypes, MetALD and ALD, whereas MASLD was not associated with stroke risk. These findings are consistent with the current recommendations for comprehensive risk-factor management in AF, with particular attention to alcohol intake in patients with alcohol-related SLD phenotypes.

recs.title: Baseline Characteristics, Geriatric Syndromes, and Clinical Outcomes During Implementation of a Cardiovascular Center on Aging.
The evolution and future of conduction system pacing.
recs.abstract: Cardiac pacing has undergone a fundamental paradigm shift from conventional right ventricular apical pacing towards physiological activation of the native conduction system of the heart. Decades of evidence have established that chronic right ventricular pacing induces ventricular dyssynchrony, contributing to pacing-induced cardiomyopathy and adverse clinical outcomes. Conduction system pacing, which engages the intrinsic His-Purkinje network of the heart, has emerged as a transformative approach that preserves or restores the natural ventricular activation sequence. His bundle pacing, the earliest form of conduction system pacing, provided proof of concept but is limited by technical challenges and high capture thresholds. Left bundle branch area pacing has since become the dominant modality, offering greater procedural success, lead stability and broader applicability: from management of bradycardia and prevention of pacing-induced cardiomyopathy to cardiac resynchronization therapy in heart failure. Bachmann bundle area pacing is an emerging atrial counterpart: by capturing a preferential interatrial conduction pathway, this approach reduces interatrial conduction delay and produces a more physiological atrial activation sequence than conventional right atrial appendage pacing. Bachmann bundle area pacing might, therefore, help to prevent atrial fibrillation. In this Review, we bring these ventricular and atrial strategies together under the unifying principle of physiological pacing, describe their mechanistic basis and technical evolution, appraise the latest evidence from randomized trials and address the practical questions that arise in clinical application, indicating where more evidence is required.
