Effectiveness of Discrete Strategies and Implementation Bundles for Improving Clinician Prescription of Clinical Practice Guideline-Recommended Medications for Atherosclerotic Occlusive Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: We sought to determine the effectiveness of discrete strategies and implementation bundles for improving clinical practice guideline (CPG) strongly recommended medication prescription to adults with atherosclerotic occlusive disease. METHODS: We searched MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, PsycINFO, and Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature (inception to December 9, 2025) for randomized controlled trials evaluating discrete strategies or implementation bundles for improving CPG strongly recommended medication prescription to adults with atherosclerotic occlusive disease. Two investigators screened titles/abstracts and full texts, extracted data, assessed risk of bias, and classified discrete strategies and implementation bundles. Random-effects models were used for meta-analysis. Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation was used to assess certainty. RESULTS: We included 31 randomized controlled trials studying 29 unique discrete strategies and implementation bundles. The implementation bundle with the largest effect size for improving CPG strongly recommended medication prescription combined case management, team changes, continuous quality improvement, audit/feedback, and clinician and patient education (relative risk, 2.62 [95% CI, 2.08-3.29]; moderate certainty). Meta-regression analyses suggested that discrete strategies and implementation bundles using patient education were more effective at improving statin (P=0.037) and all CPG strongly recommended medication (P=0.006) prescription. Combining case management, team changes, facilitated relay of information, and audit/feedback reduced all-cause death and new vascular event risk. Team changes improved prescription of all CPG strongly recommended medications (relative risk, 1.23 [95% CI, 1.11-1.36]; moderate certainty) and reduced major adverse cardiac event risk. CONCLUSIONS: Combining case management, team changes, continuous quality improvement, audit/feedback, and clinician and patient education had the largest effect size for improving CPG strongly recommended medication prescription and improved patient outcomes. Team changes improved CPG strongly recommended medication prescription and reduced major adverse cardiac event risk.

recs.title: Classification and Outcomes of Coronary Microvascular Disease in Myocardial Infarction and Angina With Nonobstructive Coronary Arteries.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Myocardial infarction with nonobstructive coronary arteries (MINOCAs) and angina with nonobstructive coronary arteries (ANOCAs) present diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. We assessed the frequency of coronary microvascular disease (CMD) and its subtypes in MINOCA compared with ANOCA and evaluated long-term cardiovascular outcomes. METHODS: Patients with nonobstructive coronary arteries undergoing invasive coronary function testing from 2012 to 2022 were prospectively enrolled and retrospectively classified as MINOCA or ANOCA (reference group). Myocardial infarction due to atherothrombosis, myocarditis, and Takotsubo syndrome were excluded. Invasive provocation testing was performed. CMD was classified as endothelium-independent (coronary flow reserve <2.5 with adenosine) and endothelium-dependent (<50% increase in coronary blood flow with acetylcholine). Major adverse cardiovascular events (cardiac death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, heart failure hospitalization, urgent revascularization, stroke) were recorded over 8 years. RESULTS: Of 622 patients, 73 (12%) had MINOCA (69% female, median age 56 years) and 549 (88%) ANOCA (72% female, median age 53 years). CMD was common in both groups (71% versus 64%; P=0.271), while endothelium-independent CMD was more frequent in MINOCA (41% versus 21%; P<0.001). Over a median follow-up of 4.5 years, major adverse cardiovascular events occurred more often in MINOCA (40% versus 11%; adjusted hazard ratio, 2.4; P=0.001). CMD predicted higher major adverse cardiovascular events in both MINOCA (hazard ratio, 3.6 [95% CI, 1.1-12.0]; P=0.038) and ANOCA (hazard ratio, 7.9 [95% CI, 2.9-21.8]; P<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: CMD is common in both MINOCA and ANOCA. The higher prevalence of endothelium-independent CMD in MINOCA suggests a potential mechanistic role in infarction. Patients with MINOCA have a worse prognosis than ANOCA, particularly when CMD is present.

recs.title: Physical Activity and Cardiovascular Risk in Type 2 Diabetes With Normal Body Mass Index and Abdominal Obesity: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The prognostic implications of abdominal obesity and moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) in patients with type 2 diabetes who have a normal body mass index remain unclear. METHODS: This nationwide retrospective cohort study included 323 029 adults with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes and a normal body mass index (<23 kg/m2) between January 1, 2010, and December 31, 2023, from the Korean National Health Insurance Service database. Abdominal obesity was defined using sex-specific waist circumference thresholds (≥90 cm for men, ≥80 cm for women). MVPA was assessed through standardized self-reported questionnaires administered during routine health screenings. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events, defined as a composite of all-cause death, myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, or hospitalization for heart failure. RESULTS: Among the study population, 34 033 (10.5%) had abdominal obesity. During a median follow-up of 6.0 years (interquartile range, 2.6-9.0 years), abdominal obesity was associated with a higher risk of major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 1.13 [95% CI, 1.09-1.17]). Among patients with abdominal obesity, regular MVPA after diagnosis (27.1%) was associated with a significantly lower risk of major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (adjusted HR 0.74 [95% CI, 0.68-0.80]), all-cause mortality (adjusted HR 0.72 [95% CI, 0.65-0.80]), ischemic stroke (adjusted HR 0.77 [95% CI, 0.66-0.89]), and hospitalization for heart failure (adjusted HR 0.75 [95% CI, 0.60-0.93]). The cardiovascular protective effects of MVPA were consistent regardless of statin or antidiabetic medication use. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with type 2 diabetes and a normal body mass index, abdominal obesity was independently associated with a higher risk of major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events. Regular engagement in MVPA showed consistent cardiovascular benefits in this population, irrespective of pharmacotherapy. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT07071545.

recs.title: Life expectancy after aortic valve replacement: a nationwide analysis.
Retatrutide Once Weekly for Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Retatrutide, an investigational triple agonist of glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon-like peptide 1, and glucagon receptors, may be useful for treating obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). METHODS: In two phase 3, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trials nested within larger basket trials of once-weekly subcutaneous retatrutide, we assigned adults with moderate-to-severe OSA and a body-mass index (the weight in kilograms divided by the square of the height in meters) of at least 27, without (TRIUMPH-1-OSA) or with (TRIUMPH-2-OSA) type 2 diabetes, to receive retatrutide (4, 9, or 12 mg) or placebo. The primary end point was the change in the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI, the average number of apneas and hypopneas per hour of sleep) at 80 weeks with 9 mg and 12 mg of retatrutide. For OSA-related end points, a hybrid-treatment estimand was applied, with a hypothetical strategy used for participants who had intercurrent events suggesting treatment failure and a treatment-policy strategy used elsewhere. We also report intention-to-treat (ITT) results. RESULTS: A total of 243 participants underwent randomization in TRIUMPH-1-OSA and 448 in TRIUMPH-2-OSA. The baseline mean AHI was 58.6 and 55.9 events per hour, respectively, and the mean body weight was 119.6 and 115.9 kg. At 80 weeks, the mean changes in the AHI (hybrid-treatment estimand) with retatrutide in TRIUMPH-1-OSA were -22.9 (4 mg), -34.3 (9 mg), and -31.7 (12 mg) events per hour, versus -9.9 with placebo (difference vs. placebo, -13.0 [95% confidence interval {CI}, -23.0 to -3.0], -24.4 [95% CI, -34.1 to -14.7], and -21.9 [95% CI, -32.2 to -11.5], respectively). The changes with retatrutide in TRIUMPH-2-OSA were -19.2 (4 mg), -24.7 (9 mg), and -25.4 (12 mg) events per hour, versus -10.3 with placebo (difference vs. placebo, -8.9 [95% CI, -15.9 to -2.0], -14.4 [95% CI, -21.6 to -7.2], and -15.1 [95% CI, -22.5 to -7.7]). For the ITT estimand, the corresponding differences from placebo were -13.2 (95% CI, -22.6 to -3.9), -24.7 (95% CI, -34.1 to -15.3), and -22.5 (95% CI, -31.9 to -13.1) in TRIUMPH-1-OSA and -8.8 (95% CI, -15.8 to -1.7), -13.9 (95% CI, -21.3 to -6.6), and -15.0 (95% CI, -22.5 to -7.4) in TRIUMPH-2-OSA. The mean percent change in body weight with retatrutide (key secondary end point) was -12.5 to -22.2% in TRIUMPH-1-OSA and -12.1 to -18.5% in TRIUMPH-2-OSA, versus -4.8% and -5.6% with placebo (treatment-regimen estimand). The most common adverse events were gastrointestinal. CONCLUSIONS: In adults with OSA and obesity or overweight with or without type 2 diabetes, retatrutide resulted in significantly greater decreases in the AHI than placebo. (Funded by Eli Lilly; TRIUMPH-1 and -2 ClinicalTrials.gov numbers, NCT05929066 and NCT05929079.).

recs.title: Vascular Function and Cardiorespiratory Fitness in Adults Who Use Nicotine Vapes.
recs.abstract: IMPORTANCE: The rising use of nicotine vapes among young adults who have never smoked combustible tobacco raises concerns regarding potential early cardiovascular and respiratory effects in an otherwise low-risk population. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether regular daily nicotine vape use is associated with altered vascular function and cardiorespiratory fitness in young adults without established cardiovascular risk factors. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This was a cross-sectional, single-center, laboratory-based physiological assessment study conducted between July 2023 and April 2025 among young adults without known cardiovascular disease or major risk factors. Based on self-report and verification of smoking status, participants were stratified into 3 groups: adults who exclusively used nicotine vapes, adults who used combustible cigarettes, and tobacco- and nicotine vape-naive individuals. Data analysis was performed from September 2023 to April 2025. EXPOSURE: Regular daily use of nicotine vapes or combustible cigarettes. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary outcomes included vascular function, assessed by flow-mediated dilation (FMD) and carotid artery reactivity (CAR), and cardiorespiratory fitness, assessed through ventilatory, metabolic, and cardiac responses during maximal cardiopulmonary exercise testing. Secondary measures included spirometry results and physical activity. RESULTS: Fifty-eight young adults (mean [SD] age, 26 [7] years; 30 [52%] female) were included, among whom 17 exclusively used nicotine vapes, 19 used combustible cigarettes, and 22 were tobacco and nicotine vape naive. Lung function and physical activity levels did not differ significantly across groups. FMD and CAR were lower both in adults who used nicotine vapes (mean [SD] FMD, 5.5% [3.4%]; mean [SD] CAR, 0.6% [5.3%]) and in adults who used combustible cigarettes (mean [SD] FMD, 4.4% [2.9%]; mean [SD] CAR, -1.4% [5.3%]) compared with tobacco- and nicotine vape-naive individuals (mean [SD] FMD, 8.3% [3.4%]; mean [SD] CAR, 4.7% [3.2%]). Peak oxygen uptake was lower in adults who used nicotine vapes compared with tobacco- and nicotine vape-naive individuals but did not differ significantly between combustible cigarette and naive groups; minute ventilation and cardiac output were lower in both nicotine use groups. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Regular daily nicotine vape use in young adults who have never smoked combustible tobacco was associated with lower vascular function and cardiorespiratory fitness. These findings highlight the need for longitudinal studies to determine long-term clinical implications.

recs.title: Hypertension and Subclinical Vascular Damage After Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with hematological malignancies undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (alloHSCT) face a higher risk of premature cardiovascular disease that may partly be explained by hypertension. OBJECTIVES: The authors studied the prevalence of hypertension in alloHSCT survivors at least 1 year post-transplant. METHODS: Two hundred survivors were clinically screened for hypertension. Hypertension was defined according to established ambulatory blood pressure monitoring (ABPM) thresholds. Subclinical vascular damage was assessed through carotid intima-media thickness by ultrasonography of the carotid arteries, pulse wave velocity, and renal function. RESULTS: Of the 200 patients, 168 (84%) completed the 24-hour ABPM. The median age was 57 years (IQR: 46.3-65.0; range: 18-75). Of the 168 patients, 90 patients (53.6%) had hypertension, of which 26 (15.5%) were newly diagnosed, and 56 (33.3%) were untreated. Hypertensive patients by ABPM tended to be older (median 58 [IQR: 49-67] vs 55.5 [IQR: 39.75-64] years; P = 0.060), had a higher intima-media thickness (0.84 ± 0.25 vs 0.76 ± 0.26 mm; P = 0.009), higher pulse wave velocity values (9.0 ± 2.3 vs 7.3 ± 1.6 m/s; P < 0.001), and lower mean estimated glomerular filtration rate (72.3 ± 18.7 vs 80.4 ± 22.5 mL/min/1.73 m2; P = 0.010) compared to normotensive patients. In the logistic regression model, both age in years (OR: 1.03; 95% CI: 1.01-1.05; P = 0.019) and family history of cardiovascular disease and/or premature death (OR: 2.28; 95% CI: 1.17-4.44; P = 0.016) were independently associated with hypertension. CONCLUSIONS: Hypertension is highly prevalent, underrecognized, and undertreated in alloHSCT survivors and is cross-sectionally associated with subclinical vascular and renal organ damage.

recs.title: Operator-level variation in the extensiveness of percutaneous coronary intervention for acute coronary syndrome.
Efficacy and Safety of Pharmacologic Therapies in Nonobstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: A Systematic Review.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Nonobstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) affects approximately one-third of all patients with HCM and carries substantial morbidity, yet no approved disease-modifying therapies exist. We conducted a systematic review of prospective interventional studies evaluating pharmacologic therapies in adults with nonobstructive HCM. METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and Clinicaltrials.gov was performed through September 2025. Eligible studies included randomized and nonrandomized prospective interventional trials. A narrative synthesis was performed by pharmacologic class and outcome domain. RESULTS: Twenty-nine clinical trials evaluating 9 pharmacologic classes were identified: cardiac myosin inhibitors, cardiac sarcomere modulators, metabolic modulators, angiotensin II receptor blockers, angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, SGLT2 (sodium-glucose cotransporter 2) inhibitors, beta blockers, and calcium channel blockers. Cardiac myosin inhibitors demonstrated reductions in left ventricular hypertrophy, improvements in diastolic function, and marked reductions in cardiac biomarkers, although improvements in exercise capacity and symptoms were variable. SGLT2 inhibition showed concordant improvements in diastolic function, atrial remodeling, biomarkers, and functional status in patients with symptomatic nonobstructive HCM and comorbid type 2 diabetes. Angiotensin receptor blockade showed signals of structural remodeling with valsartan and candesartan without consistent functional benefit. Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonism and angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibition demonstrated largely neutral effects. Among metabolic modulators, ninerafaxstat improved ventilatory efficiency and quality of life in patients with greater baseline symptom burden. CONCLUSIONS: Pharmacologic responsiveness in nonobstructive HCM is variable and appears to be mechanism- and disease stage-dependent. Ongoing trials evaluating cardiac myosin inhibitors, SGLT inhibitors, and novel therapeutic agents including ninerafaxstat and EDG-7500 will be critical in further defining the therapeutic landscape.

recs.title: American Heart Association Life's Essential 8 and Heart Failure in Black Individuals: An Analysis of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Self-reported Black individuals have a disproportionately high prevalence of heart failure (HF) compared with other racial groups. In an effort to empower patients and health providers to combat cardiovascular disease, the American Heart Association identified Life's Essential 8 as the 8 health behaviors crucial for heart health. In this study, we evaluate the association between components of Life's Essential 8 and HF outcomes among Black individuals. METHODS: This cross-sectional observational study analyzed 107 622 individuals captured in the NHANES (National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey) from 1999 to 2020 who were categorized by self-reported race. To represent Life's Essential 8, variables of self-reported sleep duration, physical activity, smoking status, and dietary habits were used. Additionally, self-reported diagnoses of diabetes, hyperlipidemia, hypertension, and heart failure were included. Multivariable logistic regression models were constructed to estimate odds ratios (ORs) and 95% CIs for the associations between Life's Essential 8 components and HF among Black individuals. RESULTS: Black individuals were diagnosed with HF at a younger age compared with White individuals (54 years vs 65 years, P<0.001). Among Black individuals, body mass index (odds ratio [OR], 1.041 [95% CI, 1.027-1.055], P=0.02), hypertension (OR, 3.175 [95% CI, 2.14-4.69], P<0.0001), hyperlipidemia (OR, 1.36 [95% CI, 1.04-1.76], P=0.02), and diabetes (OR, 2.07 [95% CI, 1.60-2.67], P≤0.0001) were associated with increased odds of HF. Physical activity was associated with lower odds (OR, 0.564 [95% CI, 0.38-0.836], P=0.004) of HF in Black individuals. CONCLUSIONS: Black individuals experienced HF at significantly younger ages, with traditional cardiometabolic factors (body mass index, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, diabetes) each independently being associated with HF risk. Physical activity appears protective, underscoring the importance of early, targeted prevention strategies.

recs.title: Identification of a Novel EBF1-Expressing Disease-Associated Arterial Subpopulation in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a debilitating disease with a poor prognosis. However, only a limited number of palliative interventions are currently available. To address this unmet need, it is essential to understand the molecular causes of PAH by identifying unique disease-associated populations and their key molecular regulators during disease progression. METHODS: We constructed a single-cell multiome data set at 4 distinct time points during the pathogenesis of pulmonary hypertension (PH) using endothelial cells isolated from the Sugen5416/hypoxia rat model. We assessed the conservation of novel disease-associated endothelial cells by reanalyzing previously reported single-cell RNA sequencing data from human patients with PAH. We validated the functional importance of EBF1 (early B-cell factor 1) in PAH by performing in silico simulations and an in vivo knockdown mediated by a pulmonary endothelium-targeting associated virus. RESULTS: We found that PH progression gradually altered the transcriptional and epigenetic landscape of the pulmonary endothelium in a stage-specific manner, leading to the emergence of a novel disease-associated arterial endothelial population expressing EBF1. A similar endothelial subset was present in human patients with PAH. Immunofluorescence revealed that EBF1 expression was elevated in both human and rat lungs during PH progression. In silico simulations suggested that EBF1 is required for the pathogenic state, and the associated virus-mediated in vivo knockdown of Ebf1 ameliorated the pathological hallmarks of PH, including right ventricular systolic pressure and right ventricular hypertrophy, when delivered either before the onset of PH or after its establishment. CONCLUSIONS: We identified EBF1 as a key transcriptional regulator of a novel disease-associated population in both humans and rats. We further demonstrated that inhibiting EBF1 within the pulmonary endothelium ameliorates the pathological features of PH, suggesting that EBF1 and its transcriptional targets represent a novel and promising therapeutic avenue for PAH.

recs.title: Low-grade inflammation and cardiovascular events among patients with chronic kidney disease.
recs.abstract: AIMS: Chronic inflammation is associated with cardiovascular disease in the general population, but data on patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) are limited. We sought to assess whether systemic low-grade inflammation is independently associated with cardiovascular events in CKD patients not yet on kidney replacement therapy, with or without a history of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD). METHODS: CKD-REIN is a prospective cohort study of adults with CKD stages 2-5, conducted in 40 French nephrology outpatient facilities. Baseline high-sensitivity plasma C-reactive protein (hs-CRP) was centrally measured using an immunoturbidimetric method. Systemic low-grade inflammation was defined as hs-CRP ≥2 mg/L. Cox proportional hazards models estimated cause-specific hazard ratios (HR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; composite of stroke, myocardial infarction, or cardiovascular death) or hospitalization for heart failure (HHF). RESULTS: We included 2078 patients: 67% men, mean (SD) age 67(13) years, mean eGFR 36(12) mL/min/1.73 m2, 38% with history of ASCVD, median hs-CRP concentration 2.4 mg/L (inter-quartile range 1.1-5.1). After median follow-up of 5 years, 171 patients had a MACE and 207 had HHF. After controlling for potential confounders, a twofold increase in hs-CRP was associated with a 12% (95% CI 0-26) higher cause-specific hazard of MACE and a 26% (95% CI 13-40) higher cause-specific hazard of HHF. CONCLUSION: In CKD patients not yet on kidney replacement therapy, systemic low-grade inflammation, measured through hs-CRP, is associated with occurrence of cardiovascular events independently of traditional risk factors, including a history of ASCVD.

recs.title: ICare-FASTER (Improving Care by Faster Risk Stratification Through Use of High-Sensitivity Point-of-Care Troponin in Patients Presenting With Possible Acute Coronary Syndrome in the Emergency Department): A Stepped-Wedge Cluster-Randomized Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Point-of-care high-sensitivity cTn (cardiac troponin; hs-cTn) testing has the potential to expedite decision-making and reduce emergency department (ED) length of stay for patients presenting with possible myocardial infarction by ensuring that results are consistently available when sought by clinicians. We assessed the real-life effectiveness and safety of implementing point-of-care hs-cTn testing in the ED. METHODS: We conducted a pragmatic, stepped-wedge cluster-randomized trial. The control arm was usual care with an accelerated diagnostic pathway using a single-sample rule-out step with a central laboratory hs-cTn assay. The intervention arm used the same pathway with a point-of-care hs-cTnI assay. The primary effectiveness outcome was ED length of stay assessed using a generalized linear mixed model. The safety outcome was myocardial infarction or cardiac death within 30 days. RESULTS: Six sites participated, with 59 980 ED presentations (44 747 individuals; mean 61±19 years of age; 49.5% female) from February 2023 through January 2025; 31 392 presentations were during the intervention arm. After adjustment for covariates associated with length of stay, the intervention reduced length of stay by 13% (95% CI, 9%-16%; P<0.001), corresponding to a reduction of 47 minutes (95% CI, 33-61 minutes) from a mean length of stay in the control arm of 376 minutes. The 30-day myocardial infarction or cardiac death rate was similar in the control and intervention arms (0.39% and 0.39%, respectively; P=0.54). CONCLUSIONS: Implementation of whole-blood hs-cTnI testing at the point of care into an accelerated diagnostic pathway was safe and reduced length of stay in the ED compared with laboratory testing. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.anzctr.org.au; Unique identifier: ACTRN12619001189112.

recs.title: Non-Invasive Stimulation of the Median Nerve: Neuromodulation to Reduce Atrial Arrhythmias in Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation (The Randomized BEAT-AF Pilot Study).
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Non-invasive low-level electrical stimulation of the median nerve favorably affects atrial electrophysiology and reduces inflammation. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether a novel wearable home-care neuromodulation device that performs median nerve stimulation (MNS) reduces atrial arrhythmias (AA) and related symptoms. METHODS: BEAT-AF was a randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled, 12-week pilot study. Patients with a paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF) burden of 0.5-25% on ambulatory 14-day ECG (aECG) monitoring were randomized 1:1 to either MNS or Sham, using a wristband-like neuromodulation and ECG monitoring device. RESULTS: Among 31 patients (n=15 MNS / n=16 Sham; age 67.3±9.7; 23 M / 8 F; CHA2DS2-VASc 2.6±1.7; median AF burden 4.9% [IQR 5.2%]),immediate pre-/post-treatment ECG recordings demonstrated a 35% reduction in premature atrial contraction (PAC) burden with MNS versus a 7% increase with Sham (p=0.039).Comparing baseline to 12-week 14-day ECGs, PAC burden was reduced by 26.5% (p=0.046) vs a numerical change of +3.94% (p=0.94; Sham, between group p=0.46), and the adjusted median AF burden numerically was reduced by 63% (MNS) vs 4.1% (Sham; p=0.42). By EHRA classification, symptomatology improved with MNS (0.45 vs 0.02 reduction in score; p=0.017), with a 26.3% shift from EHRA Class III to I with MNS) (vs Sham; p=0.048). CONCLUSIONS: In patients with paroxysmal AF, non-invasive median nerve stimulation reduced PAC burden and improved symptomatology; there was a numerical but non-significant reduction in AF burden. This pilot study sets the stage for future pivotal trials of MNS in AF patients.

recs.title: Plasma Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme as a Prioritized Candidate Target for Alzheimer's Disease: Evidence From Proteome-Wide Mendelian Randomization and a Large Prospective Cohort Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: We aimed to provide hypothesis-generating evidence on druggable targets for Alzheimer's disease (AD) by integrating proteome-wide Mendelian randomization (MR) with evidence from a conventional observational analysis of drug use in a large prospective cohort. METHODS: Proteome-wide MR analysis was conducted to identify plasma proteins causally related to AD risk using the largest summary-level data to date, followed by colocalization and multiomic validation analyses (on the gene expression, alternative splicing, and DNA methylation levels in blood and brain, respectively) to prioritize potential druggable targets. We also replicated our MR findings using additional genetic data and performed multivariable MR for the prioritized findings. Conventional observational analysis in UK Biobank, a large prospective cohort, was performed to provide further clinical implications, using active comparator to minimize confounding by indication. RESULTS: MR analysis identified 15 plasma proteins with putative causal effects on AD risk. Of them, inhibition of angiotensin-converting enzyme was found to increase the risk of AD (odds ratio, 1.10 [95% CI, 1.08-1.14]), which was likely independent of blood pressure as suggested by multivariable MR. Observational analysis in UK Biobank showed a higher incidence (hazard ratio, 1.23 [95% CI, 1.00-1.50]) of AD among regular users of angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors, compared with the active comparator angiotensin receptor blocker users. CONCLUSIONS: Our genetic analyses prioritized angiotensin-converting enzyme as a candidate target, and a conventional observational analysis in a large prospective cohort provided supportive evidence that regular angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor use was associated with a higher AD risk, which needs further investigation with high-quality real-world evidence and clinical trials before being translated into practice changes.

recs.title: Global Prevalence of Adherence to Antihypertensives and Associated Moderating Factors Among Adults With Hypertension: A Meta-Analysis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypertension is a significant public health issue affecting over a billion adults worldwide with adherence to antihypertensives being crucial for achieving sustained blood pressure control and reducing cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. To extend previous evidence, we conducted a meta-analysis on global prevalence of adherence to antihypertensives among adults. METHODS: A systematic search was conducted in Scopus, PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and CINAHL. Pooled prevalence of antihypertensive medication adherence was estimated using generalized linear mixed-effects model in R software version 4.4.3. Cochran's Q, τ2, and I2$$ {I}^2 $$ statistics examined statistical heterogeneity with moderator analysis exploring sources of heterogeneity. Sensitivity analysis was analyzed using exact fixed-effects model. RESULTS: A total of 123 studies with 1 052 445 adults with hypertension were included. Pooled global prevalence of adherence to antihypertensives was estimated at 58% (95% CI, 52%-63%), with 39% for high adherence, 29% for moderate adherence, and 35% for low adherence. Results for sensitivity analysis were 57.91% (95% CI, 57.81%-58.01%) with δ̂ being 24.3%. Prevalence across continents was 67% for Europe, 65% for South America, 60% for Africa, 56% for Asia, and 45% for North America. Adherence to antihypertensives was similar across low-income countries (61%), high-income countries (58), upper-middle-income countries (57%), and lower-middle-income countries (56%). In multivariate model, age and assessment tool only were significantly associated with medication adherence. CONCLUSIONS: Globally, a large proportion of adults with hypertension exhibit moderate to low adherence to antihypertensive medications. Future studies should prioritize establishing consensus-based operational definitions and cutoff values to enhance adherence.

recs.title: Depressive and Anxiety Symptoms in U.S. Adults With Type 1 Diabetes.
Effect of telemedicine-based integrated management of atrial fibrillation in village clinics on recurrent nonfatal cardiovascular events: a secondary analysis of the MIRACLE-AF trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is an increasing public health challenge, particularly among rural older adults, where awareness and treatment remain inadequate. While the MIRACLE-AF trial demonstrated that telemedicine-based, village doctor-led integrated care reduced cardiovascular mortality or first major cardiovascular events, its impact on recurrent nonfatal cardiovascular events remains unknown. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effect of the MIRACLE-AF care model on recurrent nonfatal cardiovascular events. METHODS: We conducted a secondary analysis of the MIRACLE-AF trial (NCT04622514), a cluster-randomized controlled trial enrolling 1,039 rural patients aged ≥65 years with confirmed AF across 30 village clinics over 36 months. Village clinics were randomized 1:1 to village doctor-led telemedicine integrated care or enhanced usual care. The primary outcome was recurrent nonfatal events over 36 months, including strokes, hospitalizations for worsening heart failure or acute coronary syndrome, and emergency visits for AF, analyzed using a conditional frailty model. RESULTS: Among 1039 patients (mean age 75.8 ± 5.7 years; 44.3% female), the intervention experienced fewer cardiovascular events than the control (118 events in 82 patients [15.65%] vs. 173 events in 122 patients [23.69%]). The observed recurrent event rates were 6.75 and 9.11 per 100 patient-years, respectively. The estimated hazard ratio was 0.76 (95% CI, 0.583-1.004; p = 0.053), indicating that the difference did not reach statistical significance. CONCLUSION: Although the overall difference did not reach statistical significance, directional trends consistently favored telemedicine-based integrated care, suggesting a potential reduction in recurrent cardiovascular event burden. Larger studies with longer follow-up are needed to confirm these findings.

recs.title: Concomitant Balloon-in-Basket Pulsed Field Ablation and Next-Generation Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion: Acute Procedural Success and Early Safety and Effectiveness results from the Prospective Multicenter CLEAR Study.
Maximising the prognostic value of non-contrast cardiac CT.
Unipolar Electrograms at the Pulmonary Vein Antrum: Spatial and Directional Heterogeneity with Distinct Postablation Morphologies.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Disappearance of the near-field S-wave in the unipolar electrogram (U-EGM) is commonly used to assess lesion formation during pulmonary vein (PV) isolation; however, interpretation of U-EGMs in anatomically complex atrial regions remains uncertain. OBJECTIVE: We aimed to characterize spatial, directional, and postablation changes in antral PV U-EGMs, and evaluate the limitations of conventional waveform interpretation. METHODS: In 15 patients undergoing radiofrequency ablation for atrial fibrillation, U-EGMs were recorded at 116 antral PV sites during sinus rhythm and distal coronary sinus (CS) pacing before and after ablation. U-EGM morphology and R- and S-wave amplitudes were analyzed. RESULTS: Baseline U-EGMs showed spatial heterogeneity, with a small r and deep S in the right anterior PV antrum transitioning to a positive-dominant morphology (Rs) in the left-lower PV antra. Distal CS pacing altered the activation sequence, causing direction-dependent changes, most prominently in the right PV antrum. After ablation, overall S-wave amplitude decreased from -0.94 ± 0.70 to -0.08 ± 0.55 mV (P<0.001). Residual negative deflections ≥0.5 mV persisted in 18.1% (21/116) of recordings, frequently in association with direction-dependent far-field activity. Newly developed positive deflections ≥1.0 mV were observed in 17/116 sites (14.7%; mean 1.42 ± 0.42 mV), predominantly in the right-sided antra. CONCLUSIONS: Antral PV U-EGMs frequently represent composites of near- and far-field signals with spatial heterogeneity and direction-dependent variation. Postablation responses are diverse, including S-wave disappearance, residual negativity, often reflecting contributions from overlapping far-field components, and newly developed positive deflections. PV-antral U-EGMs should be interpreted in the context of their composite nature.

recs.title: As conflict and the climate emergency converge, we must put women, children, and adolescents at the heart of integrated action.
Pacing Related Conduction Delay as an Indicator of Intramural Site of Origin of Focal Ventricular Arrhythmias.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The diagnosis of intramural focal ventricular arrhythmias (VA) can be challenging and is often made in retrospect after a long ineffective procedure. OBJECTIVES: In this cohort of patients, we aim to assess the value of pace-mapping (PM), stimulus-QRS interval (S-QRS interval), and electrogram (EGM)-QRS intervals to identify the site of origin (SOO) of focal VAs. METHODS: In a consecutive series of 46 patients with frequent premature ventricular complexes (PVCs), activation mapping and PM were performed to identify VA target sites. VA target sites were defined as sites with matching PM (≥10/12 leads) and/or sites with the earliest activation time. S-QRS interval and bipolar activation time at target sites were assessed and correlated with acute outcomes. If ablation at a target site failed, alternative sites were sought in adjacent anatomical structures. An intramural origin was defined as a VA with early activation time without a matching PM. RESULTS: Matching PMs were identified for 32 VAs in 30 of the 46 patients. Receiver operating characteristic analysis was performed at the target site/PVC level and demonstrated that a mismatch between S-QRS and EGM-QRS of >26 milliseconds distinguished effective from ineffective ablation sites with a matching PM (area under the curve: 0.98; 95% CI: 0.94-1; sensitivity: 100%; specificity: 88.9%). A mismatch was present in 9 patients, and radiofrequency ablation failed in 8/9 of them. Alternate sites with early activation times (-48.4 ± 37.39 milliseconds) without matching PM, where radiofrequency eliminated the PVCs, were identified in 5/8 patients. CONCLUSIONS: Conduction delay with matching PMs but late activation indicates a deeper SOO. A cutoff value of >26 milliseconds between S-QRS and EGM-QRS intervals identified deeper-seated VA target sites. This required further mapping to identify alternative ablation sites. A matching PM may not always be indicative of the SOO in patients with PVCs.

recs.title: Nuclear Factor Kappa-B Inducing Kinase- and Inhibitor of Nuclear Factor Kappa-B Kinase Subunit Beta-Binding Protein Promotes Pathological Cardiac Hypertrophy by Regulating Inhibitor of Nuclear Factor Kappa-B Kinase Subunit Beta-Mediated Nuclear Factor Kappa-B Activation.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pathological cardiac hypertrophy is a major risk factor for heart failure. NIBP (NF-κB [nuclear factor kappa-B] inducing kinase- and inhibitor of NF-κB kinase subunit beta-binding protein) is a key regulator of cytokine-induced NF-κB signaling, but its role in cardiac hypertrophy remains unknown. METHODS: We established transverse aortic constriction-induced cardiac hypertrophy in mice and phenylephrine-induced hypertrophy in neonatal rat ventricular myocytes. Genetic interventions included generation of whole-body Nibp knockout mice via CRISPR-Cas9; creation of cardiomyocyte-specific Nibp knockout mice using adeno-associated virus serotype 9-delivered Cre and single-guide RNAs in Rosa26-LSL-Cas9 mice; and cardiac-specific Nibp overexpression via adeno-associated virus serotype 9delivery. In neonatal rat ventricular myocytes, NIBP was knocked down or overexpressed using adenoviruses. Phenotypes were assessed by echocardiography, histology (wheat germ agglutinin, picrosirius redstaining), and molecular analyses. Mechanisms were investigated via RNA-sequencing, coimmunoprecipitation, and Western blotting for key signaling molecules. RESULTS: NIBP protein was upregulated in hypertrophic hearts and cardiomyocytes. Both Nibp-knockout and cardiomyocyte-specific Nibp knockout attenuated transverse aortic constriction-induced cardiac dysfunction, hypertrophy, and fibrosis, whereas Nibp overexpression exacerbated these pathologies. Consistently, in neonatal rat ventricular myocytes, NIBP knockdown mitigated, while its overexpression aggravated, phenylephrine-induced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and inflammatory responses. Mechanistically, NIBP directly interacted with IKKβ (inhibitor of NF-κB kinase subunit beta), enhanced its phosphorylation, and drove hyperactivation of the downstream NF-κB pathway. Overexpression of a kinase-dead IKKβ mutant reversed the hypertrophic effects of NIBP. CONCLUSIONS: NIBP promotes pathological cardiac hypertrophy by activating the IKKβ/NF-κB axis, identifying it as a potential therapeutic target for cardiac remodeling and heart failure.

recs.title: Dapagliflozin After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation According to Frailty in DapaTAVI Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Frailty is common in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation and portends worse outcomes. Whether the benefit of posttranscatheter aortic valve implantation dapagliflozin differs by frailty is uncertain. METHODS: In this post hoc analysis, we investigated the efficacy of dapagliflozin according to frailty status in the DapaTAVI (Dapagliflozin in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation) trial. Frailty was assessed through the Fatigue, Resistance, Ambulation, Illnesses, and Loss of Weight scale (robust=0, prefrail=1-2, frail=3-5). The primary outcome was the composite of all-cause death or worsening heart failure at 1 year. RESULTS: Among 1222 patients with baseline frailty assessment, 47.2% were frail, 40.3% prefrail, and 12.4% robust. Over 12 months, 215 patients (17.6%) experienced the primary end point. Patients who were prefrail and frail had higher risk than robust patients (adjusted hazard ratios [HRs], 1.88 [95% CI, 1.05-3.38] and 2.29 [1.29-4.07], respectively; P=0.004). Dapagliflozin was associated with a lower risk of the primary end point in patients who were frail (HR, 0.53 [95% CI, 0.36-0.77]) but not in those who were prefrail (HR, 1.01 [95% CI, 0.66-1.55]) or robust patients (HR, 1.26 [95% CI, 0.42-3.75]); P for interaction=0.021. There was no evidence that frailty modified the safety profile of dapagliflozin. CONCLUSIONS: Frailty was common and independently associated with worse outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation. Dapagliflozin appeared to confer greater relative benefit in patients with frailty.

recs.title: Impact of surgical timing in left-sided infective endocarditis with persistently positive blood cultures.
recs.abstract: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Guidelines define persistent infection in infective endocarditis (IE) as positive blood cultures after 7 days of adequate antibiotic therapy. However, persistently positive blood cultures (PPBC) at 48 to 72 hours are already associated with a worse prognosis. We aimed to assess the clinical profile, temporal trends, and impact of surgical timing on outcomes in patients with left-sided IE and PPBC at 48 to 72 hours. METHODS: We performed a retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data from 3 Spanish tertiary centers (1998-2024). We compared patients with PPBC with those with blood culture clearance and assessed the effect of surgical timing using a time-dependent Cox model, inverse-probability-of-treatment weighting, and a day-7 landmark analysis to minimize immortal time bias and confounding by indication. RESULTS: Among 1265 patients with positive baseline cultures, 283 (22.4%) had PPBC at 48 to 72 hours. These patients exhibited a more severe clinical and microbiological profile and higher in-hospital mortality (36.0% vs 22.3%; P < .001). In the day-7 landmark analysis, surgery within the first 7 days was associated with lower in-hospital mortality (HR, 0.53; 95%CI, 0.30-0.95), with consistent trends across the time-dependent Cox and inverse-probability-of-treatment weighting models. CONCLUSIONS: PPBC at 48 to 72 hours identifies a high-risk subgroup of patients with left-sided IE. In these patients, early surgery within the first 7 days was associated with a potential survival benefit in adjusted models, supporting earlier reassessment of infection control to optimize surgical timing.

recs.title: Individualized Cardiac Index-Guided Hemodynamic Therapy in High-Risk Patients Undergoing Elective Major Abdominal Surgery: Research Summary.
A Novel Method for Assessing Left Bundle Branch Capture Using the Bidirectional Conduction Time Difference Between Left Bundle Branch Area Pacing and Coronary Sinus Leads.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) is an established conduction system pacing strategy; however, confirming left bundle branch (LBB) capture remains challenging. OBJECTIVE: We propose a novel method for LBB capture confirmation based on the bidirectional conduction time difference between the LBBAP and coronary sinus (CS) leads. METHODS: This observational study included 60 patients undergoing de novo left bundle branch-optimized cardiac resynchronization therapy. LBB capture was defined by (1) paced QRS transition, (2) LBB potential with current of injury, or (3) ΔV6 R-wave peak time ≥10 ms. LBBAP-to-CS and CS-to-LBBAP conduction times were measured. ΔLBB-CS ([CS-to-LBBAP] - [LBBAP-to-CS]) was compared between nonselective LBB pacing (NS-LBBP) and left ventricular septal pacing (LVSP). RESULTS: Among 60 patients (74.7±10.4 years; 42 men), 25 had left bundle branch block and 17 had non-specific intraventricular conduction delay. LBB capture was confirmed in 45 patients (75.0%). LBBAP-to-CS was 114.3±28.0 ms during NS-LBBP (n=43) and 134.2±19.0 ms during LVSP (n=29), whereas CS-to-LBBAP was 143.4±28.5 ms (n=60). ΔLBB-CS was greater during NS-LBBP than LVSP (27.5±9.9 vs. 7.9±7.4 ms, P<0.01). Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis identified a 21.5 ms cutoff for LBB capture (74.4% sensitivity; 100% specificity; area under curve [AUC] 0.95). In patients with baseline LBBB (n=25), a 20.5 ms cutoff for LBB capture yielded 92.9% sensitivity, 100% specificity, and an AUC of 0.99. CONCLUSION: ΔLBB-CS ≥ 21.5ms may serve as a novel adjunctive marker of LBB capture during LOT-CRT, with greater diagnostic accuracy at a 20.5 ms cutoff in patients with baseline LBBB.

recs.title: Thioredoxin-Interacting Protein-Regulated in Development and DNA Damage-Response 1-Driven Macrophage Senescence Promotes Hypoxia-Induced Pulmonary Hypertension.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a life-threatening vascular disorder characterized by pulmonary arterial remodeling and right ventricular failure, posing a significant clinical challenge. Although macrophage dysfunction is implicated in PH pathogenesis, its underlying molecular mechanisms remain elusive. METHODS: We employed multiomics database analysis, cross-species validation, and functional studies in hypoxia-induced PH models. Myeloid-specific Txnip deletion was achieved via bone marrow transplantation in mice. Mechanistic insights were evaluated through protein-binding assays, cellular senescence analyses in bone marrow-derived macrophages, and co-culture experiments with pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells. RESULTS: We identified that cellular senescence in pulmonary adventitial macrophages was involved in the pathogenesis of hypoxia-induced PH. Integrated multiomics analysis revealed elevated TXNIP (thioredoxin-interacting protein) expression in perivascular macrophages during hypoxia-induced PH. Myeloid-specific Txnip deletion attenuated hypoxia-induced pulmonary vascular remodeling in mice. Mechanistically, TXNIP binds to and stabilizes the REDD1 (regulated in development and DNA damage-response 1) protein, promoting hypoxia-induced senescence in bone marrow-derived macrophages. Conditioned medium from senescent macrophages subsequently enhanced the proliferation and migration of pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells. CONCLUSIONS: The TXNIP-REDD1 axis drives hypoxia-induced macrophage senescence, which promotes pulmonary artery smooth muscle cell dysfunction and pulmonary vascular remodeling in hypoxia-induced PH. Targeting the TXNIP-REDD1 pathway may provide a novel therapeutic strategy for hypoxia-induced PH.

recs.title: Assessment and Reversibility of Hepatic Abnormalities in Heart Failure: Liver in Heart Failure.
recs.abstract: Hepatic abnormalities in non-Fontan heart failure result from congestive hepatopathy and hypoperfusion-related ischemic injury, compounded by neurohormonal activation and systemic inflammation. Assessment of liver disease severity is challenging because standard liver biochemistries, serum fibrosis markers, severity score models, elastography, and imaging modalities have limited diagnostic accuracy in congestive hepatopathy, and hepatic fibrosis is often heterogeneous on histology in this population. Management focuses on optimization of cardiac function through medical therapy or mechanical circulatory support. Although liver biochemical abnormalities frequently improve with restoration of cardiac function, histologic reversibility is variable and not consistently observed. In patients with advanced heart failure needing heart transplantation, histologic cirrhosis and/or fibrosis accompanied by portal hypertension may merit consideration of combined heart-liver transplantation, but correlation between fibrosis and clinical outcomes varies. There remains an unmet need for tests that can reliably assess liver disease severity and predict liver outcomes in non-Fontan congestive hepatopathy.

recs.title: Feasibility and results of the implementation of a post-discharge coordination circuit for patients with acute heart failure from the emergency department.
Greenspace visitation and risk of major adverse cardiovascular events: evidence from the Houston methodist cardiovascular learning health system registry.
recs.abstract: AIMS: To evaluate whether mobility-derived greenspace visitation, as a behavioural measure of environmental exposure, is associated with major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) independent of individual and neighbourhood factors. METHODS AND RESULTS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults in the Houston Methodist Cardiovascular Disease Learning Health System Registry (2016-2023). Greenspace visitation was defined at the census-tract level using mobility-derived foot-traffic data and modelled as annual visits per resident device. The primary outcome was incident MACE (myocardial infarction, stroke, coronary revascularization, and all-cause mortality). The Cox models, restricted cubic splines, and Kaplan-Meier curves assessed associations with sequential adjustment for demographics, comorbidities, smoking, and neighbourhood social vulnerability. Among 1 088 866 adults without baseline atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, median (SD) age was 49 (17.6) years, and 59.9% were female. Greenspace visitation varied across neighbourhoods and by demographic and socioeconomic characteristics. Each additional 10 annual visits was associated with lower MACE risk in unadjusted models [hazard ratio (HR) 0.82; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.81-0.83] and after adjustment for demographics, comorbidities, and smoking (HR 0.89; 95% CI: 0.88-0.91). A non-linear relationship showed risk reductions at low-to-moderate visitation, plateauing at 10-15 visits annually. After adjusting for social vulnerability, associations were attenuated and no longer significant. The Kaplan-Meier curves showed higher event-free survival in high-visitation areas, consistent across MACE components. CONCLUSION: Mobility-derived greenspace visitation is associated with lower cardiovascular risk. These findings highlight greenspace engagement as a potentially modifiable behavioural exposure and support strategies to enhance access and utilization of greenspaces for cardiovascular prevention.

Precision medicine for pediatric cardiomyopathy: lessons from pediatric oncology.
Workforce Culture and Engagement: Evolving the American College of Cardiology's Approach to Professional Excellence in Cardiovascular Medicine.
Pulmonary Vein Isolation With Contact-Force-Sensing Large-Tip Focal Pulsed Field Ablation Catheter With 3D Mapping for Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation: Omny-IRE 12-month Results.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Omny-IRE (NCT05971693) evaluated safety and effectiveness of a large-tip focal, multielectrode, contact-force-sensing, pulsed field ablation, basket catheter with electroanatomic mapping integration. OBJECTIVE: Report 12-month (M) study outcomes. METHODS: Pulmonary vein isolation was performed using the OMNYPULSE platform. Patients underwent follow-up through 12M postablation visit with electrocardiography (preprocedure, predischarge, and at 1, 3, 6, and 12M), 24-hour Holter monitoring (3, 6, and 12M), and remote rhythm monitoring (weekly: 1-5M; monthly: 6-12M; and symptom-triggered recordings). The secondary effectiveness endpoint was 12M freedom from documented symptomatic/asymptomatic atrial arrhythmia (≥30 s) and acute procedural failure. Device/procedure-related serious adverse events (SAEs), quality-of-life assessed by Atrial Fibrillation Effect on Quality-of-Life (AFEQT) scores, and healthcare-utilization (cardiovascular-hospitalizations and antiarrhythmic drug [AAD] use) were also evaluated. RESULTS: Among 188 enrolled patients, 136 comprised the main-phase-cohort for safety and effectiveness evaluations. In this cohort, 12M freedom from symptomatic/asymptomatic atrial arrhythmia was 82.5% (90.1% using standard-of-care monitoring only). Clinical success, defined as freedom from documented symptomatic arrhythmia and acute procedural failure, was 89.9%, while single procedural success was 89.2%. Device/procedure-related SAEs occurred in 2.9% of main-phase patients. Mean overall AFEQT score improved by 25.5 points from baseline to 12M. Cardiovascular-hospitalizations decreased by 40.9% versus the 12M preprocedure period, and Class I/III AAD use decreased by 49.3% 6-12M postablation versus baseline. CONCLUSIONS: Omny-IRE results demonstrated the effectiveness, safety, and healthcare benefits of PFA with the OMNYPULSE platform.

recs.title: Diagnosis and Treatment of Cardiovascular Conditions in Medicare Advantage In-Home Health Risk Assessments.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Medicare Advantage insurers conduct in-home health risk assessments (HRAs) to identify high-risk patients and facilitate appropriate care. Critics argue this practice increases risk-adjusted payments without improving quality. Comprehensive data on use of in-home HRAs and downstream treatment are lacking. OBJECTIVE: To examine trends in cardiovascular conditions diagnosed during in-home HRAs, characteristics associated with HRA-based diagnoses, and treatment rates after diagnoses. DESIGN: Cohort study. SETTING: Population-based. PARTICIPANTS: Medicare Advantage beneficiaries. MEASUREMENTS: Using 100% Medicare claims, trends in the proportion of cardiovascular conditions diagnosed during in-home HRAs (vs. facility-based visits) were examined. Multivariable logistic regression models were fit to estimate the association between beneficiary- and plan-level characteristics and HRA-based diagnoses and compare treatment rates across settings. RESULTS: Among 21 496 506 Medicare Advantage beneficiaries diagnosed with a cardiovascular risk factor or disease, the proportion diagnosed during in-home HRAs increased between 2018 and 2022 for hypertension (45.9% to 47.7%), hyperlipidemia (57.8% to 66.7%), diabetes (47.8% to 51.6%), atrial fibrillation (30.0% to 36.0%), ischemic heart disease (37.2% to 41.6%), peripheral vascular disease (64.5% to 73.9%), and heart failure (34.7% to 42.6%). Racial and ethnic minority beneficiaries and those enrolled in lower-rated plans were more likely to receive HRA-based diagnoses. Treatment rates were substantially lower after HRA-based diagnoses across all conditions. LIMITATIONS: Differences in the severity of conditions between groups could not be assessed. Prescription fills were used as a proxy for management. Observed differences in the diagnosis and treatment of conditions across encounter settings may be susceptible to unmeasured confounding. CONCLUSION: Among Medicare Advantage beneficiaries, an increasingly large share of cardiovascular conditions are being diagnosed through in-home HRAs, but treatment rates after these diagnoses are consistently lower than after facility-based encounters. PRIMARY FUNDING SOURCE: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute.

recs.title: Effect of Obicetrapib on Glycaemia and New-Onset Diabetes: Pooled Analysis of BROADWAY/BROOKLYN and an Updated Meta-analysis of CETP Inhibitor Trials.
recs.abstract: AIMS: New-onset diabetes (NoD) is a recognised effect of statin therapy potentially influencing acceptance of intensive LDL-C-lowering. In contrast, cholesteryl ester transfer protein (CETP) inhibition has been associated with lower NoD risk in earlier trials. We assessed the effect of the highly selective CETP inhibitor obicetrapib on glycaemia and NoD, contextualised within an updated meta-analysis of CETP inhibitor trials. METHODS: Individual participant data from the phase 3 BROADWAY and BROOKLYN trials were pooled across 1,700 participants without diabetes at baseline (899 normoglycaemic, 801 prediabetes; 38.8% women), randomised 2:1 to obicetrapib 10 mg or placebo for 52 weeks. The PRISMA-compliant, PROSPERO-registered systematic review identified six eligible trials reporting NoD. Pooled risk ratios were calculated using Mantel-Haenszel fixed-effect models, with prespecified subgroup analyses by baseline glycaemic status and CETPi potency, and trial-level meta-regression. RESULTS: Obicetrapib did not increase HbA1c at week 52 vs placebo (LSMD -0.02%, 95% CI -0.04 to 0.00). NoD occurred in 6.4% (obicetrapib) versus 8.5% (placebo) (adjusted OR 0.69, 95% CI 0.47-1.03), directionally consistent across glycaemic strata. Restricted cubic spline analyses identified associations between HDL-C, apoA1 and Lp(a) changes and NoD risk, but not HbA1c change. In the meta-analysis, CETP inhibition was associated with a 16% lower risk of NoD (RR 0.84, 95% CI 0.79-0.90; I2 = 0%). CONCLUSIONS: Obicetrapib did not adversely affect glycaemia and was associated with a numerically lower risk of NoD, consistent with a CETP inhibitor class signal of a modestly lower risk. The PREVAIL trial will provide larger-longer evidence about obicetrapib and NoD.

recs.title: Sirolimus-Coated Balloon Angioplasty for Femoropopliteal Artery Disease Without Tissue Loss: A Secondary Analysis of the SirPAD Trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Whether sirolimus-coated balloon angioplasty performs better than uncoated balloon angioplasty among patients with exertional symptoms due to femoropopliteal artery disease remains uncertain. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to describe 1-year outcomes after sirolimus-coated balloon angioplasty among participants in the SirPAD (Sirolimus-Coated Balloon for Peripheral Artery Disease) trial with femoropopliteal artery disease. METHODS: In this analysis of the multicenter, randomized, blinded-endpoint SirPAD trial, we evaluated outcomes for patients with femoropopliteal target lesions and without tissue loss (Rutherford category ≤4, Fontaine stage ≤III). A secondary subgroup was restricted to patients with a lower disease burden, excluding ischemic rest pain, prior major amputation, or below-the-knee revascularization. We compared the 1-year rate of: 1) target-lesion revascularization (TLR); 2) the composite of TLR and any unplanned amputation; 3) major adverse limb events; and 4) all-cause death. RESULTS: Among 597 patients, median age was 71 years, 34.7% were women, and median target-lesion length was 150 mm; 53.8% had total occlusion. After 1 year, 50 patients (17.0%) had undergone TLR in the sirolimus-coated balloon group vs 82 (27.1%) among control subjects (absolute risk difference [ARD]: -10.1%; 95% CI: -16.6 to -3.0). Any amputation or any TLR occurred in 17.7% and 27.1% of patients respectively (ARD: -9.4%; 95% CI: -16.0 to -2.7). Major adverse limb events occurred in 4.1% vs 8.9% of patients, respectively (ARD: -4.8%; 95% CI: -9.0 to -0.8). One-year all-cause death was similar (3.7% vs 5.3%). CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with femoropopliteal artery disease and no tissue loss, sirolimus-coated balloon angioplasty was associated with a lower 1-year rate of TLR compared with uncoated balloon angioplasty. These findings are descriptive rather than confirmatory. (Sirolimus-Coated Balloon for Peripheral Artery Disease; NCT04238546).

recs.title: First use of empagliflozin to treat a patient with congenital long QT syndrome type III.
From Marker of Risk to Marker of Response: Using Biomarkers to Guide Heart Failure Rehabilitation.
Atrial Septostomy and Left Ventricular Venting During Peripheral VA-ECMO.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Peripheral venoarterial (VA)-extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) increases left ventricular (LV) afterload, and therefore the risk of LV distension, pulmonary edema, and cardiac stasis. Balloon atrial septostomy (BAS) provides atrial-level unloading, but the durability of LV venting remains uncertain. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the clinical effectiveness of BAS for LV venting in patients requiring peripheral VA-ECMO for cardiogenic shock (CS). METHODS: The authors conducted a retrospective study of consecutive adults with CS supported with peripheral VA-ECMO who underwent BAS for LV unloading at an academic center (2019-2024). The primary endpoint was LV venting failure, a composite of pulmonary edema, LV distension, spontaneous echocardiographic contrast, LV or aortic root thrombus, stroke due to ECMO, or escalation to additional mechanical support. RESULTS: A total of 28 patients were included in the study. BAS resulted in a significant reduction in mean left atrial pressure (20.5-13.5 mm Hg; P < 0.001). Durable LV venting was achieved in a subset of patients; however, LV venting failure occurred in 53.6%, driven primarily by pulmonary edema. Pulse-pressure trajectories differed according to eventual LV venting-failure status (interaction P = 0.018). Model-estimated pulse pressure was higher at 48 hours (P = 0.010) and 72 hours (P = 0.031) among patients who ultimately did not experience venting failure. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients receiving peripheral VA-ECMO for CS, BAS achieves atrial-level decompression and may provide durable LV venting in select patients, although venting failure remains common. Observed arterial pulse-pressure trajectories differed according to eventual LV venting failure status.

recs.title: Temporal Dynamics of Complement Activation and Outcome in Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Immune-mediated inflammatory responses exacerbate brain injury and affect the prognosis in acute ischemic stroke. METHODS: We characterized longitudinal complement activation after acute ischemic stroke using serial plasma samples from 10 patients and 8 controls. Initial markers of classical (C1q), lectin (mannose-binding lectin), and alternative (complement factor Bb) pathways, as well as regulatory (complement factor H) and downstream markers (C3a, C5a, and C5b-9) were measured by ELISA at 9 time points. RESULTS: Patients with stroke showed broad complement activation, with increased C1q, mannose-binding lectin, complement factor Bb, C3a, C5a, and C5b-9, and reduced complement factor H compared with controls. Complement components showed distinct temporal patterns during follow-up. Complement factor Bb levels were lower in patients with unfavorable functional outcome and in those with moderate-to-severe stroke. C1q and C3a trajectories differed according to functional outcome, whereas C3a trajectories also differed according to stroke severity. C1q trajectories differed according to age group and infarct volume. CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest dynamic, pathway-specific complement activation after acute ischemic stroke and highlight the need for larger studies to clarify its prognostic and therapeutic relevance.

recs.title: Safety considerations and clinical monitoring during pulsed field ablation.
recs.abstract: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) has emerged as a transformative technology in cardiac electrophysiology, offering a potentially superior safety profile compared with thermal ablation due to its non-thermal mechanism of irreversible electroporation. Clinical experience confirms a substantial reduction in traditional complications such as pulmonary vein stenosis, atrio-oesophageal fistula, and permanent phrenic nerve injury, though PFA introduces a distinct spectrum of physiologic effects requiring consideration. Coronary vasospasm is the most characteristic phenomenon, ranging from transient, subclinical constriction to rare ischaemic or arrhythmic events; mitigation relies on coronary anatomical awareness, optimized lesion placement, and prophylactic vasodilators. Haemolysis, caused by red blood cell electroporation, varies with catheter design and pulse burden and is typically mild, though high exposure and inadequate hydration may rarely lead to acute kidney injury. Silent cerebral lesions could result from procedural and/or energy-related factors, including gas formation, air ingress, catheter manipulation, and anticoagulation management, with uncertain long-term clinical impact but opportunities for technique-driven reduction. Interactions between PFA and cardiac implantable electronic devices are system- and context-dependent, with monopolar configurations and catheter-lead proximity influencing the risk of transient interference and rare permanent damage.

recs.title: Shared Genetic Architecture Between Mental Disorders and Heart Failure Subtypes: A Comprehensive Multitrait Genome-Wide Analysis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Mental disorders and heart failure frequently co-occur, but their shared genetic architecture remains incompletely understood. METHODS: Prospective Cox regression analysis in the UK Biobank (UKB) quantified the risk of incident heart failure associated with mental disorders. Linkage disequilibrium score regression estimated genetic correlations, while multitrait genome-wide association and cross-phenotype association analyses identified candidate pleiotropic loci. Statistical fine mapping and gene-level association analyses prioritized candidate variants and genes. Bayesian colocalization assessed evidence for shared candidate variants, and exploratory Gene Ontology biological-process overrepresentation analysis provided descriptive biological context. Single-cell RNA sequencing and genetically informed spatial mapping (gsMap) provided cellular and spatial context for prioritized genes. Geneformer-based in silico perturbation analysis was performed using a cardiac cell atlas of dilated cardiomyopathy to prioritize candidate pleiotropic genes and identify cardiac cell states showing predicted embedding shifts. RESULTS: Prospective UKB analyses demonstrated that mental disorders, such as posttraumatic stress disorder, depression, and bipolar disorder, were associated with a higher risk of incident heart failure. Multitrait analysis identified 607 pleiotropic variants, with fine-mapping and colocalization converging on prioritized candidate loci, including TMEM18, NKX2-2, and XRN2. Single-cell expression profiling and spatial mapping provided context at the cellular and tissue levels for the prioritized genes. Geneformer-based in silico perturbation prioritized FOXP1 and TMEM106B as leading pleiotropic candidate genes on the basis of their predicted changes in downstream gene embeddings in cardiac cellular contexts. CONCLUSIONS: This study identifies shared genetic architecture between mental disorders and heart failure and prioritizes candidate pleiotropic genes associated with both. Transcriptomic and in silico perturbation analyses provide exploratory cellular, spatial, and cardiac functional context. Functional validation is required before mechanistic or therapeutic interpretation.

Refining Care Pathways for MINOCA: Lessons from the DOMINO Registry.

Cardiomyocyte-expressed TGFβ programs early heart maturation and adult myocyte identity.
recs.abstract: Transforming growth factor β (TGFβ) is a secreted factor sequestered in the extracellular matrix (ECM), but its role in developing mouse heart maturation is unknown. Here we show that cardiomyocyte-specific deletion of Tgfb1, Tgfb2 and Tgfb3 genes (TGFβ ligands) in the developing heart results in cardiac dysfunction by 6 weeks of age, altered fibroblast activity, abnormal ECM properties and endothelial and immune changes. Gene profiling reveals defective cardiomyocyte/fibroblast maturation with cardiomyocyte ectopic skeletal muscle gene expression beginning at embryonic day 17.5 (E17.5). Cardiomyocyte deletion of Tgfbr1/Tgfbr2 or Smad2/Smad3 does not phenocopy Tgfb1/2/3 deletion, suggesting that cardiomyocyte TGFβ acts through non-myocytes to regulate heart maturation. Similarly, Col1a2-/-;Col6a2-/- mice with reduced ECM stiffness, cardiomyocyte-specific Itgb1 deletion reducing ECM mechanosensing and Tcf21-/- embryos lacking cardiac fibroblasts fail to reproduce ectopic skeletal muscle gene expression. Thus, embryonic cardiomyocyte-derived TGFβ signals to non-myocytes to establish an environment that directs cardiomyocyte maturation and identity.

recs.title: The Vein of Marshall Promotes Re-Entry After Pulmonary Vein Reconnection.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Postablation re-entrant atrial tachycardia recurrence remains a major limitation of atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation. Pulmonary vein (PV) reconnection and epicardial connections from the left atrium (LA) to the vein of Marshall (VoM) and coronary sinus (CS) in proximity to mitral valve are important contributors. We hypothesized that VoM facilitates arrhythmia induction through interaction with the epicardial region encircled by wide antral circumferential ablation (WACA). OBJECTIVES: The objective of this study was to systematically evaluate the combined effect of PV reconnection and epicardial VoM connectivity on the occurrence of sustained postablation re-entrant atrial tachycardia using in silico models. METHODS: Bilayer biatrial models were constructed from electroanatomical and computed tomographic data of 10 patients with AF. Post-AF electrical remodeling and substrate remodeling following the low voltage area distribution, and left-sided WACA were incorporated. Segments of WACA lesions were sequentially restored to simulate PV reconnection. Three connectivity scenarios were evaluated: intact CS-VoM-LA epicardial connection, CS-LA connection only, and no epicardial connections. Sustained re-entry (>10 seconds) was the primary endpoint, and connectivity conditions were compared using patient-level paired vulnerability. Induction of any arrhythmia, tachycardia cycle length, and stable rotor number were secondary outcomes. RESULTS: Sustained re-entry occurred at 92 of 294 (31.3%) reconnection sites with intact CS-VoM-LA connectivity, 37 of 294 (12.6%) with CS-LA connectivity only, and 29 of 294 (9.9%) without epicardial connectivity. Patient-level paired analysis showed 19.9-percentage-point and 22.7-percentage-point higher vulnerability with intact CS-VoM-LA connectivity compared with CS-LA connectivity alone (95% CI: 7.1-37.3 percentage points) and no epicardial connectivity (95% CI: 7.4-41.3 percentage points), respectively. Mean tachycardia cycle length in the LA was 258.0 ± 25.7 milliseconds, 255.0 ± 31.4 milliseconds, and 251.0 ± 33.9 milliseconds across the 3 scenarios; the average number of stable rotors was 0.6 ± 0.3, 0.7 ± 0.2, and 0.4 ± 0.2, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: The VoM is a critical epicardial driver of arrhythmia after incomplete WACA, underscoring the importance of its targeted ablation.

recs.title: Don't Blink!-Time for "Instant" PFA?
Correction to: Use and Cost Patterns of Antihypertensive Medications in the United States From 1996 to 2021.
Deep learning-enabled assessment of right ventricular size and function is associated with cardiovascular outcomes.
recs.abstract: Right ventricular (RV) size and function inform prognosis in many cardiovascular diseases, but assessment by two-dimensional transthoracic echocardiography is challenging. Here we show that a deep learning model, Dimensional Reconstruction of Imaging Data-Right Ventricle (DROID-RV), can estimate RV end-diastolic diameter and identify RV systolic dysfunction from transthoracic echocardiography videos. We trained DROID-RV in 17,141 ambulatory cardiology patients (51,188 studies and 383,881 video clips) and validated model predictions in 9,112 primary care patients and 831 patients with RV ejection fraction assessed by three-dimensional transthoracic echocardiography. Across multiple test samples, DROID-RV accurately estimates RV end-diastolic diameter and identifies RV dysfunction, although model prediction error increases at extremes of RV size and function. We additionally show that RV size and function predictions are associated with incident mortality, atrial fibrillation and heart failure. Our work demonstrates how deep learning can automate RV assessment and risk stratification at scale using two-dimensional echocardiography.

recs.title: Tricuspid Regurgitation in Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy-Reply.
Acetic acid chromoendoscopy for detection of neoplastic Barrett's oesophagus: stepped wedge cluster randomised controlled trial (ACID-trial).
recs.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To assess the added value of acetic acid chromoendoscopy (AAC) for the detection of dysplasia and oesophageal adenocarcinoma during Barrett's oesophagus surveillance endoscopies. DESIGN: Prospective, open label, stepped wedge cluster, randomised trial. SETTING: 18 Dutch community hospitals. PARTICIPANTS: Patients undergoing surveillance for Barrett's oesophagus were eligible, excluding those with known or previously treated dysplasia. INTERVENTIONS: Hospitals randomly shifted from surveillance without AAC (control) to AAC (intervention), with endoscopists trained before implementation. Targeted biopsies were obtained if lesions were present; random four quadrant biopsies were conducted. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary endpoint was the neoplasia detection rate, defined as the percentage of participants with low grade dysplasia, high grade dysplasia, and oesophageal adenocarcinoma in any biopsy, confirmed by an experienced gastrointestinal pathologist. The secondary endpoint was the neoplasia detection rate in targeted biopsies. RESULTS: 2267 participants were included, of whom 1438 (63%) were allocated to surveillance without AAC and 829 (37%) to surveillance with AAC; AAC was applied in 679 (82%) allocated participants. Overall, neoplasia was diagnosed in 163 (7.2%) participants (111 (4.9%) low grade dysplasia, 30 (1.3%) high grade dysplasia, and 22 (1.0%) oesophageal adenocarcinoma). AAC use did not increase the neoplasia detection rate (7.4% (50/679) with AAC versus 7.1% (113/1588) without AAC; odds ratio 0.97, 95% confidence interval 0.65 to 1.44; adjusted for calendar time and Barrett's oesophagus length). Suspected lesions were detected in 95 (14.0%) participants receiving AAC versus 101 (6.4%) without AAC (P<0.001), but the targeted neoplasia detection rate was not higher (2.1% (14/679) versus 1.8% (29/1588); odds ratio 1.05, 0.49 to 2.24). CONCLUSIONS: Use of AAC did not improve detection of neoplasia in patients with Barrett's oesophagus undergoing endoscopic surveillance in routine clinical practice. TRIAL REGISTRATION: www.onderzoekmetmensen.nl; NL-OMON25059 (prospective registration; 4 Dec 2019).

recs.title: Advanced Subclinical Atherosclerosis in Young Individuals and Risk of Mortality Over 30 Years: The Coronary Artery Calcium Consortium.
recs.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Coronary artery calcium (CAC) scoring is a well-established tool for predicting cardiovascular risk, but its long-term prognostic value in young adults remains unclear. As early preventive intervention may yield substantial lifetime benefit, understanding long-term implications of elevated CAC in young adults is important for informing prevention strategies. OBJECTIVE: To investigate the long-term risk of all-cause, cardiovascular disease (CVD), and coronary heart disease (CHD) mortality associated with premature advanced subclinical atherosclerosis. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This cohort study used the CAC Consortium dataset, a retrospectively assembled cohort of referred individuals with clinically indicated CAC scans. Using multivariable regression models for time-to-event analysis, the association of CAC with all-cause, CVD, and CHD mortality was assessed, adjusting for age, sex, and traditional atherosclerotic CVD risk factors. Cumulative incidence was derived for these outcomes in 5-year increments up to 30 years using a mixed approach involving the Kaplan-Meier method and Weibull modeling. The proportion of deaths attributable to CVD and CHD across CAC groups was evaluated. Four institutions across the US provided patient-level data to assemble the CAC Consortium. Included in the analysis were adults aged 30 to 45 years from the CAC Consortium. They were followed up for a median of 22.6 years. Study data were analyzed from October 2025 to September 2026. EXPOSURE: Elevated CAC in adults aged 30 to 45 years, specifically CAC score greater than 90%. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Participants were followed up for underlying cause of mortality. RESULTS: Among 12 847 participants, the mean (SD) age was 40.5 (3.6) years, and 9922 (77.2%) were male; 9262 (72.1%) had CAC score of 0, 1626 (12.7%) had a CAC score between 75% to 90%, and 1703 (13.3%) had a CAC score greater than 90%. In total, there were 624 deaths (149 CVD and 81 CHD). Multivariable adjusted hazard ratios for CAC score greater than 90% vs CAC score of 0 were 1.87 (95% CI, 1.54-2.27), 2.60 (95% CI, 1.77-3.82), and 3.71 (95% CI, 2.24-6.16), for all-cause, CVD, and CHD mortality, respectively. Over 30 years, the group with a CAC score greater than 90% had significantly higher modeled risk of all-cause (12.9% vs 7.5%), CVD (4.5% vs 1.5%), and CHD (3.0% vs 0.6%) mortality, compared with the group with a CAC score of 0. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Results of this cohort study suggest that young adults with a CAC score greater than 90% face significantly higher long-term risk of all-cause, CVD, and CHD mortality, suggesting potential implications for guiding the intensification of preventive intervention in this high-risk phenotype.

recs.title: Determining the Optimal Treatment Strategy for Patients With Combined Aortic Stenosis and Mitral Regurgitation.
Early outcomes of transcatheter vacuum-assisted mass extraction in the left heart and the aortic arch.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Transcatheter vacuum-assisted mass extraction (TVME) in the systemic circulation is increasingly being reported. However, its feasibility, effectiveness, and safety remain poorly defined. AIMS: We sought to investigate the feasibility, effectiveness and safety of TVME in the left heart and aortic arch. METHODS: Consecutive patients from 6 centres in the United States and Canada were included. Feasibility was defined as technically successful mass extraction without unplanned cardiac surgery or intraprocedural mortality. The effectiveness endpoint was feasibility with successful debulking of ≥70% mass volume. The primary safety endpoint was the 30-day composite of procedure-attributable mortality, major cardiac structural complications, major vascular complications, Type 3-4 bleeding, acute coronary syndrome (ACS), and stroke, all according to Valve Academic Research Consortium (VARC)-3 definitions. Intraprocedural events were also reported. RESULTS: A total of 62 consecutive patients were evaluated.
