recs.abstract: Exercise is widely recognized for its cardiovascular benefits; however, its safety and role in patients with thoracic aortic aneurysms (TAAs) remains complex due to its distinctive biomechanical vulnerabilities. Fundamentally different from abdominal aortic aneurysms, TAAs develop from distinct pathophysiological processes that affect their hemodynamic responses to stressors and influence their risk of adverse aortic events. Exercise induces acute hemodynamic changes, including increased stroke volume, systolic and pulse pressures, and transient aortic stiffening. These changes impose mechanical stress on the aortic wall, potentially accelerating aneurysm progression or triggering adverse aortic events. Although moderate aerobic exercise generally appears safe with potential cardiovascular benefits, evidence supporting safe practices in TAAs is limited. Current guidelines frequently extrapolate from abdominal aortic aneurysm data, which overlook the specificities of the thoracic aorta. This review underscores the urgent need for comprehensive research, using advanced imaging, biomarker profiling, and real-time hemodynamic monitoring to understand how different exercise modalities and intensities affect TAAs. Well-designed prospective studies are crucial to improve risk stratification, optimize antihypertensive strategies, develop personalized exercise prescriptions, and provide evidence-informed guidance to patients. Perioperative strategies like prehabilitation and structured postoperative rehabilitation show promise but lack rigorous evaluation. Ultimately, this work advocates a paradigm shift from conservative inactivity toward informed, individualized physical activity regimens tailored to each patient's risk profile. This approach aims to maximize cardiovascular benefits while minimizing adverse aortic events, thereby improving overall health and quality of life in patients with TAAs.

recs.title: Greater Neighborhood Resources Predict Reduced In-Hospital Death for Children With Heart Failure and Cardiomyopathy.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with pediatric heart failure (HF) face significant morbidity and death. However, there are limited data describing neighborhood characteristics in pediatric patients with HF or exploring the relationship of these factors to resource use and clinical outcomes. We used the Child Opportunity Index 3.0 (COI), a composite index of community resources pertinent to child health, to describe neighborhood characteristics for children with HF and identify its associations with in-hospital death. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used the Pediatric Health Information System, a national administrative database of tertiary care pediatric hospitals. Inpatient encounters between January 2014 and December 2024 for pediatric patients (aged <18 years) with HF and cardiomyopathy were identified using International Classification of Diseases (ICD) codes. The primary exposure of interest was the COI, and the primary outcome of interest was in-hospital death. Mixed logistic regression models were estimated, unadjusted and adjusted for administrative sex, age, race, and primary payor. RESULTS: Our cohort consisted of index HF admissions in 7060 patients. Half of the cohort was in either the very low (n=2034 [29%]) or low (n=1521 [22%]) COI quintile. After adjustment, patients with a very high COI were less likely to experience in-hospital death than those living in very low COI neighborhoods (odds ratio, 0.73 [95% CI, 0.54-0.99]; P=0.048). CONCLUSIONS: A substantial proportion of children admitted with HF have limited neighborhood resources. Those with higher neighborhood resources are more likely to survive to discharge, emphasizing the relationship between environmental factors and clinical outcomes in pediatric HF.

recs.title: Spanish catheter ablation registry. 25th official report of the Heart Rhythm Association of the Spanish Society of Cardiology (2025).
recs.abstract: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: We report the results of the 2025 Spanish catheter ablation registry. METHODS: This retrospective registry included catheter ablation procedures performed at participating hospitals in Spain and recorded in the REDCap database using a dedicated data collection form. RESULTS: A total of 109 centers participated, reporting 33 435 ablations. Atrial fibrillation was the most commonly treated arrhythmia (14 452 cases), with single-shot techniques being the most frequently used approach (63%) and a marked increase in pulsed field ablation (37% vs 21% in 2024). The remaining arrhythmia substrates remained at similar levels. The overall acute success rate was 95%, the complication rate was 1.6%, and the mortality rate was 0.04%. There was a marked increase in outpatient procedures (33% vs 18% in 2024), particularly atrioventricular nodal re-entrant tachycardia ablation (50%) and cavotricuspid isthmus ablation (45%). A total of 467 pediatric ablations were performed in 38 centers. Accessory pathway ablation was the most common procedure (65.3%), with a 97% success rate. CONCLUSIONS: A similar number of centers participated, with a slight increase in the number of procedures compared with 2024. Atrial fibrillation remained the most frequently treated arrhythmia. Acute success, complication, and mortality rates remained stable. The accreditation process for centers and professionals is well-established, with a stable number of annual accreditations. Full English text available from: www.revespcardiol.org/en.

recs.title: Not All Strokes Are Equal: Phenotype-Dependent Surgical Timing in Infective Endocarditis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: We evaluated postoperative neurologic and mortality outcomes by stroke-to-surgery timing and stroke phenotype in patients with left-sided infective endocarditis. METHODS: Adult patients undergoing surgery for infective endocarditis complicated by preoperative stroke between 2004 and 2024 at 2 institutions were stratified by stroke-to-surgery interval (<1 week, 1-4 weeks, 4-6 weeks). The primary outcome was a composite postoperative cerebrovascular event: new stroke, enlarging stroke, or hemorrhagic conversion. Secondary outcomes were operative death and major morbidity events. RESULTS: Among 2265 patients with left-sided infective endocarditis, 322 met inclusion criteria, of whom 122 (38%) underwent surgery within 1 week, 168 (52%) between 1 and 4 weeks, and 32 (10%) between 4 and 6 weeks. Operative death was similar across groups (P=0.09). Postoperative cerebrovascular events declined with time (<1 week, 21.3%; 1-4 weeks, 11.9%; 4-6 weeks, 9.4%; P=0.015). On multivariable analysis, longer stroke-to-surgery interval was associated with reduced odds of postoperative cerebrovascular events (odds ratio, 0.92/d [95% CI, 0.85-0.98]; P=0.015), driven by early events among patients with intraparenchymal hemorrhage, subarachnoid hemorrhage, and septic emboli. Among ischemic strokes, operative death was lowest with surgery within 1 week (5.8% versus 11.2% at 1-4 weeks; P=0.24). Interval embolization occurred in 10.6% of patients awaiting surgery, most commonly affecting the spleen and kidneys. CONCLUSIONS: Excess postoperative neurologic risk was concentrated within the first 7 to 10 days and driven by intraparenchymal hemorrhage, subarachnoid hemorrhage, and septic emboli; ischemic stroke showed no appreciable temporal association. Routine delay after ischemic stroke may not be necessary, while a short delay (≈7 days) for hemorrhagic and septic embolic subtypes may be reasonable when hemodynamically feasible.

recs.title: Looking Beyond Inherited Cardiomyopathy: Reconsidering the Role of Genetics in Heart Failure.
Electrophysiological Manifestations of Suspected Bachmann's Bundle Infarction Due to Occlusion of the Right Sinus Node Artery.

Residual Cardiovascular Risk Beyond Coronary Physiology: Complementary Prognostic Value of Trimethylamine N-Oxide in Patients Undergoing Coronary Computed Tomography Angiography With Computed Tomography-Derived Fractional Flow Reserve.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Coronary computed tomography (CT) angiography with CT-derived fractional flow reserve (CT-FFR) enables noninvasive identification of flow-limiting coronary stenosis and is widely used for risk assessment. However, adverse cardiovascular events still occur in a subset of patients without functionally significant ischemia, suggesting that physiological assessment alone may not fully capture patient-level risk. We aimed to evaluate whether circulating trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO), a gut microbiota-derived biomarker, provides complementary prognostic information. METHODS: In this biobank-linked retrospective cohort study, 3978 patients undergoing clinically indicated coronary CT angiography with CT-FFR assessment were included. Serum TMAO concentrations were measured from cryopreserved samples obtained within ±30 days of imaging. Patients were stratified into high and low TMAO groups according to the receiver operating characteristic-derived threshold. The primary end point was major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events during a median follow-up of ∼3 years. Multivariable Cox models evaluated associations between TMAO and outcomes, and incremental prognostic value beyond clinical variables and CT-FFR was assessed. RESULTS: Event rates were similar across physiological strata (10.6% for CT-FFR ≤0.80 versus 10.0% for CT-FFR >0.80), indicating outcome heterogeneity beyond ischemia status. Higher TMAO levels were independently associated with major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events after adjustment for clinical covariates and CT-FFR (hazard ratio, 1.82 [95% CI, 1.44-2.31]; P<0.001). Addition of TMAO improved discrimination after bootstrap optimism correction (C-index 0.552-0.591). Among patients with preserved CT-FFR, elevated TMAO identified a subgroup with higher event rates, whereas patients with preserved CT-FFR and low TMAO had the most favorable prognosis. CONCLUSIONS: Physiological assessment and clinical outcomes are not synonymous in patients undergoing coronary CT angiography. Circulating TMAO provides complementary prognostic information and refines risk stratification, particularly among individuals without functionally significant ischemia. Integrating systemic biomarkers with coronary physiological assessment may improve individualized risk evaluation beyond imaging alone.

recs.title: Assessment of Persistent Postpartum Hypertension Following Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy: A Scoping Review.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Identifying individuals with persistent postpartum hypertension (ppHTN) after hypertensive disorders of pregnancy is an important strategy to mitigate associated long-term cardiovascular risks. Accordingly, we aimed to review the literature surrounding the assessment of ppHTN after hypertensive disorders of pregnancy. METHODS: We conducted a scoping review using Arksey and O'Malley's methodological framework. We developed and pilot-tested a data extraction tool to collect information on ppHTN assessment methods, including timing and setting, blood pressure (BP) thresholds used, and inclusion of patient preferences. Data were synthesized into tables and narrative summaries. Barriers and facilitators to BP assessment protocols, remote BP monitoring, and follow-up attendance were mapped using the Capability, Opportunity, and Motivation - Behavior (COM-B) framework. RESULTS: Of 14 593 records, 96 papers met inclusion criteria. BP measured in the hospital alone was most common (n=41), followed by the hospital/home combination (n=18), and the outpatient/home combination (n=9). Monitoring typically began within 0 to 7 days postpartum (n=28), ending at 1 to 6 weeks (n=20) or 6 to 12 months (n=20) postpartum. ppHTN was defined using elevated BP thresholds (n=28), most commonly ≥140/90 mm Hg (n=18), medication initiation (n=8), lack of BP normalization over time (n=4), or referral to a specialist (n=2). Only 7 studies assessed patient preferences. Facilitators to home BP assessment included the use of educational material, while barriers involved digital access limitations. CONCLUSIONS: ppHTN assessment methods varied in timing, setting, and BP thresholds. Findings underscore the need for standardized, patient-centered guidelines that account for BP assessment methods across settings.

recs.title: Sedation and anaesthesia in pulsed-field ablation for atrial fibrillation: mechanisms, procedural requirements, and real-world practice.
recs.abstract: Pulsed-field ablation (PFA) has rapidly emerged as an important energy source for atrial fibrillation ablation, offering tissue selectivity and procedural efficiency while introducing specific anaesthetic and sedation requirements. This narrative review examines the rationale for anaesthesia and sedation during PFA, the mechanisms underlying pain, involuntary movement, and neuromuscular stimulation, and the implications of catheter design, waveform characteristics, and patient-related factors for peri-procedural management. Available evidence indicates that both deep sedation and general anaesthesia can provide safe and effective procedural conditions when supported by appropriate monitoring, airway rescue capability, and experienced multidisciplinary teams. Deep sedation may offer advantages in workflow, recovery, and patient-centred care, particularly for standard pulmonary vein isolation procedures using contemporary biphasic systems with reduced muscle activation, whereas general anaesthesia remains appropriate for complex procedures, patients with substantial comorbidity, or settings in which complete immobility and airway control are essential. Current real-world practice is highly heterogeneous across regions and institutions, reflecting differences in regulations, staffing models, procedural complexity, and local expertise rather than a universally accepted standard. Overall, anaesthetic strategy in PFA should be individualised according to patient risk profile, expected procedural demands, and device-specific stimulation burden. Further prospective comparative studies are needed to define optimal sedation depth, standardise monitoring and outcome measures, and clarify how emerging technologies may enable lighter yet still effective sedation pathways.

recs.title: Antithrombotic Therapy for Secondary Stroke Prevention in Patients With Symptomatic Large-Artery Atherosclerosis and Atrial Fibrillation: A Multicenter Experience.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Optimal antithrombotic therapy for ischemic stroke due to symptomatic large-artery atherosclerosis in patients with atrial fibrillation remains uncertain. We describe real-world prescribing patterns and outcomes across antithrombotic regimens. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed consecutive patients with atrial fibrillation and ischemic stroke related to symptomatic large-artery atherosclerosis (intracranial or extracranial or both) at 4 US comprehensive stroke centers. Patients were grouped by discharge regimen: single anticoagulant, single antiplatelet (sAP), single anticoagulant+sAP, dual antiplatelet therapy, or triple therapy (single anticoagulant+dual antiplatelet therapy). Outcomes were recurrent ischemic stroke, symptomatic hemorrhage, and death at 90 days and 1 year. RESULTS: Among 191 patients (median age 75 years [interquartile range [IQR], 68-83]; 40% women; 36% prior stroke/transient ischemic attack), single anticoagulant+sAP was the most common discharge regimen (33%), followed by single anticoagulant (25%), whereas triple therapy was uncommon (4%). More than half of patients switched regimens within 1 year, mostly as the planned duration ended (71%) or following an outcome event (12%). During follow-up (median 68 days [IQR, 28-120]), 21 patients (11%) had recurrent ischemic stroke, and 26 (14%) had symptomatic hemorrhage, over half of each within 90 days; 25% of deaths occurred within 90 days. Ninety-day stroke/death rate was 24%, with single anticoagulant versus 8% with single anticoagulant+sAP; symptomatic hemorrhage rate was 0% and 12%, respectively. At 1 year, stroke/death was 27.3% with sAP, 11.1% with single anticoagulant+sAP, 4.5% with single anticoagulant, and 0% with dual antiplatelet therapy. Symptomatic hemorrhage was similar across groups. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with atrial fibrillation and symptomatic large-artery atherosclerosis, recurrent ischemic events and mortality were common, and antithrombotic management varied substantially. The combination of single anticoagulant+sAP was associated with lower observed short-term stroke/death than single anticoagulant; however, bleeding remains a concern with prolonged therapy. Prospective studies are needed to define optimal regimen and duration for this high-risk population.

recs.title: Management of Heart transplant recipients for the non Heart Transplant health care provider. A Clinical Consensus Statement of the Heart Failure Association (HFA) and the Association of Cardiovascular Nursing & Allied Professions (ACNAP) of the ESC.
recs.abstract: Heart transplantation (HTx) remains the gold standard treatment for selected patients with advanced heart failure and survival after transplantation has substantially improved over recent decades. As a consequence, the number of long-term HTx recipients continues to increase, and these patients are now frequently encountered in routine practice outside specialized transplant centers. Their management remains complex due to the use of chronic immunosuppression, transplant-specific complications, and a growing burden of comorbidities in the perspective of increasing longevity. Non-transplant cardiologists, general practitioners, and other healthcare professionals are therefore increasingly involved in their care but often have limited experience of post-transplant management. This clinical consensus statement from the Heart Failure Association (HFA) and the Association of Cardiovascular Nursing & Allied Professions (ACNAP) of the ESC provides practical support and a structured framework for healthcare providers involved in the care of HTx recipients outside dedicated transplant centers. The document reviews key aspects of post-transplant management, including outlining principles of care according to time from transplantation, essential knowledge around immunosuppressive therapy and drug monitoring, recognition and initial management of rejection, infection prophylaxis and treatment, and surveillance of long-term complications such as cardiac allograft vasculopathy, malignancy, chronic kidney disease, and metabolic disorders. In addition, specific clinical situations frequently encountered in practice-including fertility and pregnancy, non-cardiac surgery, rehabilitation, and palliative care-are discussed. Particular emphasis is placed on the organization of shared-care models between transplant centers and community providers and on identifying clinical scenarios requiring early referral. Through providing practical recommendations and a structured framework for follow-up, this document aims to support non-specialist clinicians in the safe management of HTx recipients and to facilitate timely collaboration with transplant centers.

recs.title: Mental Health Factors in Cardiothoracic Surgery Risk Prediction Models: A Systematic Review.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Mental health disorders are associated with substantial morbidity and death in cardiovascular disease, yet their role in perioperative risk stratification remains unclear in patients undergoing cardiothoracic surgery. We evaluated how mental health disorders are currently incorporated into cardiothoracic surgery risk prediction models. METHODS: We conducted a Preferred Reporting Items for Systemic Reviews and Meta-Analysis-concordant systematic review of PubMed and Embase on September 11, 2025 (International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews: CRD420251274958). We included studies that developed or validated risk models predicting postoperative outcomes in adults undergoing cardiothoracic surgery that either included a mental health disorder as a covariate or validated a model in patients with such disorders. Model characteristics were extracted using the Checklist for Critical Appraisal and Data Extraction for Systemic Reviews of Prediction Modeling Studies, and risk of bias and applicability were assessed using the Prediction Model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool+Artificial Intelligence. Findings were synthesized qualitatively. RESULTS: Of 17 986 articles screened, 9 studies met inclusion criteria and described 17 unique models. No study validated a model specifically in patients with mental health disorders. Depression was the most frequently included mental health covariate (8 models). When incorporated, mental health disorders had associations comparable to established clinical risk factors. The most frequently modeled outcomes were hospital readmission and postoperative depression. Three studies had a high risk of bias. Covariate selection and modeled outcomes varied substantially. CONCLUSIONS: Mental health disorders are rarely incorporated into cardiothoracic surgery risk models despite potentially important prognostic associations. Future studies should evaluate their incremental predictive value, validate models in patients with mental health disorders, and examine intersections with sociodemographic risk factors.

recs.title: PlGF modulates vascular smooth muscle cells phenotype to enhance atherosclerotic plaque stability.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Phenotypic switching of vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) is critical for determining atherosclerotic plaque stability; however, the mechanisms that drive a stability-promoting VSMCs phenotype remain unclear. While clinical evidence associates high placental growth factor (PlGF) expression with stable advanced plaques, the underlying pathways are undefined. This study investigates the mechanism by which PlGF regulates VSMCs phenotypic switching to enhance plaque stability. METHODS: PlGF expression was quantified in human carotid plaques by immunohistochemistry. Atherosclerosis was induced in ApoE-/- mice fed a high-fat diet, followed by PlGF administration for 7 days. Plaque size, composition, and the expression of PlGF, Flt-1, CD209/CD163, TGF-β1, α-SMA and CD68 were assessed at 14 and 28 days by immunohistochemistry/immunofluorescence. In vitro, flow cytometry, Western blot, ELISA and conditioned co-culture systems evaluated macrophage polarization, TGF-β1 secretion, and effects on human carotid VSMCs phenotype. RESULTS: PlGF was elevated in stable human plaques, co-localized with α-SMA in fibrous cap and shoulder regions. In PlGF-treated mice, PlGF, α-SMA and TGF-β1 increased in the fibrous cap and shoulder regions of plaques, while aortic root plaque area decreased. Co-localization of Flt-1/CD209 and TGF-β1/CD209 was enhanced, with TGF-β1/CD209 exceeding TGF-β1/α-SMA. Mechanistically, PlGF polarized macrophages toward an anti-inflammatory phenotype, increasing TGF-β1 secretion, which upregulated α-SMA in VSMCs. CONCLUSIONS: This study identifies a PlGF/anti-inflammatory macrophage/TGF-β1/contractile VSMCs signaling axis that reinforces fibrous cap integrity and promotes plaque stability in advanced atherosclerosis.

Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy Using a Conduction System Pacing Defibrillation Lead in Patients Meeting CRT-D Indications: Six-Month Clinical Outcomes Results From the ASCEND CSP Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Conduction system pacing (CSP) via left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) is a physiologic alternative to conventional biventricular (BiV) pacing for cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT), but prospective data using purpose-built implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) leads are limited. OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to evaluate procedural success, defibrillation efficacy, safety, and 6-month clinical outcomes of left bundle branch-optimized cardiac resynchronization therapy (LOT-CRT) delivered with a purpose-built CSP ICD lead and compare outcomes to conventional BiV-CRT. METHODS: A total of 52 CRT defibrillator patients (age 66 ± 10 years, 31.4% female, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) 29.5 ± 6.7%, left bundle branch block [LBBB] 66.7%, QRSd 164.6 ± 25.3 milliseconds, 29.4% ischemic) in the ASCEND CSP IDE (A Stylet-Driven ICD Lead Intended for Conduction System Pacing IDE Study) study underwent attempted implantation of a CSP ICD lead and a coronary sinus lead (LOT-CRT). Implant success, safety and efficacy outcomes, electrocardiographic characteristics, echocardiographic remodeling, heart failure status, patient-reported quality of life, and CRT response were assessed through 6 months. Outcomes were compared with a propensity-matched conventional CRT cohort (BiV-CRT). RESULTS: Implantation succeeded in 98.1% (51 of 52), with LBBAP capture achieved in all (51 of 51). Freedom from CSP lead-related serious adverse device effects through 6 months was 98.1% (95% CI: 87.1%-99.7%). Defibrillation was successful in all tested patients (100%). Compared with baseline, QRS narrowed by 30.4 ms and LVEF increased by 10.4 points (both P < 0.0001), with a CRT response (≥5%) in 71.1% and super-response (≥14.5%) in 34.2%. Compared with matched BiV-CRT patients from the MORE-CRT MPP (MORE response on Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy with MultiPoint Pacing) study, lead-related events were similar (2.0% vs 2.5%; P = 1.0), LVEF increase was greater (10.4 points vs 4.6 points; P = 0.0005) with more responders (≥5%) and super-responders (≥14.5%) (71.1% vs 48.5%; P = 0.0107 and 34.2% vs 7.8%; P < 0.0001, respectively), and more patients improved by clinical composite score (76.5% vs 52.0%; P = 0.0016). Significant improvements were seen with LOT-CRT in both LBBB and non-LBBB patients. CONCLUSIONS: LOT-CRT with a dedicated CSP ICD lead achieved high implant success, preserved defibrillation efficacy, and had favorable safety, with greater left ventricular systolic function and clinical improvement than matched conventional CRT, supporting CSP-based CRT defibrillator therapy.

recs.title: Coronary artery disease management in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The optimal management of coronary artery disease in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) remains uncertain. AIMS: We aimed to compare clinical outcomes between routine coronary revascularisation and conservative management in patients undergoing TAVI and to assess the relative effectiveness of individual revascularisation strategies by performing a meta-analysis of randomised trials. METHODS: We conducted a pairwise meta-analysis comparing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with conservative treatment and a network meta-analysis comparing the relative effectiveness of individual strategies, including angiography-guided and physiology-guided PCI. The primary outcome was a study-defined composite endpoint of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Secondary endpoints included the individual outcomes of all-cause death, cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, unplanned revascularisation, and major bleeding. RESULTS: Five trials (N=1,644 patients) were included in the systematic review, and four were included in the primary quantitative synthesis (N=1,476). Compared with conservative treatment, routine PCI was associated with lower risks of MACE (risk ratio [RR] 0.80, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.65-0.98) and unplanned revascularisation (RR 0.30, 95% CI: 0.11-0.83) and an increased risk of major bleeding (RR 1.57, 95% CI: 1.07-2.32). In the network meta-analysis, physiology-guided PCI significantly reduced MACE, stroke, and unplanned revascularisation compared with conservative treatment and ranked highest for all ischaemic outcomes among revascularisation strategies. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients referred for TAVI, routine revascularisation reduces the risk of ischaemic outcomes compared with conservative treatment. In this setting, physiology-guided PCI may be associated with the most favourable efficacy profile across available strategies. (PROSPERO: CRD420261330194).

recs.title: Infective Endocarditis - When Is Enough Enough?
Acute heart failure in emergency settings.
recs.abstract: Acute heart failure (AHF) represents a major cause of emergency medical care worldwide and continues to carry a substantial burden of morbidity and mortality despite advances in chronic heart failure management. Most patients with AHF present to emergency departments (EDs), where the first hours of care are critical to determine prognosis. Of these, some have been previously evaluated and treated by prehospital emergency medical services before ED arrival. This consensus document summarizes the current evidence and provides practical advice to emergency physicians for the diagnosis, treatment, and disposition of patients with AHF in these emergency settings (emergency medical services and ED). It emphasizes the importance of a rapid phenotypic classification into acute decompensated heart failure, acute pulmonary oedema, isolated right ventricular failure, or cardiogenic shock, as a key tool to guide early management and triage decisions. It reviews evidence on prehospital and ED management, including the use of biomarkers, imaging, ventilatory support, diuretic and vasodilator strategies, and early initiation or continuation of guideline-directed medical therapy. It also discusses risk stratification and disposition decisions supported by validated tools. Finally, it identifies major knowledge gaps and future research priorities, including pragmatic trials to assess prehospital interventions, biomarker-guided therapy, and early initiation of disease-modifying treatments. Ultimately, this consensus document is aimed to contribute to the improvement of outcomes in AHF.

recs.title: Multimodal KCNQ1 Variant-Effect Maps Define Ion Channel Mechanisms and Disease Risk.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Variants in the ion channel gene KCNQ1 are the leading cause of congenital long QT syndrome (LQTS), a disorder characterized by QT prolongation and risk of fatal arrhythmias. The expanding use of genetic testing has led to the identification of numerous variants of uncertain significance, complicating clinical interpretation and risk stratification. Functional characterization of KCNQ1 variants is essential to define their role in long QT syndrome and advance precision medicine in cardiovascular care. METHODS: We generated a nearly comprehensive variant library of 13 403 protein-coding variants in KCNQ1. Using 4 pooled assays followed by high-throughput sequencing, we characterized the variants' effects on cell surface abundance and channel function in both the variant-only and heterozygous states. Case-control analyses and data from large-scale biobanks were used to assess the clinical impact of loss-of-function variants on QT prolongation and long QT syndrome. Heterozygous assay results were used to determine dominant-negative effects, which were also evaluated for association with arrhythmia risk. Protein structural clustering of distinct classes of deleterious variants was analyzed. RESULTS: Across the 4 assays, we generated 49 305 functional measurements of KCNQ1 variants. Of the 13 403 KCNQ1 studied variants, 1757 demonstrated strong pathogenic evidence, and 6660 showed moderate benign evidence. Loss-of-function variants were significantly associated with QT prolongation and long QT syndrome in case-control and biobank analyses. Deleterious variants clustered within distinct structural domains based on their functional classification. A majority of pathogenic variants exhibited dominant-negative effects; these variants were linked to a higher risk of arrhythmia diagnoses than were haploinsufficient variants. CONCLUSIONS: This comprehensive KCNQ1 functional atlas provides novel functional evidence for most KCNQ1 variants of uncertain significance. It also reveals mechanistic principles linking genetic variation to ion channel biology and arrhythmia susceptibility, advancing cardiovascular precision medicine.

recs.title: Undiagnosed Arrhythmogenic Cardiomyopathy Hidden in Explanted Hearts: Insights from a Single Tertiary Center.
Beyond the Gradient: Patient-Reported Outcomes with Aficamten in Obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
Paradoxical Association of Body Mass Index With Occurrence and Mortality of Venous Thromboembolism in Hospitalized Patients: A National Hospital-Based Cohort Analysis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: The association between body mass index (BMI) and venous thromboembolism (VTE) occurrence and mortality is controversial. This study aimed to investigate the association of BMI with VTE occurrence and mortality and explore the consistency across age, sex, and medical specialty. METHODS: This study included 3 199 526 inpatients at potential risk for VTE from a nationwide hospital-based cohort. Participants were categorized as lean weight (BMI <18.5 kg/m2), normal weight (18.5 ≤BMI<24.0 kg/m2), overweight (24.0 ≤BMI <28.0 kg/m2), and obesity (BMI ≥28.0 kg/m2). Odds ratios (ORs) were calculated by logistic regression models. RESULTS: In all participants, 59 002 (1.8%) developed VTE during hospitalization. After adjusting for the confounding factors, compared with normal weight, the risk of VTE occurrence reduced by 18% (odds ratio [OR], 0.82 [95% CI, 0.80-0.83]) in participants with overweight and 22% (OR, 0.78,[95% CI, 0.75-0.81]) in participants with obesity. The protective association of overweight/obesity was more pronounced in age ≥65 years, female patients, and surgery participants (Pfor interaction <0.05), whereas in internal medical participants, obesity was associated with a higher risk of VTE occurrence (OR, 1.11 [95% CI, 1.01-1.21]). A total of 636 (1.1%) patients with VTE died before discharge. No significant association was observed between overweight/obesity and post-VTE mortality. However, in the surgical subgroup, obesity was associated with a lower risk of post-VTE mortality (OR, 0.37 [95% CI, 0.17-0.80], Pfor interaction <0.05). CONCLUSION: An inverse association between BMI and VTE occurrence was observed among at-risk inpatients, most pronounced in older, female, and surgical subgroups. Notably, obesity remained a risk factor in medical patients, whereas among surgical patients who developed VTE, it was paradoxically associated with lower mortality.

Echocardiographic Assessment and Clinical Applications of the Left Atrial Stiffness Index in Cardiovascular Disease.
recs.abstract: The left atrial stiffness index is an emerging echocardiographic marker that integrates pressure-related burden and atrial reservoir deformation to provide a composite measure of left atrial pressure-deformation coupling. This review summarizes the pathophysiological basis of left atrial stiffness, the methodological principles underlying echocardiographic left atrial stiffness index assessment, and the current evidence supporting its clinical applications across cardiovascular diseases. The strongest evidence is available in heart failure and atrial fibrillation, in which increased left atrial stiffness index has been associated with adverse hemodynamics, exercise intolerance, rhythm recurrence, and adverse clinical outcomes. In hypertension, cardiomyopathies, valvular heart disease, and congenital or aortic disorders, available data suggest potential clinical relevance, although the evidence remains more heterogeneous and less mature; by contrast, evidence in ischemic, inflammatory, and stroke-related settings is still preliminary. Despite its physiological appeal, broader clinical adoption remains limited by methodological heterogeneity, variable thresholds, limited invasive validation, and uncertain incremental value beyond its component measures. At present, left atrial stiffness index is best positioned as an adjunctive marker for phenotyping, hemodynamic assessment, and risk stratification, particularly in heart failure and atrial fibrillation, pending further methodological harmonization and prospective disease-specific validation.

recs.title: Trends in Oral Anticoagulant Prescribing for Atrial Fibrillation and Active Cancer in UK Primary Care.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Anticoagulation is essential in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) and cancer, but recent real-world evidence on oral anticoagulant (OAC) use remains limited. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to describe recent OAC-prescribing trends and identify factors associated with OAC initiation in patients with AF and active cancer in UK primary care. METHODS: Using the Clinical Practice Research Datalink, we identified patients aged ≥50 years with incident AF (cohort entry) between 2010 and 2023 and active cancer diagnosed in the year before cohort entry. We calculated OAC initiation rates in the year following AF diagnosis among eligible patients (CHA2DS2-VASc ≥2) using Poisson regression, overall and stratified by OAC type, age, sex, and cancer characteristics. Cox proportional hazards regression was used to identify factors associated with OAC initiation. RESULTS: Among 12,254 eligible patients, 6,940 (56.6%) initiated an OAC. OAC initiation rates rose from 89 per 100 person-years in 2010 to 385 per 100 person-years in 2023 (adjusted rate ratio: 4.32; 95% CI: 3.78-4.93), driven by increased direct oral anticoagulant prescribing. By 2023, apixaban and edoxaban predominated. OAC initiation did not differ by age and sex but was less common in patients with lung cancer (HR: 0.74; 95% CI: 0.67-0.82), metastatic cancer (HR: 0.66; 95% CI: 0.51-0.87), and dementia (HR: 0.75; 95% CI: 0.64-0.88). CONCLUSIONS: In the last decade, OAC initiation has substantially increased among eligible patients with AF and active cancer, driven by direct oral anticoagulant uptake. However, OAC initiation remained lower among patients with lung cancer, metastatic cancer, or specific comorbidities.

recs.title: Cardiac Structure and Function in Women After Preeclampsia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Preeclampsia increases the risk of long-term heart failure (HF) by 4-fold. Unfortunately, however, universal guidelines for postpartum HF surveillance are lacking. Stage B/subclinical HF has been shown to predict risk of major adverse cardiac outcomes. Some suggest that initiating cardioprotective therapy at this early stage can reduce progression to symptomatic HF. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this review was to explore cardiac structure and function in women with a history of preeclampsia and to identify when subclinical HF develops in this group. METHODS: A systematic search of MEDLINE, EMBASE and CINAHL was conducted according to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines to identify all studies assessing left ventricular function on transthoracic echocardiography in women with a history of preeclampsia. RESULTS: A total of 45 case-control studies comprising 8,991 women, including 2,288 women with a history of preeclampsia, were included in the final analysis. During pregnancy, women with preeclampsia had a higher left ventricular mass index (LVMI) (standard mean difference: 10.85 [95% CI: 6.30-15.39]), relative wall thickness (0.05 [95% CI: 0.03-0.08]), E/e' (1.58 [95% CI: 1.02-2.13]), isovolumetric relaxation time (8.74 [95% CI: 3.14-14.34]), lower E/A ratio (-0.27 [95% CI: -0.51 to -0.04]) and reduced absolute global longitudinal strain (GLS) values (2.27 [95% CI: 0.43-4.11]), indicating reduced myocardial function compared with normotensive controls. Postpartum, GLS remained reduced, and LVMI remained elevated in women with a history of preeclampsia. This difference persisted out to 10 years postpartum. There was no significant difference in all other variables >6 months postpartum. Evidence for persistent LVMI elevation >6 months postpartum was not robust in sensitivity analyses excluding overlapping cohorts. Left ventricular ejection fraction and right ventricular function remained similar in the preeclampsia and control groups throughout. CONCLUSIONS: Preeclampsia is associated with subclinical myocardial dysfunction, characterized by impaired GLS and increased LVMI. Persistent impairment in GLS was observed up to 10 years postpartum, whereas the association with elevated LVMI beyond 6 months postpartum should be interpreted with caution. Further studies are required to assess when subclinical myocardial dysfunction progresses to symptomatic clinical HF.

recs.title: Specific effects of Pulsed Field Ablation on the cardiac tissue, the nervous system and the conduction system in experimental and clinical studies.
recs.abstract: AIMS: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) has emerged as a novel ablation modality for the treatment of cardiac arrhythmias and has rapidly reshaped contemporary electrophysiology practice. This article provides a comprehensive analysis on the mechanisms underlying the specific effects of PFA on myocardial, neural tissue structures, and the cardiac conduction system, integrating biophysical principles with preclinical and clinical evidence relevant to contemporary electrophysiology practice. METHODS AND RESULTS: This document provides an exhaustive mechanistic explanation for the preferential effects of PFA on myocardium and the limits of the 'tissue-selectivity' concept. The complex interplay between cellular and tissue-level biophysics, biological responses, and tissue regenerative capacity that determines differential susceptibility to electroporation across tissues is analysed. Distinct patterns of lesion formation and maturation following PFA are also reviewed, highlighting the temporal and histopathological differences compared with radiofrequency ablation. Additionally, lesion formation in heterogeneous substrates is analysed, including fibrotic and adipose-rich myocardium, where local electric field distribution critically influences lesion durability. CONCLUSION: The article further examines the interaction between pulsed electric fields and neural tissue, with emphasis on the phrenic nerve and intrinsic cardiac autonomic nervous system. While nerve stimulation and transient reversible conduction disturbances produced by reversible electroporation can occur during ablation, permanent neural injury appears extremely rare in current clinical experience. Finally, this manuscript examines current understanding regarding the specific effects of PFA on the cardiac conduction system, which according to the limited available evidence appear strongly dependent on electric field dose and anatomical proximity.

Anthracycline Cardiotoxicity as Multicellular Network Failure: Cardiac Niche Reprogramming and Pathological Cell-Cell Communication.
recs.abstract: Anthracyclines are essential anticancer agents, yet a cardiomyocyte-centered model incompletely explains why cardiac injury can be delayed, progressive, and poorly captured by resting ejection fraction. We frame anthracycline cardiotoxicity as a multicellular network failure within the cardiac niche: the spatially organized interactions among cardiomyocytes, fibroblasts, endothelial and immune cells, extracellular matrix, and circulating signals. Cardiomyocyte stress initiates injury, whereas pathological communication may propagate it. We distinguish a fibroblast-CD8+ T-cell adhesion circuit, supported by loss-of-function evidence in mice and correlative human data, from an emerging therapy-conditioned tumor-heart extracellular vesicle axis supported mainly by breast cancer models. These pathways may converge on fibrotic stiffness, microvascular dysfunction, and electrical uncoupling; however, direct cross-circuit interaction and drug-independent sufficiency remain unproven. We integrate established clinical risk modifiers with this framework, specify causal criteria, and propose spatial multiomics, living myocardial slices, tumor-bearing systems, and longitudinal phenotyping to test circuit persistence. This evidence-calibrated model shifts the goal from cataloging cell-intrinsic pathways to identifying mechanism-resolved biomarkers and therapeutically targetable communication nodes while preserving antitumor efficacy.

recs.title: Guidelines on rehabilitation and a focus on lifestyle-related cardiovascular prevention.
Lipoprotein(a) and Risk Stratification for Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease Across the Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Continuum.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Lp(a) (lipoprotein(a)) is an established risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), but its prognostic relevance across the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) continuum remains uncertain. We examined whether Lp(a) was associated with incident ASCVD across CKM stages and whether it provided complementary risk stratification beyond CKM staging. METHODS: We included 333 321 UK Biobank participants free of clinical cardiovascular disease at baseline and classified them into CKM stages 0 to 3. Elevated Lp(a) was defined as ≥125 nmol/L. The primary outcome was incident ASCVD, defined as coronary artery disease or ischemic stroke. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs), and 10-year absolute risks were estimated using Kaplan-Meier methods. RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 15.3 years, 17 581 incident ASCVD events occurred. After adjustment for demographic characteristics, socioeconomic factors, lifestyle factors, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, medications, and CKM stage, elevated Lp(a) was associated with higher ASCVD risk (HR, 1.31 [95% CI, 1.25-1.36]). In joint analyses, risk increased progressively across combined CKM-Lp(a) categories, with the highest risk observed in participants with CKM stage 3 and elevated Lp(a) versus CKM stage 0 and lower Lp(a) (HR, 3.43 [95% CI, 2.74-4.31]). Ten-year ASCVD risk ranged from 0.64% to 16.30%, and the absolute risk difference associated with elevated Lp(a) increased from 0.23% in stage 0 to 2.20% in stage 3. CONCLUSIONS: Elevated Lp(a) was associated with higher incident ASCVD risk across the CKM continuum. Although relative associations were broadly consistent across CKM stages, absolute risk increments associated with elevated Lp(a) were greater at more advanced CKM stages, supporting the integration of Lp(a) into CKM-based risk stratification for primary prevention.

Anticoagulation strategies during peripheral ultrafiltration in diuretic-resistant congestive heart failure.
recs.abstract: Introduction and objectives Peripheral ultrafiltration (UF) is an effective strategy for the management of diuretic-resistant congestion in patients with decompensated heart failure. However, extracorporeal circuit clotting remains one of the main technical limitations of the procedure, and the optimal anticoagulation strategy during UF has not been clearly established. The primary aim of this study was to evaluate the efficacy and safety of different anticoagulation strategies during UF. Methods This prospective, nonrandomized, single-center study included 87 consecutive patients who underwent UF between January 2021 and November 2025. The anticoagulation strategy was tailored according to the patients' baseline anticoagulant therapy: unfractionated heparin (UFH), n = 8; low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH), n = 41; vitamin K antagonists (VKAs), n = 12; and direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs), n = 26. Procedural efficacy was defined as successful completion of the UF session without premature interruption due to extracorporeal circuit dysfunction or clinical complications. Results Baseline characteristics and UF technical parameters were comparable among groups (P > .1). Procedural efficacy was highest with intravenous heparin (UFH = 100%, LMWH = 48.7%, VKAs = 66.6%, and DOACs = 65.4%; P = .048). Extracorporeal circuit clotting was more frequent with subcutaneous heparin (UFH = 0%, LMWH = 31.7%, VKAs = 25%, and DOACs = 27%; P = .018). Conclusions UFH was associated with a lower rate of extracorporeal circuit clotting and a higher rate of successful UF completion. Complications were infrequent. Given the observational design and the small sample size, these findings warrant confirmation in larger prospective studies. Full English text available from: www.revespcardiol.org/en.

Intravascular Imaging-Guided Drug-Eluting Stenting for Complex Coronary Lesions: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Intravascular imaging (IVI) guidance improves percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) outcomes, yet recent randomized controlled trials (RCTs) challenged these findings. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of IVI-guided vs angiography-guided PCI in complex coronary lesions, incorporating recent large-scale trials with divergent findings. METHODS: The authors conducted a meta-analysis of RCTs evaluating IVI-guided vs angiography-guided PCI among patients with complex coronary lesions. The primary outcomes were major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and cardiac death. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% CIs were calculated using frequentist random-effects models and complementary Bayesian analyses. The analysis was complemented by several sensitivity and subgroup analyses. RESULTS: Eighteen RCTs enrolling 18,975 patients were included. IVI guidance was associated with significant reductions in MACE (RR: 0.67; 95% CI: 0.55-0.83), cardiac death (RR: 0.72; 95% CI: 0.53-0.97), myocardial infarction (RR: 0.87; 95% CI: 0.76-0.998), clinically driven target lesion revascularization (RR: 0.72; 95% CI: 0.51-0.999), and stent thrombosis (RR: 0.52; 95% CI: 0.35-0.78). A significant geographic interaction was identified for MACE, with benefit predominantly driven by Asian trial populations (Pinteraction < 0.01). In subgroup analysis, patients achieving imaging-defined stent optimization were associated with lower event rates than those who did not (RR: 0.41; 95% CI: 0.26-0.62). CONCLUSIONS: IVI guidance reduces the risk of adverse events for complex lesions. The benefit was in part driven by achieving imaging-defined stent optimization.

Long-Term Safety and Procedural Performance of an Interatrial Shunt for Heart Failure According to Ejection Fraction.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Long-term device durability and phenotype-specific safety outcomes after interatrial shunting require further characterization. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the procedural success, device durability, and heart failure (HF) phenotype-specific safety outcomes of an interatrial shunt in the RELIEVE-HF trial. METHODS: Randomized patients were assigned 1:1 to shunt or sham control with prespecified stratification by left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) into heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) (LVEF ≤40%) and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) (LVEF >40%). Procedural performance, device durability, serious adverse events (SAEs), major adverse cardiovascular or neurological events (MACNE), major bleeding, and renal outcomes were assessed through 2 years. RESULTS: Among 605 enrolled patients (508 randomized; 97 roll-in), shunt implantation was attempted in 370 and was successful in 369 (99.7%). Among implanted patients with follow-up (n = 348), no device- or procedure-related MACNE occurred through 2 years (0%; 95% CI: 0%-0.9%), and shunt patency was 99.4% (95% CI: 97.9%-99.9%). Prespecified LVEF-stratified analyses demonstrated divergent safety profiles. In HFrEF, shunt therapy was not associated with excess all-cause MACNE, major bleeding, or renal decline and was associated with lower SAE burden. In HFpEF, shunt therapy was associated with higher all-cause MACNE, greater SAE burden, increased major bleeding, and greater renal decline. CONCLUSIONS: Interatrial shunt implantation was mechanically reliable and durable through 2 years. Safety outcomes differed by HF phenotype, with no evidence of excess clinical safety events in HFrEF but increased adverse events in HFpEF. These findings support phenotype-specific evaluation of interatrial shunt therapy. (REducing Lung congestion symptoms using the v-wavE shunt in adVancEd Heart Failure [RELIEVE-HF]; NCT03499236).

recs.title: Pulmonary vein narrowing after voltage-guided adjunctive pulmonary vein sleeve pulsed field ablation.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) for pulmonary vein (PV) isolation (PVI) has been associated with a low risk of PV stenosis when performed using the standard ostial workflow. However, the risk of PV narrowing after adjunctive PV sleeve PFA remains insufficiently evaluated. OBJECTIVE: To assess PV narrowing after voltage-guided adjunctive PV sleeve PFA. METHODS: We retrospectively studied 147 patients who underwent an initial pentaspline PFA-based PVI for atrial fibrillation. In addition to standard ostial PVI, voltage-guided PFA applications were delivered to target PV sleeve potentials identified on pre-ablation voltage mapping. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography was performed before and approximately six months after ablation. PV cross-sectional areas (PVAs) were measured at predefined levels, and the maximum PVA reduction rate was defined as ΔPVA. Significant PV narrowing was defined as ΔPVA ≥25%. RESULTS: Post-ablation PVA was significantly smaller than pre-ablation PVA at all PV sites. The median ΔPVA was 5.4%, 6.4%, 4.6%, and 4.0% in the left superior, left inferior, right superior, and right inferior PVs, respectively, and differed significantly among the four PV sites (P = 0.012). No significant PV narrowing was observed in this cohort. CONCLUSIONS: In patients undergoing an initial PFA-based PVI, no significant PV narrowing was observed approximately six months after voltage-guided adjunctive PV sleeve PFA using a pentaspline catheter. Further controlled studies with larger populations and longer follow-up are needed to better characterize the safety and clinical utility of this strategy.

Feedback Control of Arterial Pressure Using Deep Brain Stimulation: Transfer Function Analysis and Simulation Study.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) is an established treatment for Parkinson disease. Emerging evidence suggests that DBS of the subthalamic nuclei may be a target for neuromodulation therapy for orthostatic hypotension due to efferent baroreflex failure. To develop a central algorithm for an artificial baroreflex system, we first estimated the dynamic responses of arterial pressure to DBS, and then determined the feedback correction factors for DBS. METHODS: A total of 14 Parkinson disease patients treated with DBS participated in submaximal stimulation screening tests for 20 s to identify responders exhibiting a pressor reaction of ≥10 mm Hg in systolic arterial pressure. In the responders, we randomly performed stimulation while tonometrically measuring the systolic arterial pressure. The transfer function from stimulation-to-systolic arterial pressure was computed using a fast Fourier transform algorithm. Finally, the feedback correction factors were determined via numerical simulations. RESULTS: The transfer function was identifiable in all 3 responders. The average stimulation-to-systolic arterial pressure transfer function exhibited low-pass characteristics, with a steady-state gain of 8.24 mm Hg/stimulation, corner frequency of 0.02 Hz, and pure delay of 2.5 s. Based on these results, the proportional and integral correction factors were set to 0.12 and 0.018, respectively, for the feedback control of the stimulation. Computer simulations revealed that the system could quickly and effectively attenuate a sudden drop in systolic arterial pressure induced by external disturbances, such as head-up tilt. CONCLUSIONS: An artificial baroreflex system with the feedback correction of stimulation of DBS may be a novel therapeutic approach for efferent baroreflex failure.

recs.title: From Risk Trajectories to Surrogate Endpoints in Mild HCM.
Epicardial Closure for Peridevice Leaks from Endocardial Left Atrial Appendage Closure - Early LARIAT-4-PDL Registry Results.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Closure of clinically significant peri-device leaks (PDLs) after left atrial appendage (LAA) occlusion remains crucial to prevent thromboembolism. A variety of techniques exist to close PDLs, each with its own advantages and disadvantages. The LARIAT (Atricure, Mason, OH) suture device may provide an alternative for closing PDLs. OBJECTIVE: We report the initial feasibility of LARIAT for endocardial LAA closure PDLs. METHODS: In a multicenter, retrospective study, we reviewed consecutive patients who underwent LARIAT for closure of device-related LAA leaks. All patients had PDLs ≥3 mm after either a Watchman FLX Pro (Boston Scientific, Marlborough, MA) or an Amplatzer Amulet (Abbott, Chicago, IL) endocardial LAA occluder, as seen on postoperative imaging. Acute PDL closure - pericardial access with device deployment and elimination of the PDL on intraprocedural imaging - was evaluated with either transesophageal or intracardiac echocardiogram, along with 45-day safety. RESULTS: We report 10 cases in patients aged 67.2±10.7years, 30.0% female, and with a body mass index 32.4±6.4 kg/m2. Baseline comorbidities included a CHADSVASC of 4.4±0.7 and HASBLED of 3.7±0.7. Initially, patients underwent Watchman (80.0%) or Amulet (20.0%) with an average PDL of 5.4±0.8 mm. Few cases had attempted PDL closure with radiofrequency ablation (10.0%), coiling (20.0%), or a previous device (10.0%). After procedural and fluoroscopy times of 48.7±10.8 min and 7.0±3.7 min, respectively, LARIAT PDL closure was successful in all cases, and no difference when stratified by initial endocardial LAA closure type. CONCLUSION: These initial results suggest that a LARIAT may be an alternative strategy in patients with clinically significant PDLs after endocardial LAA closure. Future studies are needed to corroborate our initial findings and long-term closure results.

recs.title: Targeting Transmural Substrate: Noninvasive Radioablation for Refractory Chagasic VT.
Sex-Based Differences in Chronic Heart Failure: a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Sex-based disparities in patient enrollment and treatment effects in heart failure (HF) randomized controlled trials (RCTs) have been reported. We aim to systematically analyze sex-based enrollment and treatment effect differences in HF RCTs over time. METHODS: RCTs enrolling patients with chronic HF were systematically searched on PubMed-MEDLINE. Eligible trials included pharmacological or device-based interventions with a hard primary endpoint (mortality and hospitalization) and reporting enrollment of women. Sex-specific treatment effects (HR or RR) were extracted. Meta-analyses were performed using random-effects models, and pre-specified subgroup analyses were performed. RESULTS: A total of 56 RCTs (39 drug, 17 device) were included. The pooled proportion of women enrollment was 27.0% (95%CI: 22.0% to 32.4%) in drug trials and 25.3% (95%CI: 21.0% to 29.9%) in device trials. Women were more underrepresented in HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) than in HF with preserved EF (HFpEF) trials (21.0% vs 49.6%, p < 0.001). Among drug trials reporting sex-specific effects, the pooled sex interaction for RCTs reporting HR was 0.94 (95%CI 0.89-1.01) and RR was 0.81 (95%CI 0.68-0.96), suggesting potentially greater benefit for women. No interaction was observed between HFrEF and HFpEF trials (HR: p = 0.44; RR: p = 0.95). The pooled interaction estimate on event counts was 0.90 (95%CI 0.84-0.96). For devices, the pooled sex interaction for RCTs reporting HR was 1.05 (95%CI 0.90-1.22) and RR was 0.68 (95%CI 0.50-0.93). CONCLUSION: Women remain underrepresented in HF RCTs. Sex-stratified analyses suggest a potentially greater relative benefit of drug intervention in women, which might inform future RCTs. Further studies are required to investigate the mechanisms of these differences.

Three ablation strategies using very high-power short-duration catheter in paroxysmal atrial fibrillation: The Q-INDEX randomized trial.
recs.abstract: BACKGROUND: Very high-power short-duration (vHPSD; 90 W/4 sec) ablation shortens pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) but produces shallower lesions that may be inadequate in the thick anterior left atrium. OBJECTIVE: To compare vHPSD, ablation index (AI)-guided, and hybrid strategies for PVI in paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. METHODS: In this multicenter, randomized, open-label trial, 150 patients with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation were assigned 1:1:1 with the QDOT MICRO catheter to (1) AI-guided (AI 500 anterior, 400 elsewhere), (2) hybrid (AI-guided anterior [AI 500], vHPSD elsewhere), or (3) vHPSD (90 W/4 sec, all segments). The primary endpoint was total ablation time; secondary endpoints included acute PV reconnection, safety, and 1-year freedom from atrial arrhythmia. RESULTS: Acute PVI was achieved in all patients. Total ablation time was longest with AI-guided and shortest with vHPSD ablation (median 2220 vs 1450 vs 794 sec; P < .001). Acute reconnection across the 14 PV segments was lowest with AI-guided and highest with vHPSD (7.7% vs 9.4% vs 10.6%; P = .40). One-year freedom from atrial arrhythmia was 92.0%, 85.4%, and 77.6%, respectively (log-rank P = .13; for AI-guided vs vHPSD; P = .049). No tamponade occurred; steam pops occurred only in the 90 W groups. Two minor periprocedural strokes occurred (both vHPSD; full recovery), and silent cerebral lesions on magnetic resonance imaging did not differ among the groups (5%, 10%, 0%; P = .35). CONCLUSION: Uniform vHPSD more than halved PVI ablation time but was associated with the lowest 1-year efficacy, whereas the hybrid strategy preserved efficiency without significant loss of durability. These exploratory findings-from a trial powered for ablation time-support region-tailored lesion depth in point-by-point ablation and warrant confirmation.
